requirement_text: The blueprint is complete only when every mandatory requirement is unambiguous and testable; financial formulas, signal logic and state transitions are specified; source/interface and failure contracts are defined; security and audit controls are covered; every requirement maps to verification evidence; dependencies and implementation sequencing are explicit; and Gemini can independently determine pass, fail or blocked status.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete blueprint would leave ambiguous requirements that cannot be implemented or audited.
issue_note: "Unambiguous" and "testable" are judgement-based; no defined pass/fail method for blueprint completion.

requirement_text: Blueprint completion is not implementation completion. Production readiness requires the separate implementation acceptance, operational readiness and release gates.
criticality_rationale: Treating blueprint completion as implementation readiness gives a false released status.

requirement_text: ☐ The construction edition is the only scope; NDIS-specific product requirements are excluded.
criticality_rationale: Scope exclusion check; failure imports irrelevant NDIS requirements, limited financial consequence.
issue_note: No requirement row states construction-only scope or NDIS exclusion; criterion has nothing to verify.

requirement_text: ☐ Whole-project and whole-business profit protection and improvement are the governing mission.
criticality_rationale: Checks governing mission is stated; failure allows scope drift.
issue_note: Checklist item tests presence of a mission statement, not behaviour.

requirement_text: ☐ The system proactively searches for both downside leakage and upside opportunities, including when no threshold is breached.
criticality_rationale: Failure means upside opportunities on on-budget projects go undiscovered.

requirement_text: ☐ Materials/global-market/procurement intelligence is included as a major supporting domain, not the entire product.
criticality_rationale: Checks materials is supporting, not entire product; failure narrows scope.

requirement_text: ☐ Financial outputs are explainable, traceable, deterministic where authoritative, and explicit about uncertainty.
criticality_rationale: Failure permits non-deterministic or untraceable authoritative financial figures.

requirement_text: ☐ Real-time claims are bounded by source availability and measured freshness/latency.
criticality_rationale: Failure allows stale data to be presented as real-time.

requirement_text: ☐ Human approval remains required for consequential external actions in the initial scope.
criticality_rationale: Failure allows consequential external actions without human approval.

requirement_text: ☐ Actual Anchor platform contracts must be discovered before detailed architecture is frozen.
criticality_rationale: Failure freezes architecture on unverified platform assumptions.

criticality_rationale: Checks implementer and auditor obligations exist; failure weakens evidence discipline.

requirement_text: 00.12 Required control artefacts
elements: Versioned product requirements and architecture specifications. ¶ Architecture decision records documenting alternatives, rationale, consequences and status. ¶ Requirements Traceability Matrix mapping requirement → design → implementation → test → evidence → status. ¶ Data dictionary, canonical entity/state contracts and integration schemas. ¶ Formula catalogue with worked examples and independent arithmetic checks. ¶ Source coverage/freshness register and data quality contracts. ¶ Threat model and security/tenant-isolation test matrix. ¶ Test plan, acceptance criteria, regression evidence and mutation-testing results where applicable. ¶ Assumptions, dependencies, risks, defects and DB-dependent/deferred-closure registers. ¶ Implementation log, independent audit report, release checklist and version/hash manifest.
criticality_rationale: Missing RTM, formula catalogue or hash manifest removes inputs needed for release gates and audit.

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED BASELINE — VERSION 1.0. This charter has been consolidated to include the accepted whole-project profit-improvement mission, real-time/material-market intelligence, and post-completion retention/security/DLP scope. Changes require a documented amendment, impact analysis, version increment and approval.
criticality_rationale: Lock and change-control record; documentation-only.

requirement_text: This section establishes the controlling product mission, scope, non-negotiable principles, blueprint governance and acceptance method for Anchor Profit Guardian — Construction Edition. It is the baseline against which all later sections, implementation instructions, tests and independent audit criteria must be checked.
criticality_rationale: Baseline-control statement; without it later sections lack a reference for conformance checks.

requirement_text: This document describes requirements and intended behaviour. It is not evidence that any capability already exists in code, is integrated with a live source, or has passed testing.
criticality_rationale: Evidence boundary; omission could let the spec be mistaken for proof of implemented capability.

requirement_text: Anchor Profit Guardian is an active construction profit intelligence and protection system. Its primary mission is continuously to discover, explain, prioritise and help realise opportunities to increase expected profit while detecting, preventing and mitigating profit leakage across construction projects and, where supported, across the construction business portfolio.
criticality_rationale: Without the governing mission the product could drift to passive reporting, reducing profit protection.
issue_note: Mission statement ("continuously", "help realise") has no objective pass/fail; verified indirectly via PGR-00-A004/A005.

requirement_text: It is not merely a job-costing system, accounting dashboard, paperwork tool, recordkeeping system, compliance tool, purchasing application or retrospective reporting product. Job-costing, recordkeeping, reporting, materials intelligence and purchasing intelligence are supporting capabilities. The governing objective is whole-project and whole-business profit protection and improvement.
criticality_rationale: Scope drift to job-costing or procurement-only tool would leave whole-project leakage undetected.

requirement_text: The system is intended to sit alongside customers' existing accounting, estimating, feasibility, scheduling, procurement, construction/project-management and other relevant systems, using controlled integrations and targeted field data capture where required. Replacing those systems is not the default objective.
criticality_rationale: Building replacement systems instead of integrating wastes effort and duplicates authoritative records.
issue_note: "Not the default objective" leaves unclear when replacing customer systems is permitted.

requirement_text: Mission A — Stop profit leakage
elements: Identify emerging and existing avoidable costs as early as reliable source data permits, preferably before the cost becomes irreversible. ¶ Detect symptoms, contributing conditions and plausible root causes; do not merely report an overrun after it has happened. ¶ Estimate the financial exposure, affected project/package, relevant time horizon, intervention window and evidence supporting the finding. ¶ Investigate evidenced leakage such as labour/productivity loss, rework, idle resources, delay and holding costs, material waste, procurement errors, avoidable expediting, duplicate or excess commitments, unbilled/under-recovered variations, supplier or subcontractor performance, quality defects and other supported cost drivers. ¶ Track whether an exposure was prevented, mitigated, realised, dismissed or remains unresolved, with reasons and evidence.
criticality_rationale: Missing Mission A behaviours means leakage is detected late or not tracked to resolution.

subclause: Mission B — Find ways to increase profit
requirement_text: Mission B — Find ways to increase profit
elements: Search for upside even when the project is on budget and no alert threshold has been crossed. ¶ Discover operational, commercial, scheduling, procurement, resource, quality, design/constructability, cash-flow and portfolio opportunities where relevant data supports analysis. ¶ Evaluate feasible alternatives against an explicit baseline and comparable time horizon, including implementation costs, risk, uncertainty, quality, compliance, contractual constraints and schedule consequences. ¶ Rank opportunities using transparent criteria such as expected net benefit, confidence, urgency, feasibility, time to benefit, downside exposure and reversibility. ¶ Reassess recommendations when material events, market conditions, source data, schedules, quotes, commitments or user decisions change the economics. ¶ Track opportunities from discovery through assessment, approval, action, outcome or rejection; distinguish projected benefit from realised benefit.
criticality_rationale: Without proactive upside search, profit opportunities on on-budget projects are never surfaced.

requirement_text: The required operating model is event-driven and continuously reassessed, not dependent on a user logging in and requesting a report.
criticality_rationale: Report-on-login model delays detection, missing intervention windows for leakage.

requirement_text: 00.4 Active operating model
elements: A relevant source event arrives, a scheduled reassessment runs, a rule/threshold changes, or a user requests an analysis. ¶ The system validates the event, its provenance, freshness, tenant/project scope and data quality. ¶ The system identifies affected financial calculations, forecasts, risks and opportunity candidates. ¶ Deterministic calculation and versioned rules assess financial consequences and eligibility; analytical/AI components may assist pattern discovery and explanation within explicit limits. ¶ The system prioritises material, timely, actionable findings and provides evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, net financial impact, trade-offs and the latest useful intervention time where supportable. ¶ The user receives an appropriately routed alert or work item and can inspect evidence, approve/reject/defer, assign an owner and track the action. ¶ Relevant inputs and outcomes trigger reassessment; the system preserves prior recommendations and explains material changes.
criticality_rationale: Skipping validation, scope checks or approval routing yields untrusted findings and lost decision history.
issue_note: Row text is only the heading; the operative 7-step sequence sits in elements.

requirement_text: Real-time means as promptly as the source and system can reliably support. Each source must have a declared update method, freshness target, latency measurement and outage behaviour. A daily feed must never be represented as second-by-second data. Missing, stale, conflicting or incomplete inputs must be visible and must limit or block conclusions where necessary.
criticality_rationale: Stale or daily data presented as real-time would produce unqualified, misleading conclusions.
issue_note: "Freshness target" and "limit or block" criteria are required per source but no values or blocking rule are given here.

requirement_text: 00.5 Whole-project and whole-business intelligence domains
elements: Commercial and revenue protection — Scope changes, approved/unapproved variations, potentially unbilled work, under-recovery, claims/payment timing and configured contractual entitlement workflows where legally and contractually validated. ¶ Cost and commitment control — Budget, actuals, commitments, purchase orders, invoices, quote changes, estimate-to-complete drift, duplicate/unauthorised spend and forecast final cost. ¶ Materials and procurement — Material identity/specification/quantities, market and supplier pricing, purchase timing, landed cost, availability, lead times, waste, shortages, over-ordering, stock reuse and approved alternatives. ¶ Labour, productivity and capacity — Labour cost variance, rework, idle time, overtime, trade productivity, utilisation and resource allocation where source data is reliable. ¶ Schedule and time-related economics — Schedule slippage, dependencies, critical-path exposure, resequencing, acceleration economics, handover/settlement timing and holding costs. ¶ Quality and defects — Recurring defects, coordination clashes, rework drivers, rectification and warranty exposure, defect liability/maintenance-period obligations, subcontractor rectification responsibility, and prevention opportunities. ¶ Subcontractors and suppliers — Price, quality, lead time, reliability, schedule adherence, disputes, concentration and total delivered economic value. ¶ Design, scope and constructability — Potentially avoidable complexity, wasteful specifications, coordination issues and alternative methods/materials subject to required technical and design approvals. ¶ Equipment, logistics and site resources — Utilisation, hire-versus-own comparisons, mobilisation, delivery consolidation, storage, handling, idle resources and duplicated effort. ¶ Cash flow and capital exposure — Payment timing, working capital, finance/holding costs, retention monies withheld or overdue, bank guarantees/performance bonds and other security instruments, tied-up capital and release/expiry costs, and scenario comparisons using authorised financial data. ¶ External markets and operating conditions — Domestic and global material indicators, foreign exchange, supply availability, freight, energy and other relevant signals where reliable and authorised sources are accessible. ¶ Project and portfolio intelligence — Cross-project loss patterns, reusable lessons, capacity allocation, shared procurement opportunities and portfolio-wide economics subject to data rights and comparability.
criticality_rationale: Missing domains leave categories of leakage unmonitored; limited direct financial corruption.
issue_note: Row text is only the heading; the 12 domain definitions sit in elements.

requirement_text: Profit Guardian's monitoring does not automatically end at practical completion, handover or occupancy. Where source records and contractual data are available, it must continue to track relevant commercial, retention, security, defect-liability and closeout obligations until they are closed or explicitly transferred or waived by an authorised user.
criticality_rationale: Stopping at practical completion misses retention, security and DLP exposures still affecting profit.

requirement_text: 00.5.1 Retentions, security and post-completion economics
elements: Track retention amounts withheld, claimed, approved, released and outstanding; relevant caps, milestones, due dates, release conditions, disputes and supporting evidence. ¶ Track bank guarantees, performance bonds and other security instruments, including value, beneficiary, issuer, issue/expiry dates, fees/collateral where known, release conditions, dependencies, owner and source. ¶ Track practical completion, configured DLP/maintenance-period dates, defect notices, severity, responsible party, response/rectification deadlines, inspections, sign-offs, rectification costs and potential recovery workflows. ¶ Connect unresolved defects to applicable retention/security conditions and financial exposure where evidence supports the relationship. Do not assume every contract has identical release conditions or assert legal entitlement from inference alone. ¶ Distinguish a possible release opportunity from a verified contractual entitlement; flag expiry or release review needs for authorised human verification. Do not autonomously cancel, amend or release a security instrument. ¶ Calculate tied-up capital or delay cost only with declared rates, periods and assumptions. Avoid double-counting principal balances, financing costs, fees and linked defect exposures across findings.
criticality_rationale: Allows autonomous security-instrument release or double-counted retention/defect exposure in authoritative figures.
issue_note: Row text is only the subheading; six operative obligations sit in elements, mixing tracking, prohibition and calculation rules.

requirement_text: 00.6 Materials and global market intelligence
elements: Maintain a versioned project-specific materials register covering material identity, specification/grade/dimensions/standard, unit, planned and revised quantities, ordered/secured/delivered/consumed/returned/damaged/wasted quantities, remaining need, supplier, cost, lead time, required-on-site date, source and confidence. ¶ Ingest and reconcile suitable bills of quantities, estimates, material schedules, purchase orders, invoices, supplier quotes, delivery dockets, site records and approved changes; preserve provenance and source revision. ¶ Monitor available domestic supplier prices and relevant international indicators through permitted customer records, supplier integrations, licensed feeds and permitted public sources. ¶ Normalise product specification, unit, quantity breaks, geography, currency, tax basis, freight/delivery terms, quote validity, lead time and availability before comparing offers. ¶ Estimate overseas landed cost where relevant, including applicable FX, freight, insurance, duties/tariffs, tax treatment, handling, storage, compliance, minimum order quantities, finance, lead time and supplier risk. ¶ Evaluate buy now, wait/monitor, stage purchase, request/refresh quotes, negotiate/tender, transfer/reuse stock and approved substitute options where applicable. ¶ Explain the break-even future price or other condition required for waiting to outperform a feasible current purchase, including carrying costs, shortage and delay risks. ¶ Treat future market prices as uncertain estimates, not facts. Show forecast horizon, evidence, uncertainty, confidence basis and source freshness; return insufficient evidence when needed. ¶ Do not promise universal or real-time market coverage without verified coverage and permitted access. Track gaps by material category, geography, specification and freshness.
criticality_rationale: Unqualified price forecasts or incomparable offers would mislead purchasing decisions.
issue_note: Row text is only the heading; nine materials obligations sit in elements.

requirement_text: 00.7 Financial integrity and evidence rules
elements: Separate actual, committed, forecast, scenario, opportunity, avoided cost, expected net benefit, additional revenue, margin impact and realised outcome. ¶ Every material finding must trace to source records/observations, timestamps, units, transformations, assumptions and calculation/rule/model versions. ¶ Use deterministic, versioned and independently testable financial calculations for authoritative amounts, thresholds, eligibility and state transitions. ¶ AI may assist pattern discovery, candidate generation, summarisation and explanation, but must not silently invent, alter or override authoritative financial arithmetic. ¶ Compare total economic outcomes, not a single cost line. Include material implementation, procurement, financing, storage, transition, delay, quality, warranty and other applicable costs. ¶ Prevent double counting between related causes, interventions, packages and scenarios; mark overlap explicitly when it cannot be resolved. ¶ Present uncertainty, data quality, freshness, sensitivity and limitations; do not express estimates as guarantees. ¶ Maintain an auditable baseline and record user decisions, overrides, action history and outcome evidence. ¶ Do not claim a realised saving or causal impact without evidence adequate to support that claim.
criticality_rationale: Mixing actual/forecast/avoided values or AI-altered arithmetic produces wrong authoritative financial figures.
issue_note: Row text is only the heading; nine core financial-integrity rules sit in elements and should be individually traceable.

clause: 00.8 Human authority and prohibited autonomous actions
requirement_text: Profit Guardian is an intelligence and advisory system. It may automatically ingest permitted events, calculate, detect, reassess, prioritise and notify. In the initial scope it must not autonomously commit funds, place purchase orders, amend contracts, approve design/material substitutions, change construction schedules in authoritative systems, approve claims or take other consequential external actions.
criticality_rationale: Autonomous orders, contract amendments or claims would bypass human approval for consequential actions.

clause: 00.8 Human authority and prohibited autonomous actions
requirement_text: Consequential action requires an authorised human decision and any applicable external-system approval. Any later execution capability requires a separately approved architecture, permission model, limits, confirmation flow, audit controls, recovery behaviour and acceptance gates.
criticality_rationale: Execution without authorised human decision bypasses approval for consequential external actions.

requirement_text: Profit Guardian is a vertical module in the Anchor ecosystem. The detailed blueprint must inspect the actual current Anchor Engine, Governor, integration framework/AUIF, identity and tenant model, entities/state/events, workflows/notifications, audit trail, frontend conventions, deployment and test infrastructure. Existing capabilities must be reused only where their actual contracts and evidence support the intended use.
criticality_rationale: Unverified reuse of platform contracts risks incompatible interfaces and broken governance integration.

requirement_text: Do not assume repository paths, APIs, database schemas, integrations, database access, live data or deployment readiness without verification. Unknowns belong in a versioned assumptions/dependency register. If access is unavailable, record the blocked item, why access is required, exact closure instructions, required validation and closure evidence. Do not declare a blocked gate passed.
criticality_rationale: Declaring a blocked gate passed falsely asserts verified status and permits release despite failure.

requirement_text: 00.10 Security, privacy and tenant boundaries
elements: Enforce tenant, organisation, project and role permissions server-side for all reads, writes, calculations, alerts, exports and integrations. ¶ Apply least privilege to users, services, market connectors and external credentials; keep secrets out of logs and source control. ¶ Record provenance and access for commercially sensitive project, supplier, pricing, contract and financial data. ¶ Define retention, deletion, export, audit, backup and incident-response expectations in the relevant later sections. ¶ Treat external documents, supplier responses and imported data as untrusted data, not instructions to the system. ¶ Ensure a tenant cannot access another tenant's projects, price agreements, supplier terms, material records, credentials or intelligence outputs.
criticality_rationale: Missing server-side tenant enforcement exposes one tenant's pricing, contracts and outputs to another.
issue_note: Row text is only the heading; six security obligations sit in elements.

requirement_text: 00.11 Blueprint sections and controlled sequence
elements: Section 00 — Control & Product Charter. This controlling mission, scope, principles, workflow and governance. ¶ Section 01 — Discovery, Current-State Inventory & Assumptions Register. Verify actual repository/platform state, dependencies, available source access, unknowns and evidence. ¶ Section 02 — Product Requirements, Actors & Workflows. Personas, permissions, user journeys, functional and non-functional requirements. ¶ Section 03 — Domain Model & Canonical Financial Semantics. Entities, relations, states, units, currencies, cost categories, margins, provenance and definitions. ¶ Section 04 — Data Ingestion, Normalisation & Reconciliation. Source contracts, mapping, freshness, idempotency, conflicts, retries and recovery. ¶ Section 05 — Profitability Calculation Engine. Budget/actual/commitment/forecast semantics, cost-to-complete, estimate-at-completion, margin, rounding and reconciliation. ¶ Section 06 — Active Intelligence & Leakage Detection. Event-driven triggers, signal catalogue, root-cause hypotheses, thresholds, evidence, confidence and false-positive handling. ¶ Section 07 — Schedule, Delay & Holding-Cost Intelligence. Schedule dependencies, delay scenarios, time-related costs, acceleration and resequencing economics. ¶ Section 08 — Materials, Global Markets & Procurement Intelligence. Material registry, source coverage, price normalisation, landed cost, forecasts, buy/wait/stage decisions and limits. ¶ Section 09 — Opportunity Discovery & Profit Improvement Engine. Whole-project/business opportunity generation, cross-signal analysis, ranking, feasibility, net benefit and interaction controls. ¶ Section 10 — Recommendations, Scenario Engine & Human Approval. Option comparisons, approval workflow, trade-offs, action lifecycle, outcomes and re-evaluation. ¶ Section 11 — Alerts, Dashboard, Reporting & User Experience. Prioritisation, drill-down, freshness, evidence presentation, accessibility and user actions. ¶ Section 12 — Integrations & Anchor Platform Contracts. Engine/Governor/AUIF boundaries, API/event contracts, external systems, authentication and failures. ¶ Section 13 — Security, Privacy, Audit & Governance. Threat model, permissions, audit, retention, safety and isolation tests. ¶ Section 14 — Testing, Verification & Acceptance. RTM, unit/integration/contract/E2E/property/mutation tests, fixtures and release gates. ¶ Section 15 — Deployment, Operations & Recovery. Environments, observability, backup, migrations, incident handling and rollback. ¶ Section 16 — Implementation Plan & Claude Handoff. Sequenced work packages, discovered file-level instructions, dependencies, stop conditions and evidence outputs. ¶ Section 17 — Gemini Independent Audit Pack. Independent audit protocol, adversarial cases, acceptance matrix, defect classification and closure rules. ¶ Section 18 — Release Readiness & Closure Dossier. Final traceability, test evidence, residual risks, blocked items, sign-off and package/hash manifest.
criticality_rationale: Section sequence is document structure; omission affects navigation, not product behaviour.
issue_note: Heading-only row; list numbering in source starts at 8 (renumbering artefact).

requirement_text: Inspect the actual repository and platform contracts before proposing code changes.
criticality_rationale: Coding before inspecting contracts leads to duplicate infrastructure and incompatible platform integration.
issue_note: Restated as Gate 01-A obligation in Section 01.

requirement_text: Implement against approved, versioned requirements and decisions; maintain traceability by requirement ID.
criticality_rationale: Without requirement-ID traceability, coverage gaps cannot be detected before release.

requirement_text: Keep changes scoped, reviewable, testable and compatible with existing platform invariants.
criticality_rationale: Unscoped changes reduce reviewability and risk breaking platform invariants.
issue_note: "Scoped" and "reviewable" have no objective criterion.

requirement_text: Report exact commands, environment, changed files, test results, failures and limitations.
criticality_rationale: Missing commands and results prevent reproduction of test evidence used for gate decisions.

requirement_text: Never claim a test passed, database was verified, integration works or saving was realised without evidence.
criticality_rationale: False claims of passed tests or realised savings corrupt evidence and release decisions.

requirement_text: Stop and raise a decision request when requirements conflict, a safety/security invariant is unclear, or a dependency blocks safe implementation.
criticality_rationale: Proceeding through conflicts or unclear security invariants risks unsafe implementation.

requirement_text: Do not silently downgrade the active profit-improvement mission to retrospective reporting, basic alerts or a procurement-only tool.
criticality_rationale: Mission downgrade reduces product value; detectable at audit but not financially corrupting.
issue_note: "Silently downgrade" and "basic alerts" lack an objective test; relies on PGR-00-A005.

requirement_text: Audit specifications and implementation independently rather than relying solely on Claude's summary.
criticality_rationale: Audit relying on Claude summaries cannot detect unsupported claims before gate decisions.

requirement_text: Trace each requirement into design, code, tests and evidence; identify omissions and contradictions.
criticality_rationale: Without independent tracing, omitted requirements reach release undetected.

requirement_text: Independently recalculate financial examples and challenge baseline, net-benefit, overlap and forecast assumptions.
criticality_rationale: Unrechecked financial examples allow formula errors into authoritative calculations.

requirement_text: Probe stale/missing/conflicting data, duplicate delivery, partial failure, event replay, concurrency, authorisation and tenant boundaries.
criticality_rationale: Unprobed replay, concurrency or tenant paths leave isolation and integrity defects undetected.

requirement_text: Challenge whether intelligence is genuinely proactive, actionable and evidence-backed, including upside opportunity discovery when no budget breach exists.
criticality_rationale: Weak challenge of proactivity reduces value but not financial integrity.
issue_note: "Genuinely proactive" has no objective acceptance measure.

requirement_text: Classify findings by severity with reproduction steps and evidence; verify fixes after remediation.
criticality_rationale: Unclassified findings lack prioritised remediation and verified fixes.

requirement_text: Do not close mandatory gates while defects, required evidence or DB-dependent items remain unresolved.
criticality_rationale: Closing gates with open defects or DB-dependent items permits release despite failed blocking gates.

requirement_text: Section 01 can be recommended for closure only when:
elements: All mandatory discovery gates have been investigated. ¶ Each gate has evidence-backed findings or explicitly documented blockers. ¶ Platform reuse decisions are justified. ¶ Tenant-isolation risks have been tested where the environment permits. ¶ Audit and state-machine conventions are understood or their gaps recorded. ¶ Integration behaviour and source-freshness constraints are documented. ¶ Financial and post-completion domain reuse is mapped. ¶ Baseline test results and environmental limitations are recorded. ¶ Assumptions and DB-dependent work are tracked. ¶ Architecture implications are ready to inform Section 02.
criticality_rationale: Premature discovery closure lets implementation start on unverified foundations.
issue_note: "Understood", "justified" and "ready to inform" lack objective criteria; "tested where environment permits" allows untested closure.

requirement_text: A documented blocker is not a passed verification. Use PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED or NOT APPLICABLE, with a reason and evidence for each status.
criticality_rationale: Treating a documented blocker as passed falsely asserts verified status.

requirement_text: Production feature/integration freeze until discovery sign-off with narrow diagnostic/prototype exemptions
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-01-1

requirement_text: Tenant-isolation defects block deployment wherever the vulnerable boundary is exposed and are a hard module release-stopper
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-01-2

requirement_text: Gemini audits the complete ten-artifact discovery dossier as one unified package
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-01-3

requirement_text: Section 01 is not complete merely because Claude has read the code. Findings must be recorded in inspectable artifacts.
criticality_rationale: Unrecorded discovery findings leave the exit gate without inspectable inputs.

requirement_text: A. Repository Baseline | Repositories, commits, dependencies, build commands and baseline results.
criticality_rationale: Missing repository baseline prevents reproducible build and test comparison.

requirement_text: B. Platform Contract Inventory | Engine, event bus, Governor, AUIF and relevant module interfaces.
criticality_rationale: Missing contract inventory undermines platform reuse decisions.

requirement_text: C. Tenant Isolation Matrix | Enforcement mechanisms, test evidence and security gaps.
criticality_rationale: Missing tenant isolation matrix removes evidence for the tenant-isolation release gate.

requirement_text: D. Audit & State-Machine Report | Audit semantics, transition rules and financial traceability.
criticality_rationale: Missing audit report leaves financial traceability conventions unverified.

requirement_text: E. Integration Surface Register | Connectors, source coverage, freshness, retries and failure behaviour.
criticality_rationale: Missing integration register hides source freshness and failure behaviour.

requirement_text: F. Domain Reuse Matrix | Existing versus missing financial, construction and post-completion concepts.
criticality_rationale: Missing reuse matrix risks duplicate domain concepts.

requirement_text: G. Assumptions & Unknowns Register | Unverified assumptions, owners, impact and resolution method.
criticality_rationale: Missing register lets unverified assumptions pass as facts.

requirement_text: H. Dependency & Access Register | Missing database access, credentials, services or tooling.
criticality_rationale: Missing access register hides DB-dependent blocked work.

requirement_text: I. Baseline Test Report | Commands executed, results, failures and evidence locations.
criticality_rationale: Missing test report removes executed-command evidence.

requirement_text: J. Discovery Exit Report | Findings, architectural implications, blockers and readiness recommendation.
criticality_rationale: Missing exit report blocks sign-off that gates the implementation freeze.

requirement_text: 4. Evidence and deliverables
elements: Every material finding must reference evidence: repository path and relevant symbol, configuration, schema, test, command output or other verifiable artifact. Narrative assertions must not substitute for executable evidence where executable verification is possible.
criticality_rationale: Narrative-only findings would let unverifiable claims through the discovery gate.
issue_note: Row text is the section heading; the operative evidence-reference rule is the sole element, and is a process rule, not a deliverable.

requirement_text: Status and evidence boundary: This document locks the discovery requirements and governance rules. It does not assert that the live Anchor repository, database, integrations, or security controls have already been inspected or passed. Those conclusions require evidence produced under this specification.
criticality_rationale: Evidence boundary statement; documentation-only.

requirement_text: Section 01 supplies the verified current-state baseline. Section 02 uses that baseline to define product requirements, actors, workflows, permissions and acceptance-level behaviour. Any unresolved discovery finding that materially affects requirements must be carried forward as a named dependency; it must not disappear when the project moves to the next section.
criticality_rationale: Dropped discovery findings become unrecorded dependencies, a missing gate input.

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED — governing discovery specification.
criticality_rationale: Lock status record; documentation-only.

requirement_text: Lock basis: user audit recommendations accepted, including (1) production feature/integration freeze until discovery sign-off with narrow diagnostic/prototype exemptions; (2) tenant-isolation defects block deployment wherever the vulnerable boundary is exposed and are a hard module release-stopper; and (3) Gemini audits the complete ten-artifact discovery dossier as one unified package.
criticality_rationale: Lock basis record; operative rules exist elsewhere.

requirement_text: Evidence boundary: this lock approves the discovery mandate, not the live repository's compliance with it. Repository findings, test results, security status and discovery exit sign-off must be established later from actual evidence.
criticality_rationale: Evidence boundary statement; documentation-only.

requirement_text: Section 01 establishes the evidence-based starting point for building Anchor Profit Guardian — Construction Edition. Before implementation begins, Claude must discover and document the actual state of the Anchor platform, repositories, integration architecture, data model, security boundaries, testing environment and operational constraints. The objective is to reuse established platform capabilities where appropriate, identify genuine gaps, and prevent duplicate infrastructure, incompatible interfaces and unsupported assumptions.
criticality_rationale: Implementing without documented current state causes duplicate infrastructure and unsupported assumptions.

requirement_text: 1. Purpose
elements: Governing rule: repository and environment evidence outrank architectural assumptions. Missing evidence must be recorded, not silently inferred.
criticality_rationale: Inferring missing evidence would present unverified platform state as fact.
issue_note: Row text is the heading "1. Purpose"; the operative governing rule sits in the single element.

requirement_text: Claude must locate and inspect the existing Anchor platform contracts before designing new services or adapters.
criticality_rationale: Designing services before contract inspection risks parallel, incompatible infrastructure.

requirement_text: Gate 01-A — Core Platform Contract Inspection
elements: Central Anchor Engine API wrappers, service interfaces and authentication boundaries. ¶ Event bus, event schemas, delivery semantics and consumer registration. ¶ Governor modules, authorisation flow, adapter contracts, policy enforcement and failure handling. ¶ AUIF and existing connector, module-client and Governor-adapter interfaces, where present. ¶ Entity, organisation, project and state-management conventions. ¶ Workflow execution, notification and audit-log interfaces. ¶ AI orchestration boundaries and deterministic calculation conventions. ¶ API versioning, error envelopes, correlation identifiers and compatibility requirements.
criticality_rationale: Uninspected engine, event or Governor contracts produce incompatible integrations.
issue_note: Heading-only row; inspection list separated from its lead-in PGR-01-N003.

requirement_text: For each relevant interface, record its repository location, public contract, dependencies, callers, tests, failure behaviour and suitability for Profit Guardian. Required output: a Platform Contract Inventory and integration map showing how external data enters Anchor, is validated and reconciled, and reaches governed intelligence and user-facing workflows. Do not create a parallel event bus, authorisation system, audit mechanism or integration framework without evidence that existing capabilities are insufficient.
criticality_rationale: Parallel event bus, auth or audit mechanism would fragment governance and audit integrity.

subclause: Gate 01-B — Tenant and Data Isolation Verification
requirement_text: Claude must establish how multi-tenancy is actually enforced. Inspect and verify, as applicable:
elements: Tenant and organisation identification at authentication and request boundaries. ¶ Database schema, tenant keys and relationship constraints. ¶ PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies, if used. ¶ Application-level tenant filtering and authorisation checks. ¶ Background jobs, event consumers, scheduled tasks and integration callbacks. ¶ Object storage, caches, search indexes and other persistence layers. ¶ Cross-tenant access controls for projects, suppliers, subcontractors, materials, documents and market intelligence. ¶ Administrative access, service accounts and system-level privileges.
criticality_rationale: Unverified tenant enforcement paths could leave cross-tenant data exposure undiscovered.

subclause: Gate 01-B — Tenant and Data Isolation Verification
requirement_text: Do not assume a tenant header, ORM filter or frontend restriction provides sufficient isolation. Required output: a Tenant Isolation Evidence Matrix identifying each data-access path, enforcement mechanism, verification method and unresolved exposure. Tests must attempt cross-tenant access through direct API requests, altered identifiers, background processing and integration/event pathways, as applicable.
criticality_rationale: Relying on headers/ORM filters without cross-tenant tests risks undetected tenant data exposure.

subclause: Gate 01-B — Tenant and Data Isolation Verification
requirement_text: Gate 01-B — Tenant and Data Isolation Verification
elements: Release rule: a demonstrated tenant-isolation defect blocks deployment of Profit Guardian to any environment where the vulnerable boundary is exposed. The defect is a hard release-stopper for the module and affected release paths; unrelated company services that do not expose that boundary need not be halted solely because the defect exists. Closure requires remediation evidence and independent re-testing.
criticality_rationale: Deploying with a demonstrated tenant-isolation defect exposes cross-tenant data.
issue_note: Row text is the Gate 01-B heading; the release-stopper rule is the sole element. It is a release gate, not a heading.

subclause: Gate 01-C — Audit Logging and State Machine Conventions
requirement_text: Inspect the platform's existing audit trail and state-transition architecture before defining financial records or approval workflows.
criticality_rationale: Defining financial records before inspecting audit/state conventions risks non-reproducible records.

subclause: Gate 01-C — Audit Logging and State Machine Conventions
requirement_text: Gate 01-C — Audit Logging and State Machine Conventions
elements: Audit event schemas and persistence. ¶ Actor identity, tenant, timestamp, correlation ID and source provenance. ¶ State-transition rules, invariants and invalid-transition handling. ¶ User approvals, rejections, overrides and reversals. ¶ Financial calculation inputs, versions, outputs and reproducibility. ¶ Event ordering, duplicate handling and concurrent updates. ¶ Immutable or append-only guarantees, if implemented. ¶ Permissions governing audit access and supported retention/export mechanisms.
criticality_rationale: Uninspected audit/state semantics leave duplicate handling and immutability unknown.
issue_note: Heading-only row; inspection list separated from lead-in PGR-01-N009.

subclause: Gate 01-C — Audit Logging and State Machine Conventions
requirement_text: Distinguish between an audit log that records activity and a mechanism that technically prevents historical records from being altered. Neither property may be claimed without evidence. Required output: an Audit and State-Machine Compatibility Report identifying the preferred platform-native mechanism for calculation runs, evidence references, recommendation lifecycle changes and consequential user decisions. Financial calculations must be reproducible from recorded inputs, calculation versions and assumptions. Corrections must preserve the history of prior decisions and outputs rather than silently rewriting it.
criticality_rationale: Unproven immutability claims or rewritten history destroy audit and evidence integrity.

requirement_text: Inspect existing integration infrastructure before designing construction data ingestion.
criticality_rationale: Ingestion designed without mapping idempotency/retry semantics risks duplicate financial records.

requirement_text: Gate 01-D — Integration Surface Mapping
elements: Webhook handlers, authentication and signature verification. ¶ Connector registration and credential management. ¶ Idempotency keys and duplicate-event protection. ¶ Retry policies, backoff, dead-letter handling and replay. ¶ Queue processing, concurrency and stale-message behaviour. ¶ Rate limits, timeouts, cancellation and partial failures. ¶ Pagination, incremental synchronisation and historical backfills. ¶ Data validation, schema changes and malformed-source handling. ¶ Reconciliation of external records against canonical Anchor entities. ¶ Observability, alerting and failed-ingestion recovery.
criticality_rationale: Unmapped retry, idempotency and replay behaviour can corrupt ingested financial data.
issue_note: Heading-only row; list separated from lead-in PGR-01-N012.

requirement_text: Map existing and potential source categories, including accounting, job costing, estimating, scheduling, procurement, supplier quotations, project-management systems and domestic or international material-market sources. These are discovery targets, not claims that particular integrations exist or that specific providers are available. Required output: an Integration Surface Register covering contracts, authentication, data coverage, update cadence, reliability, failure recovery and test evidence. Source freshness and coverage must be explicit. Do not label data real-time when the source updates periodically or ingestion is delayed.
criticality_rationale: Mislabelling periodic data as real-time misleads decisions on stale inputs.
issue_note: Real-time labelling prohibition restates Section 00.4.

requirement_text: 3.1 Repository and build baseline
elements: Identify actual repositories, branches, commit identifiers and relevant package versions. ¶ Inspect project structure, dependency manifests, environment configuration and build/test commands. ¶ Establish module-registration and deployment conventions. ¶ Run available baseline tests and static checks where the environment permits. ¶ Record pre-existing failures separately from defects introduced by Profit Guardian. ¶ Identify unavailable credentials, external services, databases or infrastructure.
criticality_rationale: Missing baseline obscures pre-existing failures versus new defects.
issue_note: Heading-only row; six obligations in elements.

requirement_text: Locate existing representations of organisations, projects, entities, users, budgets, estimates, actual costs, commitments, purchase orders, invoices, supplier quotations, receipts, variations, claims, revenue, commercial approvals, labour, subcontractors, schedules, progress, cash flow, forecasts, scenario assumptions, defects, rectification, retentions, security instruments and post-completion obligations.
criticality_rationale: Unmapped domain models cause duplicate or conflicting entity representations.

requirement_text: Document what exists, what can be reused and what is absent. Do not assume these concepts are already represented in the engine.
criticality_rationale: Assuming concepts exist leads to integration against absent models.

requirement_text: Establish conventions for monetary precision, currency, rounding, tax treatment, unit conversions, time periods and source corrections. Determine whether the platform distinguishes actuals from commitments; forecasts from scenarios; identified opportunities from approved actions; estimated savings from realised savings; avoided costs from cash savings; and gross benefit from net benefit after implementation costs. Record gaps for resolution in later sections rather than prematurely inventing authoritative accounting semantics.
criticality_rationale: Unestablished precision, currency and tax conventions risk incorrect monetary semantics later.

requirement_text: Identify data structures and connectors for material specifications, supplier pricing, quantities, lead times, availability and purchasing history. Determine whether market data is domestic, international or unavailable; whether it is current; and whether units, currencies, taxes, freight, duties and specifications can be compared reliably. Do not claim market coverage, forecast accuracy or purchasing advantage without supporting evidence.
criticality_rationale: Unverified market coverage claims mislead purchasing decisions.

requirement_text: Verify how existing systems represent practical completion and obligations that continue afterwards. Investigate:
elements: Retention amounts withheld, claimed, approved, released and outstanding. ¶ Security instruments, including bank guarantees and performance bonds where applicable. ¶ Expiry dates, release conditions, fees and capital tied up. ¶ Defect liability or maintenance periods, defects and rectification costs. ¶ Relationships between open defects, responsible parties and delayed retention or security release. ¶ Final account, closeout and unresolved obligations.
criticality_rationale: Unmapped post-completion representations delay retention/security monitoring design.

requirement_text: Examine these concepts across Commercial & Revenue, Cash Flow & Capital, and Quality & Post-Completion. An open defect and its related withheld retention are connected facts, not two independent profit losses. Model their effects without double-counting. Do not infer a legal entitlement or release date solely from a generic rule; contract terms and relevant evidence require verification.
criticality_rationale: Double-counting defect and retention, or inferred entitlements, corrupt exposure figures.
issue_note: Defect-retention linkage, no-double-count and no-inferred-entitlement rules restate 00.5.1 elements.

requirement_text: 3.6 Testing and operational readiness
elements: Unit, integration, contract and end-to-end test conventions. ¶ Test fixtures, seed data and isolated test environments. ¶ Database migrations and rollback. ¶ Performance and concurrency testing. ¶ Security testing and dependency scanning. ¶ Logs, metrics, traces and operational alerts. ¶ Backup, restore and recovery procedures.
criticality_rationale: Unknown test and ops conventions delay verifiable delivery.

requirement_text: Record which checks can run immediately and which require unavailable services or access.

requirement_text: Each unresolved item must include:
elements: Unique identifier and description of why it matters. ¶ Evidence currently available. ¶ Classification: verified fact, provisional inference, unverified assumption or blocker. ¶ Risk if the assumption is wrong. ¶ Required action and responsible party. ¶ Validation method and acceptance evidence. ¶ Status and closure date, once resolved.

requirement_text: A missing answer must remain visible. Do not convert 'not inspected' into 'not present', or 'not tested' into 'working'.

requirement_text: If a real or staging database, credentials, integrations or required tooling are unavailable, Claude must continue with all work that can be completed safely without them. The DB-Dependent Closure Register must record each deferred item:
elements: Exact blocked task. ¶ Why missing access prevents valid completion. ¶ Exact instructions for Amir or the responsible environment owner. ¶ Query, migration, integration test or validation to run when access is available. ¶ Required evidence to prove closure. ¶ Dependencies and downstream sections affected.
criticality_rationale: Unrecorded DB-dependent tasks lose closure instructions and downstream impact.

requirement_text: No affected task may be declared closed merely because code was written or mocked tests passed.

requirement_text: Zero production feature code or core integration logic may be merged or executed until the Section 01 Discovery Exit Report is signed off. requirement_text: Claude must submit the complete ten-artifact package (Artifacts A through J) as a unified dossier. requirement_text: Anchor Profit Guardian is an active construction profit protection and improvement system. It must help construction businesses identify where profit is leaking, explain why with evidence, identify additional profit that could be protected or created, recommend timely actions and measure whether those actions improved the financial outcome.
criticality_rationale: Without this definition scope could narrow to passive reporting.
issue_note: Restates Section 00 mission; "help" has no objective pass/fail.

requirement_text: It must operate across the project lifecycle, from estimating and procurement through construction, practical completion, final account and post-completion obligations. It is not merely a job-costing dashboard, procurement optimiser, compliance system or retrospective reporting tool. Those may supply data or capabilities, but the governing objective is to improve the economic outcome of the construction business.
criticality_rationale: Lifecycle gaps leave final-account and post-completion profit unmonitored.
issue_note: Second sentence restates Section 00.2 "not merely" scope statement.

requirement_text: Commercial & revenue | Variations, claims, scope changes, commercial entitlements, final accounts and revenue at risk.
criticality_rationale: Missed variation and claim tracking leaves revenue leakage undetected.

requirement_text: Costs & commitments | Budgets, estimates, actuals, commitments, forecasts, cost overruns and emerging margin pressure.
criticality_rationale: Missed overrun and margin-pressure detection delays leakage response.

criticality_rationale: Undetected delay exposure delays mitigation of holding costs.

criticality_rationale: Missed defect/retention exposure leaves post-completion capital unmonitored.

requirement_text: Suppliers, subcontractors & trade compliance | Pricing, delivery reliability, variation behaviour, quality outcomes, commitments, licensing, insurance validity, safety accreditations and relevant statutory or industrial compliance risk.
criticality_rationale: Missed compliance and supplier risk causes work interruption and replacement cost.

requirement_text: Design & constructability | Evidence-backed opportunities involving specifications, sequencing, alternatives and avoidable construction costs.
criticality_rationale: Missed constructability opportunities reduce upside only.

requirement_text: Equipment & logistics | Plant utilisation, hire duration, delivery coordination, storage, transport and idle-resource costs.
criticality_rationale: Missed idle-plant costs reduce leakage visibility with limited consequence.

requirement_text: Cash flow & capital | Forecast inflows and outflows, payment timing, working capital, retention balances and capital tied up in security.
criticality_rationale: Missed cash-flow and tied-capital visibility misleads working-capital decisions.

requirement_text: Markets & external conditions | Domestic and international price signals, supply availability, freight, currency, lead times and market uncertainty.
criticality_rationale: Missing market signals reduce procurement decision quality.

criticality_rationale: Missed cross-project patterns lose transferable lessons.

requirement_text: These are required areas of intelligence, not a claim that every data source is already integrated. Each feature must identify its data prerequisites, coverage, freshness and limitations. Compliance-related intelligence must record the source, status, expiry or review date where relevant, and verification provenance; it must not represent an unverified document or third-party signal as definitive legal compliance.
criticality_rationale: Unverified documents presented as legal compliance mislead risk decisions.

requirement_text: 2.2 Core product capabilities
elements: Continuous or source-event-driven monitoring, subject to actual source freshness. ¶ Detection of existing and emerging profit leakage. ¶ Identification of profit-improvement opportunities even when budgets remain on track. ¶ Quantification of financial exposure and potential benefit. ¶ Prioritisation by financial materiality, urgency, confidence and actionability. ¶ Recommendations with evidence, assumptions, trade-offs and deadlines. ¶ Scenario comparison before consequential decisions. ¶ Human approval and an auditable record of consequential actions. ¶ Verification of actual outcomes against the original estimate. ¶ Project, portfolio and business-level visibility without double-counting.
criticality_rationale: Missing core capabilities degrade detection, prioritisation and outcome verification.
issue_note: Heading-only row; ten capabilities in elements.

requirement_text: The following are logical roles. Section 01 must establish actual Anchor identity and authorisation conventions before mapping them to platform roles.
criticality_rationale: Mapping roles before discovery risks mismatched platform authorisation.

requirement_text: 3.1 Permission and segregation principles
elements: Access is scoped to the authorised organisation, projects and functions. ¶ A recommendation does not grant permission to execute the recommended action. ¶ Approval rights are explicit and configurable within the platform's verified authorisation model. ¶ Sensitive commercial, supplier and financial information must not be exposed to unauthorised users or tenants. ¶ Administrative access must not silently alter financial history. ¶ Where practical and supported by policy, preparation of financial data and approval of consequential financial actions should be separated. ¶ The AI component cannot grant itself permissions or override deterministic governance.
criticality_rationale: AI self-granting permissions or admins altering history corrupts governance and audit integrity.
issue_note: Segregation element "where practical and supported by policy" is untestable; row text is heading only.

subclause: Workflow A — Connect and establish the project baseline
requirement_text: Workflow A — Connect and establish the project baseline
elements: Connect authorised data sources. ¶ Validate and normalise incoming records. ¶ Reconcile records against canonical project and business entities. ¶ Flag missing, contradictory, stale or low-quality data for correction. ¶ Establish a verified baseline when required data quality thresholds are met. ¶ Calculate the current financial position using versioned deterministic logic. ¶ Activate monitoring and expose any known coverage limitations.
criticality_rationale: Activating monitoring on an unverified baseline produces unqualified findings.
issue_note: "Required data quality thresholds" for a verified baseline are not specified here or found elsewhere; heading-only row.

subclause: Workflow A — Connect and establish the project baseline
requirement_text: The baseline must distinguish approved budgets, estimates, actual costs, commitments, forecasts and scenarios. Missing data must be visible rather than silently replaced with assumed values.
criticality_rationale: Silently assumed values or blurred budget/actual/commitment states produce wrong authoritative figures.

subclause: Workflow B — Detect leakage and create an actionable finding
requirement_text: Workflow B — Detect leakage and create an actionable finding
elements: Process a source event or scheduled refresh. ¶ Validate evidence, provenance and freshness. ¶ Evaluate relevant financial and operational rules. ¶ Determine whether a material issue or opportunity exists. ¶ Calculate potential impact and uncertainty where inputs permit. ¶ Check for duplicate or related findings sharing the same underlying exposure. ¶ Prioritise the finding and assign an authorised owner. ¶ Notify the appropriate user and preserve the evidence trail.
criticality_rationale: Missing duplicate checks or ownership delays and inflates leakage findings.
issue_note: Heading-only row; eight steps in elements.

subclause: Workflow B — Detect leakage and create an actionable finding
requirement_text: The system should detect issues before they become final losses wherever available data permits. It must also identify improvement opportunities that are not triggered by a budget breach.
criticality_rationale: Late detection converts recoverable exposure into final loss.
issue_note: Second sentence restates PG-FR-005; first sentence uses "should".

subclause: Workflow C — Evaluate a profit-improvement opportunity
requirement_text: Workflow C — Evaluate a profit-improvement opportunity
elements: Identify the opportunity and supporting evidence. ¶ Establish the current baseline and relevant constraints. ¶ Calculate estimated gross benefit, implementation cost and net benefit. ¶ Identify uncertainty, timing, dependencies and downside risk. ¶ Compare realistic alternatives. ¶ Recommend an action and specify the required approver. ¶ Record the decision and the baseline used. ¶ Track execution and measure the realised outcome.
criticality_rationale: Unevaluated implementation cost or alternatives misstates net benefit of opportunities.
issue_note: Heading-only row; eight steps in elements.

subclause: Workflow C — Evaluate a profit-improvement opportunity
requirement_text: Do not report the same benefit as both avoided cost and realised savings, or count a cost reduction twice through linked findings.
criticality_rationale: Counting a benefit as both avoided and realised overstates authoritative profit figures.

requirement_text: Workflow D — Materials purchase timing
elements: Identify the required material, specification, quantity and required-on-site date. ¶ Compare project demand with ordered, delivered, consumed, returned, damaged, wasted and remaining quantities where those records are available. ¶ Retrieve available supplier quotations and supported market signals. ¶ Normalise comparable prices and calculate landed cost where relevant. ¶ Compare buy-now, wait, staged-purchase and negotiation scenarios. ¶ Account for lead time, quote expiry, schedule risk, storage, financing, availability and specification. ¶ Present a recommendation with assumptions and a break-even threshold where calculable. ¶ Obtain authorised human approval before placing an order. ¶ Compare the eventual purchase and delivery outcome with the original recommendation.
criticality_rationale: Placing orders without authorised human approval bypasses control of a consequential action.
issue_note: Heading-only row; approval step is element 8 of nine.

requirement_text: A cheaper international market price is not automatically a cheaper purchase. Freight, duties, foreign exchange, specification differences, quality, availability and delivery risk may reverse the apparent advantage.
criticality_rationale: Explanatory rationale; operative rule is landed-cost comparison in PGR-02-N043.

subclause: Workflow E — Delay and holding-cost exposure
requirement_text: Workflow E — Delay and holding-cost exposure
elements: Detect a schedule deviation or emerging delay risk from available evidence. ¶ Identify affected milestones and dependent work. ¶ Estimate incremental time-related costs. ¶ Separate observed costs from modelled exposure. ¶ Identify feasible mitigation options and their costs. ¶ Compare the expected net effect of each option. ¶ Assign the action to an authorised owner. ¶ Monitor the schedule and update the estimate as evidence changes. ¶ Compare forecast exposure with actual outcomes.
criticality_rationale: Unseparated observed and modelled delay costs mislead mitigation decisions.
issue_note: Heading-only row; nine steps in elements.

subclause: Workflow E — Delay and holding-cost exposure
requirement_text: Do not automatically attribute delay to a party or assert a contractual entitlement without supporting evidence and appropriate review.
criticality_rationale: Asserting delay responsibility without evidence misleads commercial and claim decisions.

subclause: Workflow F — Retentions, security and post-completion
requirement_text: Workflow F — Retentions, security and post-completion
elements: Record practical completion and relevant documented contractual milestones. ¶ Track retention balances and their evidenced status. ¶ Register applicable security instruments, costs, expiry dates and release conditions. ¶ Track defects, responsible parties, rectification costs and maintenance periods. ¶ Link open defects to relevant retention or security conditions where evidence supports the relationship. ¶ Highlight approaching dates, blocked releases, unresolved closeout items and capital remaining tied up. ¶ Recommend evidence gathering, follow-up or review by an authorised person. ¶ Track release, recovery, rectification and final closure. ¶ Reconcile the final financial outcome without counting a single underlying exposure multiple times.
criticality_rationale: Counting a single post-completion exposure multiple times misstates final financial outcome.
issue_note: Heading-only row; nine steps in elements.

subclause: Workflow F — Retentions, security and post-completion
requirement_text: Monitoring must continue after practical completion until relevant obligations are closed, explicitly transferred or otherwise resolved with documented evidence.
criticality_rationale: Premature end of monitoring misses retention release and defect obligations.
issue_note: Restates Section 00.5.1 continuation rule.

subclause: Workflow G — Subcontractor and trade compliance exposure
requirement_text: Workflow G — Subcontractor and trade compliance exposure
elements: Identify subcontractors and trades associated with projects, scopes and active work. ¶ Record available licensing, insurance, safety accreditation and relevant statutory or industrial compliance evidence, including provenance and expiry or review dates. ¶ Flag missing, expired, conflicting or unverified evidence without falsely declaring legal non-compliance where the evidence is inconclusive. ¶ Assess documented operational and financial consequences, such as possible work interruption, replacement cost, delay exposure or additional verification effort. ¶ Assign the issue to an authorised compliance, commercial or project owner for verification and action. ¶ Track evidence refresh, human decisions and the resulting operational or financial outcome.
criticality_rationale: Unflagged expired licences or insurance risk work interruption and replacement costs.
issue_note: Heading-only row; six steps in elements.

requirement_text: Workflow H — Validate realised benefit
elements: Original estimate and assumptions. ¶ Approved action and decision date. ¶ Execution evidence. ¶ Actual financial result. ¶ Difference between estimated and realised benefit. ¶ Reasons for material differences. ¶ Outcome classification: realised, partially realised, avoided, reversed or unverified.
criticality_rationale: Without validation fields, estimates could be reported as realised benefit.
issue_note: Source lists record fields with no obligation verb or lead-in; required behaviour must be inferred.

requirement_text: This feedback should improve future recommendations without silently changing historical calculations or presenting correlation as proof of causation.

requirement_text: Every actionable recommendation should use a consistent logical structure:
elements: Finding: what was detected, where and when. ¶ Evidence: source records, calculations, timestamps and data-quality limitations. ¶ Financial effect: current exposure, potential gross benefit, expected net benefit and calculation basis. ¶ Action: specific proposed intervention and accountable role. ¶ Alternatives: relevant options and their cost, timing and downside trade-offs. ¶ Uncertainty: confidence, assumptions, sensitivity and missing information. ¶ Decision: approval requirements, status, decision-maker and timestamp. ¶ Outcome: execution evidence and measured financial result, if available.
criticality_rationale: Inconsistent recommendation structure omits evidence, alternatives or decision record.

requirement_text: A recommendation must not be labelled guaranteed savings. Estimated benefits remain estimates until validated. A recommendation may be withdrawn, superseded or invalidated when evidence changes, but its historical record must remain traceable.
criticality_rationale: Labelling estimates as guaranteed or erasing superseded history falsely claims realised status.

requirement_text: 7. Financial and decision boundaries
elements: Deterministic financial core: authoritative arithmetic must use versioned, testable calculation logic. AI-generated explanations must not alter authoritative totals. ¶ No unsupported certainty: incomplete or stale source data must affect recommendations and be disclosed. ¶ Human approval only for consequential external actions: purchasing, purchase orders, contracts, variations, claims submissions, supplier changes, design or material substitutions, changes to bills of quantities and other actions that create external financial, legal, safety, warranty or contractual consequences require an authorised human decision and verified approval before execution. ¶ Advisory and analytical operation: in the initial release, Profit Guardian may detect, calculate, prioritise, model, explain, recommend, notify and track, but it must not autonomously execute consequential external actions. ¶ No unsupported contractual conclusions: entitlements, delay responsibility and legal obligations must not be inferred as established facts without appropriate evidence and review. ¶ No double-counting: linked findings must represent shared underlying financial exposures explicitly. ¶ No unverified market claims: coverage, forecasts and expected purchasing advantages require source evidence and stated limitations. ¶ No autonomous expansion of authority: AI cannot bypass platform permissions or governance rules.
criticality_rationale: Breaching boundaries lets AI alter totals or autonomously execute consequential actions.
issue_note: Heading-only row; eight boundary rules in elements.

requirement_text: The human-approval-only boundary is a permanent default for the initial release, not a temporary implementation convenience. requirement_text: The system must avoid duplicate and low-value alert flooding. requirement_text: Section 03 defines the canonical domain model and financial semantics for Anchor Profit Guardian — Construction Edition. Every module, integration, calculation, recommendation and report must interpret construction business data consistently. The model connects commercial revenue, project costs, procurement, productivity, schedule exposure, cash flow, defects and post-completion obligations without contradictory figures or double-counting the same economic event.
criticality_rationale: Inconsistent interpretation across modules yields contradictory figures; purpose-level statement only.
issue_note: Purpose statement "interpret consistently" has no objective pass/fail; enforced via specific rules N006, N007, N020.

requirement_text: 1. Purpose
elements: Governing principle: one canonical meaning for each financial concept, one traceable source for each recorded fact, and explicit relationships between facts that affect the same economic outcome.

requirement_text: Use existing Anchor primitives where suitable. Do not create duplicate canonical entities solely because Profit Guardian needs a different view. Repository inspection must determine actual schemas, names and service boundaries.

requirement_text: 3.1 Identity and duplicate handling
elements: Distinguish source records from the canonical entities to which they map. ¶ Scope external identifiers to the source system and relevant tenant or organisation context. ¶ Do not merge records solely because names, amounts or dates look similar. ¶ Flag ambiguous matches for reconciliation. ¶ Keep source revisions traceable. ¶ Preserve history needed to reconstruct prior calculations and decisions.
criticality_rationale: Unscoped identifiers or similarity merges corrupt financial records or collide across tenants.

requirement_text: These categories have different meanings. Related representations of one underlying item must not be summed as though each were a separate economic event.
criticality_rationale: Summing related representations double-counts one economic event in authoritative figures.

requirement_text: 4.1 Mandatory separation rules
elements: An estimate is not an actual. ¶ A commitment is not automatically an incurred cost or cash payment. ¶ A forecast is not an approved budget. ¶ A scenario is not the current expected result unless explicitly adopted as the forecast. ¶ An opportunity is not a saving. ¶ An avoided cost is not automatically a reduction in recorded expenditure. ¶ A retention balance is not automatically a loss. ¶ A bank guarantee's face value is not automatically a project expense. ¶ Potential delay cost is not actual cost until supported by financial evidence. ¶ A recommendation's estimated benefit is not a realised benefit until measured and verified.
criticality_rationale: Conflating estimate/actual or claiming unverified benefit produces false authoritative figures or realised status.

clause: 5. Canonical financial views and margin authority
requirement_text: Profit Guardian must support multiple explicitly named financial views. It must not collapse accounting performance, expected final project performance and liquidity/capital pressure into a single margin figure. Every view must disclose its definition, inputs, time basis, assumptions, exclusions and calculation version.
criticality_rationale: Collapsing accounting, forecast and liquidity into one margin yields a wrong authoritative figure.

clause: 5. Canonical financial views and margin authority
requirement_text: Recognised Margin represents recognised revenue less recognised costs for a defined reporting period or cumulative reporting basis, under the accounting and progress-recognition policy applicable to the business/project. The system must identify the policy and source data used. It must not independently assert compliance with accounting standards or infer earned revenue solely from cash received.
criticality_rationale: Inferring earned revenue from cash received misstates recognised margin.

clause: 5. Canonical financial views and margin authority
requirement_text: Forecast Final Margin represents forecast final revenue less forecast final cost at project completion. It must use a defined estimate-at-completion (EAC) approach, current cost-to-complete assumptions, relevant commitments, known commercial changes and documented risks. Actual costs and remaining forecasts must not overlap. Unapproved claims or variations must remain explicitly classified rather than silently treated as secured revenue.
criticality_rationale: Overlapping actuals/forecasts or treating unapproved claims as secured inflates forecast margin.

clause: 5. Canonical financial views and margin authority
requirement_text: Cash-Position-Adjusted Margin is a distinct management view that connects project economics with cash collection, overdue payments, disputed variations, withheld retentions, payment timing and other working-capital constraints. It must not be presented as a statutory or accounting margin. Its exact calculation must be explicitly defined and versioned, with components and assumptions shown, so users can distinguish underlying profitability from liquidity pressure.
criticality_rationale: Undefined cash-adjusted calculation may be confused with accounting margin.
issue_note: Exact Cash-Position-Adjusted Margin calculation is required but not specified here or in Section 05 §3.4.

clause: 5. Canonical financial views and margin authority
requirement_text: 5.4 Required view metadata
elements: Canonical view identifier and version. ¶ Reporting period and effective timestamp. ¶ Revenue and cost recognition basis. ¶ Included and excluded categories. ¶ Source records and reconciliation status. ¶ Currency and tax treatment. ¶ Treatment of unapproved claims, retention and security. ¶ Assumptions, limitations and confidence indicators where relevant.
criticality_rationale: Missing view metadata leaves margin figures unqualified and irreproducible.

clause: 5. Canonical financial views and margin authority
requirement_text: The same project may legitimately show different values across these views. The interface must label the views clearly and explain material differences rather than treating them as contradictory values.
criticality_rationale: Unlabelled view differences mislead users into treating margins as contradictory.

requirement_text: 6.1 Revenue concepts
elements: Contracted or approved revenue. ¶ Approved variations. ¶ Submitted but unapproved variations. ¶ Claims submitted, certified, disputed or rejected. ¶ Forecast additional revenue. ¶ Revenue at risk. ¶ Amounts invoiced, received and outstanding. ¶ Retention withheld from payments. ¶ Final-account adjustments.
criticality_rationale: Missing revenue states prevents separating approved from claimed revenue.

requirement_text: These states must not be collapsed into one revenue field. A submitted variation is not approved revenue merely because it has been submitted.
criticality_rationale: Collapsing revenue states treats submitted variations as approved revenue.

requirement_text: 6.2 Cost concepts
elements: Original estimate and current approved budget. ¶ Revised estimate and forecast cost to complete. ¶ Actual costs, outstanding commitments and accruals. ¶ Risk-adjusted or scenario cost. ¶ Unapproved cost exposure. ¶ Expected rectification cost. ¶ Verified cost savings.
criticality_rationale: Missing cost states prevents separating actual, committed and forecast cost.

requirement_text: Business-specific estimating and accounting conventions must be explicit and consistently applied.
criticality_rationale: Inconsistent conventions reduce comparability across projects.
issue_note: "Explicit and consistently applied" lacks a stated recording location or verification method.

requirement_text: For a defined scope, period and accounting convention:
elements: Gross Margin = Recognised Revenue − Recognised Cost. ¶ Gross Margin % = Gross Margin ÷ Recognised Revenue × 100, when the denominator is valid and non-zero. ¶ Forecast Final Cost = Actual Cost to Date + Forecast Cost to Complete, only where the inputs are compatible and non-overlapping. ¶ Forecast Final Margin = Forecast Final Revenue − Forecast Final Cost.
criticality_rationale: Wrong core margin/forecast formulas produce wrong authoritative financial figures.
issue_note: Uses Actual Cost to Date where PGR-05-N008 uses Cost Recognised to Date; "Gross Margin" duplicates Recognised Margin under another name.

requirement_text: The system must define zero or negative revenue handling. Accounting treatment for accruals, unapproved claims, contingency, overhead allocation and tax must be specified before implementation.
criticality_rationale: Unspecified accounting treatments leave margin calculations open to inconsistent assumptions.
issue_note: Negative-revenue handling, accrual, contingency, overhead and tax treatments deferred; zero denominator covered only in PGR-05-N005.

requirement_text: 6.4 No mixed-basis calculations
