elements: Do not silently combine cash-received revenue with incurred costs. ¶ Do not combine budget values from one revision with actuals for an incompatible scope. ¶ Do not mix tax-inclusive costs and tax-exclusive revenue without normalisation. ¶ Do not count committed costs and actual costs where actuals already replace the same commitment. ¶ Do not combine historical prices and current quotations without dates and comparability adjustments. ¶ If a comparable calculation cannot be produced reliably, report the limitation instead of inventing a result.
criticality_rationale: Mixed-basis arithmetic produces invalid authoritative financial results.

requirement_text: The logical lifecycle may include estimate/budget, quote/tender, approved commitment, delivery or work performed, invoice/cost evidence, reconciliation/posting, actual cost and payment/settlement. Actual source systems may have different statuses; preserve equivalent semantics.
criticality_rationale: Losing equivalent lifecycle semantics weakens commitment-to-actual reconciliation.
issue_note: "May include" lifecycle is permissive; only "preserve equivalent semantics" is binding and lacks criteria.

requirement_text: 7. Cost and commitment lifecycle
elements: Purchase orders must have identifiable revisions and approval history. ¶ Changes to scope, quantity, price or status must be traceable. ¶ Partially fulfilled commitments must not be treated as fully consumed without evidence. ¶ Actual costs and remaining commitments must be reconciled under documented rules. ¶ Cancelled commitments must not remain fully active in forecasts. ¶ Invoices linked to purchase orders must not be counted as both a fully outstanding commitment and an additional independent future cost. ¶ Credits and reversals should link to the original record where possible. ¶ Duplicate source events must not create duplicate financial effects.
criticality_rationale: Commitment/invoice double counting or stale cancelled POs corrupt forecast cost.

requirement_text: 8.1 Material specification
elements: Material identity and category. ¶ Grade, class, performance rating, dimensions, size and tolerances where relevant. ¶ Standard, certification or compliance requirements. ¶ Brand or approved-equivalent constraints where contractually relevant. ¶ Unit of measure, packaging and order multiples. ¶ Required quality and delivery conditions. ¶ Source and revision of the specification.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete specifications allow non-comparable materials to be compared.

requirement_text: Two prices must not be treated as equivalent solely because they refer to the same broad material category.
criticality_rationale: False price equivalence misleads procurement recommendations.

requirement_text: Distinguish required, planned, quoted, ordered, delivered, accepted, consumed/installed, returned, damaged, wasted and remaining usable stock where relevant. Quantity states must be connected by documented movements and reconciliations; the same physical quantity cannot be counted as both inventory and consumed material.
criticality_rationale: Counting quantities as both stock and consumed misstates material cost.

requirement_text: 8.3 Procurement cost semantics
elements: Supplier unit price and extended quotation value. ¶ Contracted purchase price. ¶ Freight and handling. ¶ Insurance, duties and applicable taxes. ¶ Currency conversion. ¶ Storage and financing costs. ¶ Expected waste or yield loss. ¶ Delivery and schedule-related costs. ¶ Total landed cost or another explicitly defined comparable cost.
criticality_rationale: Missing cost components reduce procurement comparison completeness.

requirement_text: Where a component is unavailable, disclose the omission. Do not label an incomplete supplier price as verified total landed cost.
criticality_rationale: Labelling incomplete price as verified landed cost is a false verified claim.

requirement_text: 8.4 Buy, wait and stage scenarios
elements: Required-on-site date; current quotation and expiry, if available. ¶ Expected delivery time, availability and substitution constraints. ¶ Price assumptions and source timestamps. ¶ Early-purchase storage and capital costs. ¶ Waiting risks, including price movement and schedule exposure. ¶ Scenario-specific assumptions, uncertainty and human approval requirements.
criticality_rationale: Missing scenario inputs degrade buy/wait recommendation quality.

requirement_text: A wait recommendation must account for the cost of late delivery. An early-buy recommendation must account for storage, financing, damage, obsolescence and quantity-change risk.
criticality_rationale: Ignoring late-delivery or holding risks produces misleading procurement recommendations.

requirement_text: Schedule facts include planned, forecast and actual dates; milestone dependencies; progress; delay events; schedule revisions; and required-on-site dates.
criticality_rationale: Enumerates schedule facts; descriptive with no obligation.

requirement_text: 9. Schedule, delay and holding-cost semantics
elements: Every effect must have a defined calculation basis and time window. ¶ A schedule deviation does not automatically establish contractual responsibility. ¶ Causation and entitlement may require additional evidence and human review. ¶ Overlapping delay events must not count the same days or holding costs multiple times.
criticality_rationale: Unbased or overlapping delay costs overstate exposure and misattribute responsibility.

requirement_text: 10.1 Retention record
elements: Associated contract and project. ¶ Relevant contractual clause or evidence reference. ¶ Retention basis and calculation method. ¶ Amounts withheld, claimed for release, approved, released and outstanding. ¶ Relevant milestone and documented due/review date. ¶ Conditions, disputes and linked defects. ¶ Source system, revision and last verification.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete retention records hide release conditions and outstanding balances.

requirement_text: Distinguish a balance withheld from an amount confirmed due for release. Do not infer a contractual release date without supporting terms and evidence.
criticality_rationale: Treating withheld balance as due or inferring release dates misstates receivables.

requirement_text: 10.2 Security instrument record
elements: Instrument type and issuer. ¶ Associated contract and beneficiary where relevant. ¶ Face value and currency. ¶ Issue and expiry dates. ¶ Documented release or reduction conditions. ¶ Fees and renewal costs. ¶ Capital or facility usage where known. ¶ Status, verification evidence and linked obligations, disputes or defects.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete security records reduce expiry/release monitoring.

requirement_text: Face value is not itself an expense. Fees, renewal costs and capital/facility constraints are separate concepts.
criticality_rationale: Booking security face value as expense produces wrong authoritative cost.

requirement_text: 10.3 Defect and DLP record
elements: Defect identifier, description, project/location and related work package. ¶ Discovery date and evidence. ¶ Severity and operational impact. ¶ Responsible party where established. ¶ Rectification estimate and actual cost. ¶ Rectification status and verification. ¶ Applicable defect liability or maintenance period. ¶ Relevant contractual obligations and source references. ¶ Links to retention or security conditions where supported.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete defect records weaken DLP and retention linkage.

requirement_text: The system must model the face value of withheld retention or security separately from the incremental economic cost of having capital tied up. It must not label the face value as a profit loss solely because it remains withheld or secured.
criticality_rationale: Labelling withheld face value as profit loss misstates margin.

requirement_text: Where sufficient evidence exists, the system may calculate an estimated carrying cost using a documented principal/balance, time window, annualised rate, rate source, day-count convention and calculation method. It must distinguish an actual financing expense from an estimated opportunity cost or scenario.
criticality_rationale: Confusing estimated opportunity cost with actual financing expense misleads decisions.

requirement_text: A simple conceptual model is: Estimated Carrying Cost = Eligible Tied-Up Balance × Applicable Annual Rate × Applicable Time Fraction. The exact convention, compounding, balance changes and rate selection must be explicit and versioned.
criticality_rationale: Unversioned or unspecified carrying-cost conventions yield irreproducible estimates.
issue_note: Eligibility rule for "Eligible Tied-Up Balance" and rate selection deferred; partially addressed by PGR-12-N016.

requirement_text: An unresolved defect may delay a retention release. Represent the defect, affected retention and any resulting incremental financing cost as linked records, not automatically as independent losses. Distinguish the withheld balance, the portion demonstrably affected by a condition, the estimated release timing, incremental carrying cost, actual rectification cost and additional security fees. Aggregate only the appropriate economic effects.
criticality_rationale: Treating linked defect/retention effects as independent losses double counts.
issue_note: "Aggregate only the appropriate economic effects" gives no aggregation rule.

requirement_text: Practical completion alone does not mean the project is economically closed. Relevant obligations remain monitored until documented as closed, explicitly transferred, validly waived or otherwise resolved. Outstanding retention, security, defect and final-account items remain visible in authorised views.
criticality_rationale: Treating practical completion as closure falsely reports economic closure.

requirement_text: Every monetary value must have an explicit currency. Currency conversions must record source and target currencies, rate source, rate and timestamp, conversion method, included fees/adjustments and whether the rate is actual, quoted, contractual or scenario-based.
criticality_rationale: Missing currency or conversion provenance produces wrong financial figures.

requirement_text: Material and labour quantities must have explicit units. Conversions must use defined, testable rules. Incompatible quantities must not be compared or aggregated without conversion or an explanation of the limitation.
criticality_rationale: Aggregating incompatible units misleads quantity and cost comparison.

requirement_text: Distinguish effective/event time, source-reported time, Anchor observation time, persistence time and calculation time. Contractual dates, calendar versus working days, time zones and business calendars must be explicit wherever they affect financial outcomes.
criticality_rationale: Ambiguous time bases misstate period, delay and calendar-dependent calculations.

requirement_text: Record tax-inclusive/exclusive treatment where applicable. Freight, duties, discounts, rebates and other adjustments must be explicit where they affect comparability. Unknown inclusions must be marked unknown rather than assumed.
criticality_rationale: Assumed tax/inclusions distort cost comparability.

clause: 12. Finding, recommendation, decision and outcome relationships
requirement_text: Preserve the distinction between what was observed, inferred, recommended, decided, executed and verified.
criticality_rationale: Blurring observed, inferred and verified states misleads decision quality.

clause: 12. Finding, recommendation, decision and outcome relationships
requirement_text: 12. Finding, recommendation, decision and outcome relationships
elements: Findings reference supporting evidence and calculations. ¶ Recommendations reference the findings that justify them. ¶ Decisions identify the authorised actor, decision time and recommendation version. ¶ Approved actions are distinguishable from proposed actions. ¶ Outcomes are distinguishable from estimated benefits. ¶ Superseded findings remain historically traceable. ¶ Related findings can link to shared causes, transactions, obligations or exposures. ¶ Portfolio aggregation avoids counting the same underlying effect multiple times. ¶ Historical results remain reproducible under verified audit and retention capabilities.
criticality_rationale: Unlinked or double-aggregated outcomes allow false realised-benefit claims.

requirement_text: 13. Canonical state and transition rules
elements: Reject or explicitly handle invalid transitions. ¶ Enforce the verified authorisation model for consequential transitions. ¶ Retries must not duplicate a transition or financial effect. ¶ State changes preserve provenance and relevant prior values. ¶ Corrections and reversals remain traceable. ¶ Approval alone does not mean a recommendation was executed. ¶ Task completion alone does not prove a defect is verified as resolved where independent verification is required. ¶ A retention is not released merely because release was requested or approved; status requires evidence.
criticality_rationale: Unauthorised transitions or status without evidence falsely claim executed, resolved or released.

requirement_text: 14.1 Deterministic responsibilities
elements: Arithmetic and aggregation. ¶ Unit and currency conversion under explicit rules. ¶ Budget-to-actual and forecast comparisons. ¶ Commitment and cost reconciliation. ¶ Financial impact calculations and scenario arithmetic. ¶ Retention/security balances and carrying-cost calculations. ¶ Duplicate-exposure controls and reproducible results.
criticality_rationale: Non-deterministic handling of listed operations undermines reproducibility.

requirement_text: 14.2 AI-assisted responsibilities
elements: Classify unstructured evidence for review. ¶ Identify candidate relationships or anomalies. ¶ Summarise source evidence and explain calculation results. ¶ Suggest potential interventions and candidate scenarios. ¶ Highlight missing information.
criticality_rationale: Scopes AI assistance; boundary enforced by N051.

requirement_text: AI output must not silently become an authoritative financial fact. Material extracted or inferred information must be validated according to risk and evidence quality.
criticality_rationale: AI output silently becoming authoritative corrupts financial facts.
issue_note: "Validated according to risk and evidence quality" lacks criteria; strengthened by PGR-04-N022.

requirement_text: 14.3 Calculation record
elements: Calculation identifier and version. ¶ Input record identifiers and revisions. ¶ Relevant source timestamps. ¶ Formula or rule identifier. ¶ Assumptions and scenario parameters. ¶ Output values and currency. ¶ Warnings and data-quality limitations. ¶ Execution timestamp and references to resulting findings/recommendations.
criticality_rationale: Missing calculation record fields breaks audit and evidence integrity.

requirement_text: Material calculations must be reproducible from recorded inputs and calculation versions, subject to documented source availability and platform retention capabilities.
criticality_rationale: Irreproducible material calculations lose audit integrity.

requirement_text: Map the logical model to existing Anchor entities and data contracts.
criticality_rationale: Unmapped model risks duplicate or incompatible schemas; gates implementation.

requirement_text: Reuse suitable existing canonical entities rather than create duplicates.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate entities cause divergent records.
issue_note: Restates N003 reuse/no-duplicate-entity rule.

requirement_text: Identify gaps and propose the smallest coherent extensions that satisfy the requirements.
criticality_rationale: Oversized extensions add complexity; limited financial consequence.
issue_note: "Smallest coherent extensions" is a judgement with no objective test.

requirement_text: Define schemas, relationships, constraints and lifecycle rules in accordance with established platform conventions.
criticality_rationale: Missing constraints weaken enforcement of domain rules.

requirement_text: Document authoritative source and precedence rules for each financial fact.
criticality_rationale: Missing precedence rules let wrong source govern financial facts.
issue_note: Overlaps Section 04 Source Authority Register obligation; should cross-reference rather than define separately.

requirement_text: Define calculation inputs, outputs, versions and invariants.
criticality_rationale: Undefined calculation versions/invariants block reproducibility.

requirement_text: Create tests for financial classification, reconciliation, state transitions, currency/unit handling, margin views, retention/DLP relationships, carrying-cost calculations and double-counting.
criticality_rationale: Missing tests leave double-counting and margin-view defects undetected before release.

requirement_text: Record unresolved decisions in a domain-model decision register.
criticality_rationale: Unrecorded decisions become silent assumptions.

requirement_text: Preserve backward compatibility or document and test approved migrations.
criticality_rationale: Untested migrations can corrupt or lose existing financial records.

requirement_text: Submit the model and test evidence for independent review before treating it as implemented.
criticality_rationale: Skipping independent review risks treating model as implemented without evidence.

requirement_text: This section does not override the Section 01 discovery freeze. Production implementation remains subject to the required discovery sign-off.
criticality_rationale: Bypassing discovery freeze starts production work without signed-off evidence.
issue_note: Restates Section 01 implementation freeze; governance precedence statement rather than process step.

requirement_text: Check that every financial category is clearly distinguished.
criticality_rationale: Audit check on category distinction; detection aid only.

requirement_text: Check that the domain hierarchy supports Section 02 requirements.
criticality_rationale: Audit coverage of Section 02 support; detection aid.

requirement_text: Verify traceability of source facts and derived values.
criticality_rationale: Audit of traceability; missed gaps reduce assurance.
issue_note: Uses "Verify" in an audit instruction; scope of traceability check unspecified.

requirement_text: Test whether duplicate representations could create duplicate financial impacts.
criticality_rationale: Missed duplicate-impact probe lets double counting reach release.

requirement_text: Check that material comparisons use comparable specifications and units.
criticality_rationale: Audit check on material comparability.

requirement_text: Check separation of commitments, invoices, actual costs and payments.
criticality_rationale: Missed commitment/invoice separation check risks double-counted costs reaching release.

requirement_text: Check retention/security/DLP relationships and ensure withheld balances are not treated as losses.
criticality_rationale: Missed check risks withheld balances being reported as losses.

requirement_text: Review carrying-cost assumptions, time windows and rate provenance.
criticality_rationale: Audit review of carrying-cost assumptions.

requirement_text: Check currency, tax, time and conversion assumptions.
criticality_rationale: Audit review of currency/tax/time assumptions.

requirement_text: Review state transitions, approval requirements and history preservation.
criticality_rationale: Missed approval-requirement review risks unauthorised consequential transitions.

requirement_text: Check separation of deterministic arithmetic from AI inference.
criticality_rationale: Missed AI/deterministic separation check risks AI output becoming authoritative.

requirement_text: Compare proposed implementation with verified Anchor platform contracts.
criticality_rationale: Audit comparison with platform contracts.

requirement_text: Identify missing tests for critical invariants.
criticality_rationale: Untested critical invariants could pass the release gate.

requirement_text: Unsupported financial conventions, ambiguous relationships and untested critical invariants must be recorded as audit findings.
criticality_rationale: Unrecorded audit findings hide unsupported conventions from release decision.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-01: A source cannot update a material authoritative field unless an approved field-level source authority rule exists.
criticality_rationale: Gate on field-level authority before authoritative updates.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-02: Authority rules support different sources governing different fields and are versioned and auditable.
criticality_rationale: Gate on field-specific, versioned authority rules.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-03: Conflicting material financial records are excluded from authoritative calculations until resolved.
criticality_rationale: Gate excluding conflicting records from authoritative calculations.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-04: Quarantined records remain available to authorised reviewers without silently changing authoritative figures.
criticality_rationale: Gate on quarantine visibility without silent authoritative change.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-05: Provisional analysis is explicitly labelled and traceable to its unverified inputs and assumptions.
criticality_rationale: Gate on labelled, traceable provisional analysis.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-06: Promotion to authoritative state requires documented resolution and required approval.
criticality_rationale: Gate on controlled promotion to authoritative state.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-07: Material AI/OCR-extracted values cannot become authoritative before authorised human verification.
criticality_rationale: Gate on human verification of material extracted values.
issue_note: Inherits undefined materiality threshold from PGR-04-N022.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-08: Duplicate deliveries, retries and replay do not duplicate financial effects or downstream side effects.
criticality_rationale: Gate against duplicate financial and downstream effects.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-09: Revisions, credits, cancellations and replacements preserve lineage and are not mistaken for duplicate deliveries.
criticality_rationale: Gate ensuring legitimate credits/revisions are not discarded as duplicates.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-10: Currency, unit, tax, date and landed-cost transformations are explicit, versioned and reproducible.
criticality_rationale: Gate on reproducible normalisation transformations.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-11: Missing critical values are not silently invented or defaulted.
criticality_rationale: Gate against invented or defaulted critical values.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-12: Entity matching does not force uncertain matches merely to clear a queue.
criticality_rationale: Gate against forced uncertain matches.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-13: Freshness and completeness are visible and influence decision eligibility.
criticality_rationale: Gate on freshness visibility and decision eligibility.
issue_note: Decision eligibility depends on freshness thresholds not specified in Section 04 (deferred to policy; see PGR-16-N012).

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-14: Tenant isolation is tested across ingestion, staging, queues, quarantine, replay and downstream publication.
criticality_rationale: Gate on tenant-isolation testing across async paths.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-15: Audit records trace the source through validation, reconciliation, authority decision and canonical outcome.
criticality_rationale: Gate on end-to-end audit traceability.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-16: The implementation maps to existing Anchor/AUIF contracts identified during Section 01 discovery.
criticality_rationale: Gate on mapping to discovered platform contracts.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-17: Tests cover out-of-order events, partial batches, upstream corrections, stale data, conflicting sources and replay.
criticality_rationale: Gate on failure-path test coverage.

requirement_text: PG-DI-AC-18: The baseline test and evidence reports distinguish specification acceptance from proof of live implementation.
criticality_rationale: Gate preventing specification acceptance being reported as live proof.

requirement_text: Approved field-level Source Authority Register
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-04-1

requirement_text: Quarantine with controlled, labelled provisional visibility and no silent promotion
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-04-2

requirement_text: Authorised human verification of materially consequential AI-extracted values
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-04-3

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED after review of Draft v0.1 and independent audit. This document specifies required behaviour; it does not assert that the live repository, integrations, database, or production system already implements or satisfies these requirements.
criticality_rationale: Evidence boundary prevents treating specification as implemented.

requirement_text: Section 04 v1.0 is locked as the approved Data Ingestion, Normalisation & Reconciliation specification. The independent audit decisions are incorporated as mandatory requirements: (1) approved field-level Source Authority Register; (2) quarantine with controlled, labelled provisional visibility and no silent promotion; and (3) authorised human verification of materially consequential AI-extracted values.
criticality_rationale: Records lock decisions; behaviours enforced by N008, N016, N022.

requirement_text: This lock approves the specification baseline only. It is not a declaration that connectors, source registers, quarantine controls, verification workflows, tenant isolation or any other live implementation has been built, tested, deployed or accepted. Evidence must be produced through the Section 01 discovery gate and Section 14 verification process.
criticality_rationale: Evidence boundary prevents treating lock as implementation proof.
issue_note: Repeats front-matter evidence boundary.

requirement_text: Next section in sequence: Section 05 — Profitability Calculation Engine.
criticality_rationale: Sequence pointer to next section; no obligation.

requirement_text: Define the controls by which Anchor Profit Guardian receives, validates, normalises, reconciles and maintains data from construction and business systems. Successful transport or ingestion is not proof that a record is correct, reconciled, authoritative, or safe to use in authoritative financial calculations.
criticality_rationale: Treating ingestion success as correctness lets unverified data be trusted.

requirement_text: The pipeline must preserve source evidence and provenance, detect ambiguity and conflict, isolate unverified records, and publish governed canonical changes only when the applicable acceptance conditions are met.
criticality_rationale: Publishing unverified records corrupts authoritative canonical financial data.

requirement_text: 2. Source categories and scope
elements: Accounting and finance: posted invoices, credits, payments, receipts, journals and relevant account balances. ¶ Estimating, job costing and project controls: budgets, estimates, cost codes, forecasts and cost-to-complete inputs. ¶ Procurement and commitments: purchase orders, subcontract orders, amendments, supplier quotations and delivery commitments. ¶ Project management and scheduling: programme dates, activities, progress, dependencies, delay events and completion forecasts. ¶ Materials and inventory: demand, specifications, quantities, stock, substitutions, delivery records and material movements. ¶ Suppliers, subcontractors and trade compliance: identity, commercial terms, delivery/performance evidence, licences, insurance, safety accreditation and relevant statutory or industrial compliance evidence. ¶ Commercial management: contract values, claims, variations, notices, approvals, revenue events and disputed items. ¶ Quality and defects: inspections, non-conformances, rework, defect responsibility, rectification, completion and DLP evidence. ¶ Retentions and security: balances, release conditions, due dates, bank guarantees, bonds, expiry and release/cancellation evidence. ¶ Domestic and international market sources: prices, indices, exchange rates, freight, duties, lead times, availability and source-specific market observations. ¶ Manual uploads and documents: invoices, quotes, contracts, delivery dockets, spreadsheets, emails and approved forms.
criticality_rationale: Enumerates source categories; scope context without obligation.

requirement_text: These are source categories, not claims that connectors exist or are configured. Actual supported sources and contracts must be discovered and recorded under Section 01 before production integration work.
criticality_rationale: Integrating undiscovered sources bypasses the Section 01 gate.

requirement_text: The implementation must provide the following logical stages, mapping each stage to existing Anchor/AUIF conventions where available rather than inventing competing platform primitives:
elements: Source registration and connector authentication/authorisation. ¶ Receive and identify the source message, document, record or batch. ¶ Idempotency and duplicate checks. ¶ Transport/security and structural validation. ¶ Preserve the original source payload or durable evidence reference, source identifiers and provenance. ¶ Canonical mapping and normalisation with explicit units, currencies, tax treatment and time semantics. ¶ Entity matching and reconciliation against related records. ¶ Classify outcome as accepted, accepted with warnings, pending reconciliation, quarantined or rejected, subject to existing platform state conventions. ¶ Publish a governed canonical change and associated event only when allowed by the applicable rules. ¶ Record downstream processing status, errors, retries, replay and final disposition.
criticality_rationale: Missing pipeline stages allow records to bypass validation or reconciliation.

requirement_text: Maintain a source registry sufficient to identify, at minimum:
elements: Source system/provider, tenant and organisation scope, connector identity and environment. ¶ Data domains and fields supplied, expected direction of flow and source identifiers. ¶ Authentication method, permissions, secret-handling requirements and rotation/expiry controls. ¶ Transport mode, expected cadence, pagination/batch behaviour, rate limits and documented freshness. ¶ Schema/version information, mapping version and effective dates. ¶ Idempotency keys, duplicate policy, retry policy, backoff, dead-letter/error handling and replay capability. ¶ Known limitations, reliability characteristics, source authority by field, owner and escalation contact. ¶ Last successful receipt, last successful reconciliation, lag, error state and operational health.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete registry weakens connector operations and freshness tracking.

requirement_text: Connector implementation must use discovered Anchor Engine, Governor and AUIF contracts where appropriate. No implementation may assume that a connector, webhook, queue, event type or integration endpoint already exists without repository or environment evidence.
criticality_rationale: Assuming non-existent connectors causes false integration claims.

clause: 5. Source authority register — mandatory field-level precedence
requirement_text: Before a source can update an authoritative financial or contractual fact, a formally approved Source Authority Register must define which source governs each material field or fact type. A system may be authoritative for one fact and merely informational for another. A single global ranking of systems is insufficient.
criticality_rationale: Without field-level authority, wrong sources overwrite authoritative financial facts.

clause: 5. Source authority register — mandatory field-level precedence
requirement_text: 5. Source authority register — mandatory field-level precedence
elements: Record the field/fact, domain/entity, authoritative source, permitted secondary sources, precedence rule, effective period, owner, evidence basis and approval history. ¶ Define how revisions, cancellations, late-arriving records and corrections are handled. ¶ Define whether a field is source-owned, derived deterministically, human-approved, or provisional. ¶ Define conflict outcomes and the role authorised to resolve each material conflict. ¶ Use field-level precedence where appropriate—for example, posted actual payments may be governed by an accounting source while purchase commitments may be governed by procurement or job-costing records and programme dates by the approved scheduling source. These examples are illustrative and must be confirmed during discovery. ¶ Do not treat the newest timestamp as automatically correct; apply source authority, revision lineage, effective dates and reconciliation evidence. ¶ Changes to the register must be versioned, approved and auditable. Historical records must retain the authority/mapping version used at the time.
criticality_rationale: Recency-wins or unversioned authority rules corrupt facts and audit history.

clause: 5. Source authority register — mandatory field-level precedence
requirement_text: No record may become authoritative merely because it arrived from a recognised connector. If no approved authority rule exists for a material field, route it to controlled reconciliation or provisional use rather than silently selecting a source.
criticality_rationale: Records becoming authoritative by connector alone corrupt financial figures.

requirement_text: 6. Authentication, authorisation and source trust
elements: Authenticate sources and authorise access using least privilege and tenant-scoped permissions. ¶ Validate tenant, organisation, project and entity scope on every ingestion path, including asynchronous workers, retries, replay, manual uploads, storage and derived events. ¶ Do not trust payload-supplied tenant or organisation identifiers without validating them against the authenticated integration context and permitted mapping. ¶ Record the source identity and trust level; trust must be field/domain-specific rather than a blanket assumption that all content from a system is correct. ¶ Protect secrets and sensitive payloads according to discovered platform security and retention conventions.
criticality_rationale: Trusting payload tenant identifiers enables cross-tenant data exposure.

requirement_text: Design ingestion to tolerate duplicate delivery and retries without creating duplicate authoritative financial effects. Use stable source identifiers and idempotency keys where available; where unavailable, use a documented composite identity and ambiguity policy. Do not claim exactly-once delivery unless it is demonstrably guaranteed by the actual end-to-end design.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate delivery creating duplicate financial effects inflates authoritative totals.

requirement_text: 7. Idempotency, duplicates and delivery semantics
elements: Distinguish a duplicate delivery of the same source revision from a legitimate revision, reversal, credit or repeated commercial event. ¶ Retain lineage between originals, revisions, cancellations and replacements. ¶ Ensure retry and replay do not duplicate canonical changes, financial totals, alerts or downstream side effects. ¶ Send unresolvable duplicate candidates to reconciliation rather than guessing.
criticality_rationale: Replay/retry duplicates or lost lineage corrupt totals and trigger repeated side effects.

requirement_text: 8. Validation layers and outcomes
elements: Transport/security validation: authentication, authorisation, tenant scope, payload integrity and permitted size/type. ¶ Structural validation: schema, required fields, data types, identifier formats and supported versions. ¶ Semantic validation: units, currencies, sign conventions, dates, tax fields, project/entity scope and domain constraints. ¶ Reconciliation validation: relationships and consistency with purchase orders, invoices, credits, contracts, variations, payment records, programme versions, retentions and other relevant evidence. ¶ Outcome classification: accepted; accepted with warnings; pending reconciliation; quarantined; rejected. Map these to existing platform conventions after discovery.
criticality_rationale: Missing validation layers let malformed or mis-scoped records progress.

requirement_text: Quarantine is mandatory where a record is materially ambiguous, conflicting, suspicious, incomplete, or fails a control that prevents safe authoritative use. A rejection is appropriate where the record is invalid or impermissible and cannot safely proceed. Warnings must be explicit and must not disguise a blocking failure.
criticality_rationale: Failing to quarantine conflicting records lets them reach authoritative calculations.
issue_note: "Materially ambiguous" and "suspicious" lack defined thresholds or criteria.

clause: 9. Quarantine versus provisional use — mandatory isolation
requirement_text: Ambiguous or conflicting financial records must be excluded from authoritative financial calculations. They must remain visible to authorised reviewers in a controlled investigation/reconciliation workflow. Where useful, the system may expose sandboxed provisional analysis, provided that it is clearly labelled, traceable to unverified inputs and technically prevented from silently replacing authoritative figures.
criticality_rationale: Conflicting records in authoritative calculations produce wrong financial figures.

clause: 9. Quarantine versus provisional use — mandatory isolation
requirement_text: 9. Quarantine versus provisional use — mandatory isolation
elements: Authoritative views must never silently consume quarantined or provisional records. ¶ Provisional views must identify the affected figures, unverified records, unresolved conflicts, assumptions and relevant timestamps. ¶ Users must be able to compare authoritative and provisional outcomes without confusing their status. ¶ Promotion from quarantine/provisional to authoritative requires resolution of the blocking issue, required approvals, and a recorded disposition. ¶ A reviewer must be able to accept, correct, reject, merge or retain a conflict for further investigation where permitted by role and workflow. ¶ Promotion must not create duplicate financial effects or erase the original source evidence and previous decisions.
criticality_rationale: Silent consumption or unapproved promotion of provisional data corrupts authoritative figures.

requirement_text: 10. Canonical mapping and normalisation
elements: Preserve original source values and a durable reference to original evidence alongside normalised values. ¶ Record mapping rule/version and transformations applied; retain enough information to reproduce the normalised result. ¶ Normalise currencies, units, quantities, dates/time zones, tax treatment, rounding and sign conventions using explicit, versioned rules. ¶ Keep source currency and amount distinct from converted currency and amount; record exchange-rate source, timestamp/effective date and conversion method. ¶ Keep quoted unit price, freight, insurance, duties, taxes, handling, rebates/credits and other landed-cost components separate where relevant. ¶ Do not invent missing values or silently substitute defaults. Missing critical inputs must be marked and routed according to severity. ¶ Avoid destructive normalisation: the source representation must remain available for audit and dispute resolution.
criticality_rationale: Invented defaults or destructive normalisation corrupt figures and evidence.

requirement_text: Resolve incoming records against canonical projects, organisations, suppliers, subcontractors, contracts, purchase orders, invoices, variations, materials, schedule activities, defects, retention/security instruments and other relevant entities. Matching may use stable IDs, approved cross-reference tables and documented composite rules. Confidence alone must not authorise a material financial merge.
criticality_rationale: Confidence-only merges corrupt authoritative financial records.

requirement_text: 11. Entity resolution and reconciliation
elements: Invoice-to-PO matching, including partial invoices, multiple deliveries, price/quantity variance and unapproved changes. ¶ Credits, reversals, replacement invoices and amended purchase orders, preserving lineage. ¶ Invoice received before its PO or commitment is visible: do not discard it or fabricate a match; hold and reconcile under policy. ¶ Supplier aliases, legal-entity differences, project/cost-code mismatches and duplicate candidates. ¶ Retention amount/rate conflicts, security expiry/release discrepancies and DLP/defect links. ¶ Programme revision conflicts and late-arriving progress or delay evidence. ¶ Material specification, grade, unit, quantity and substitution mismatches. ¶ Partial, missing or inconsistent records where reconciliation cannot be completed automatically.
criticality_rationale: Unhandled reconciliation scenarios leave mismatches undetected.

requirement_text: Reconciliation outcomes must be explicit and auditable. The system must distinguish a genuine mismatch from a known timing difference and must not force a match simply to clear an exception queue.
criticality_rationale: Forced matches to clear queues corrupt authoritative reconciliations.

clause: 12. AI-extracted documents — mandatory human verification for material facts
requirement_text: AI/OCR-extracted values from invoices, contracts, supplier quotations, delivery dockets and other documents must not become authoritative where they materially affect financial calculations or contractual decisions until an authorised human verifies them. This is a non-negotiable control.
criticality_rationale: Unverified AI-extracted values becoming authoritative corrupt financial facts.
issue_note: Materiality threshold ("materially affect") undefined; non-material path depends on a separately defined policy.

clause: 12. AI-extracted documents — mandatory human verification for material facts
requirement_text: 12. AI-extracted documents — mandatory human verification for material facts
elements: Retain the original document or evidence reference, extraction output, model/tool version where available, extraction timestamp and confidence/uncertainty indicators. ¶ Identify extracted fields, page/region or source location where supported, and any unresolved ambiguity. ¶ Require verification for material values such as amounts, quantities, rates, tax, dates, contractual terms, retention provisions, payment conditions, specifications and variations. ¶ Do not use model confidence alone as a substitute for human verification of material facts. ¶ Keep unverified extracted values in quarantine or clearly labelled provisional analysis. ¶ Record reviewer identity, timestamp, value confirmed or corrected, evidence considered and disposition. ¶ Non-material extraction may follow a separately defined risk-based policy, but may not bypass other validation, authority or reconciliation controls.
criticality_rationale: Missing extraction evidence or verification records breaks audit integrity.

requirement_text: 13. Source revisions, conflicts and corrections
elements: Maintain source revision/version, received time, effective time where available, and relationship to superseded/corrected records. ¶ Apply the approved field-level Source Authority Register and do not resolve conflict using recency alone. ¶ Preserve prior values and decisions in the audit trail; corrections must be represented as governed changes rather than silent overwrites. ¶ Route unresolved material conflicts to authorised review and prevent them from changing authoritative financial views. ¶ Define a documented correction/replay path when an upstream source corrects a previously accepted record.
criticality_rationale: Silent overwrites or recency-based conflict resolution corrupt authoritative history.

requirement_text: Track freshness and completeness by source, project, domain and decision use. A source can be technically connected but too stale or incomplete for a particular recommendation.
criticality_rationale: Untracked freshness lets stale data drive recommendations.

requirement_text: 14. Freshness, completeness and data quality
elements: Record expected update cadence, last receipt, last successful processing, last reconciliation and current lag. ¶ Define decision-aware freshness thresholds—for example, a market quote may require a tighter freshness window than a historical posted transaction. ¶ Expose stale, missing, partial and degraded-source states to users and downstream intelligence. ¶ Suppress, qualify or downgrade recommendations when required inputs are stale or missing; do not imply real-time knowledge without evidence. ¶ Keep data-quality warnings visible and traceable to the affected calculation or recommendation.
criticality_rationale: Stale inputs produce unqualified recommendations.

requirement_text: 15. Events, retries, backfill and replay
elements: Use existing Anchor event, workflow and state conventions discovered under Section 01. ¶ Record processing state and correlation identifiers across ingestion, reconciliation, canonical update and downstream consumers. ¶ Use bounded retry/backoff and defined terminal handling; avoid infinite retries and silent data loss. ¶ Make replay/backfill idempotent and version-aware. Define whether replay recomputes derived values and how changes are surfaced. ¶ Prevent stale or out-of-order events from reverting a newer valid state without an explicit, governed correction path. ¶ Make partial batch success/failure visible at record level where feasible.
criticality_rationale: Out-of-order events reverting valid state or unbounded retries corrupt data.

requirement_text: Tenant isolation applies to the full data lifecycle: credentials, connector configuration, inbound payloads, object storage, staging, queues, workers, quarantine, reconciliation, canonical records, events, logs, caches, search/indexing, exports, replay and backups where applicable. Isolation must be verified in the actual architecture; a UI-only check is insufficient.
criticality_rationale: Isolation gaps anywhere in the lifecycle expose cross-tenant data.

requirement_text: A demonstrated tenant-isolation defect blocks release of Profit Guardian into any environment that exposes the vulnerable boundary. It does not automatically require unrelated services to be halted if they do not expose that boundary. Follow Section 01's discovery and release-gate rule.
criticality_rationale: Releasing despite isolation defect exposes cross-tenant data.
issue_note: Restates Section 01 Gate 01-B release rule.

requirement_text: Maintain a traceable chain from source receipt to final disposition, including as applicable:
elements: Source, tenant, organisation, project and source record identifiers. ¶ Receipt time, source/effective time, payload hash or durable evidence reference, and schema/mapping versions. ¶ Validation results, warnings, duplicate decisions, entity matches and reconciliation status. ¶ Authority rule applied and relevant register version. ¶ Quarantine reason, reviewer actions, corrections, approvals and final disposition. ¶ Canonical changes/events produced, downstream processing results and retry/replay history. ¶ Errors, latency, backlog, freshness, failure rates and operational alerts.
criticality_rationale: Broken source-to-disposition chain loses audit and evidence integrity.

requirement_text: Logs must avoid unnecessary sensitive payload exposure and must follow the discovered platform's access, retention and redaction controls.
criticality_rationale: Logs exposing sensitive payloads create data-exposure risk.

requirement_text: 18. Manual uploads and controlled entry
elements: Manual uploads must pass the same tenant, schema, validation, provenance, reconciliation and authority controls as connector data. ¶ Record uploader, upload time, source description, project scope, file identity/hash where feasible, and any manual transformations. ¶ Apply file-type, size, malware and content-handling controls according to platform security standards. ¶ Spreadsheet imports must define column mapping, units, currency, date interpretation, duplicate policy and row-level error reporting. ¶ Manual entry must not be a bypass around approval or audit requirements.
criticality_rationale: Manual entry bypassing controls lets unapproved figures become authoritative.

requirement_text: Do not begin production feature code or core integration logic until Section 01's Discovery Exit Report is signed off.
criticality_rationale: Starting production code before discovery sign-off bypasses the Section 01 gate.
issue_note: Restates Section 01 implementation freeze.

requirement_text: Inspect the actual repository and map existing Anchor Engine, Governor, AUIF, tenant, state, event, audit and integration contracts before choosing implementation patterns.
criticality_rationale: Unmapped contracts lead to competing primitives; gates implementation choices.

requirement_text: Produce a Source Authority Register, source/connector inventory, canonical mapping register, reconciliation rules, quarantine policy and data-quality/freshness policy.
criticality_rationale: Missing registers/policies leave mandatory controls unimplementable; gates release.

requirement_text: Implement field-level authority, quarantine/provisional isolation and human verification of material AI-extracted facts as mandatory controls.
criticality_rationale: Mandatory controls not implemented leave authoritative data unprotected.
issue_note: Restates the three lock-mandated controls (N008, N016, N022).

requirement_text: Add unit, integration, tenant-isolation, idempotency, replay, mutation/regression and failure-path tests appropriate to the discovered architecture.
criticality_rationale: Missing failure-path tests leave idempotency and isolation defects undetected.

requirement_text: Document every unavailable external source, credential, database or environment and add blocked closure items to the DB-Dependent Closure Register where applicable.
criticality_rationale: Undocumented blockers obscure closure status.

requirement_text: Do not claim an integration, security control or acceptance criterion passed without reproducible evidence.
criticality_rationale: Claiming passed controls without evidence is a false verified status.

requirement_text: Audit this section as a specification against the Section 01 discovery evidence and actual implementation evidence when available. Do not infer implementation from the presence of requirements or code names alone.
criticality_rationale: Auditing from code names alone produces false assurance.

requirement_text: Challenge completeness of field-level authority and conflict rules.
criticality_rationale: Unchallenged authority gaps let wrong sources govern facts.

requirement_text: Attempt to demonstrate that quarantined/provisional data can leak into authoritative calculations.
criticality_rationale: Missed leakage probe lets provisional data contaminate authoritative figures.

requirement_text: Test whether AI-extracted material values can be promoted without human verification.
criticality_rationale: Missed probe lets unverified AI values be promoted.

requirement_text: Probe duplicate delivery, retry, out-of-order events, revisions, credits, replay and partial batch handling.
criticality_rationale: Missed probes leave duplicate/replay defects before release.

requirement_text: Test tenant isolation across all ingestion surfaces and asynchronous paths.
criticality_rationale: Missed probe leaves cross-tenant exposure undetected.

requirement_text: Inspect source-to-canonical provenance, reproducibility of normalisation and audit completeness.
criticality_rationale: Audit of provenance and reproducibility; detection aid.

requirement_text: Report each finding with severity, evidence, reproducible steps, affected requirement, remediation and retest result.
criticality_rationale: Finding report format; affects remediation tracking.

requirement_text: Separate specification gaps, implementation defects, missing evidence and environment/access blockers.
criticality_rationale: Finding categorisation; affects remediation clarity.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-01: Recognised margin, forecast final margin and cash-position-adjusted margin remain distinct.
criticality_rationale: Interchangeable margin views would report wrong authoritative margin.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-02: Actuals, commitments, accruals, forecasts, exposures, opportunities and realised benefits are not conflated.
criticality_rationale: Conflated financial states produce wrong authoritative figures.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-03: One authoritative forecast exists for each defined project/scope/as-of state; scenarios and historical versions are isolated.
criticality_rationale: Multiple active or contaminated forecasts produce conflicting authoritative figures.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-04: Missing/stale material inputs yield an explicitly qualified forecast, with gaps and supported impact information exposed.
criticality_rationale: Unqualified forecasts from stale inputs mislead decisions.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-05: An invoice-to-PO transition does not double-count cost.
criticality_rationale: Double-counted invoice and PO cost misstates actual cost.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-06: Credits, reversals and revisions adjust prior values correctly and preserve lineage.
criticality_rationale: Wrong credit/reversal handling misstates authoritative values and lineage.
issue_note: "Adjust prior values correctly" lacks a stated rule (restate vs. offsetting entry).

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-07: Forecast cost-to-complete components reconcile to the total.
criticality_rationale: Components not reconciling to total gives wrong forecast final cost.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-08: Forecast movement bridges reconcile to forecast version changes, with unexplained movements surfaced.
criticality_rationale: Non-reconciling bridges hide unexplained forecast movement.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-09: Unapproved/disputed revenue is not silently treated as secured revenue.
criticality_rationale: Unapproved revenue treated as secured overstates margin.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-10: Holding costs use explicit rates and eligible durations and avoid overlap.
criticality_rationale: Overlapping or unevidenced holding costs inflate exposure estimates.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-11: Retention/security face values remain separate from carrying costs; linked defect impacts are not double-counted.
criticality_rationale: Face value as loss or double-counted defects misstate profit.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-12: Scenario calculations cannot silently alter authoritative financial views.
criticality_rationale: Scenarios altering authoritative views corrupt official figures.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-13: Realised net benefit requires an approved baseline, implementation evidence and authorised verification.
criticality_rationale: Realised benefit without verification is a false realised claim.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-14: Currency, units, tax and rounding rules are reproducible.
criticality_rationale: Irreproducible currency/tax/rounding yields inconsistent monetary figures.
issue_note: Checks reproducibility only; does not check decimal-safe arithmetic or explainable rounding differences required by PGR-05-N039.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-15: Zero denominators and missing inputs produce explicit qualified outcomes.
criticality_rationale: Silent handling of zero denominators/missing inputs yields unqualified outputs.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-16: Every material calculation preserves formula version and immutable input snapshot/references sufficient for historical reconstruction.
criticality_rationale: Missing snapshots/versions prevent reconstruction of reported results.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-17: Historical results can be reproduced after source records or calculation rules change.
criticality_rationale: Non-reproducible history destroys audit integrity of reported figures.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-18: Input changes, rule changes and corrections are distinguishable.
criticality_rationale: Indistinguishable change causes weaken audit explanation of result changes.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-19: Tests cover boundary values, reversals, incomplete inputs, overlapping exposures, concurrency and replay.
criticality_rationale: Missing edge-case tests leave defects undetected before release gate.
issue_note: No coverage depth or pass threshold; "concurrency" has no stated concurrency requirement beyond the single-active-forecast invariant.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-20: Provenance allows a reviewer to reconstruct a material result.
criticality_rationale: Unreconstructable material results break audit and evidence integrity.

requirement_text: PG-PC-AC-21: No acceptance claim is made without reproducible test evidence and a clear scope.
criticality_rationale: Acceptance claimed without reproducible evidence is a false verified status.
issue_note: Reclassified: evidence/claim governance rule rather than a criterion checking a body requirement.

requirement_text: One formally approved authoritative forecast with isolated scenarios and preserved history
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-05-1

requirement_text: Provisional/qualified forecasts when material inputs are missing or stale, with gaps and supported impact information exposed
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-05-2

requirement_text: Realised net profit improvement requires an approved baseline, implementation evidence and authorised verification
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-05-3

requirement_text: Every material calculation preserves its formula/rule version and immutable input snapshot or equivalent immutable references
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-05-4

requirement_text: This is a separate management view connecting profitability with liquidity constraints and capital tied up in the project. It may consider overdue receivables, disputed variations, retention timing, security instruments, supplier obligations, financing/working-capital costs and timing differences between profit recognition and cash movement.
criticality_rationale: Defines cash-position-adjusted margin scope; PGR-05-N012 relies on it without the definition.
row_origin: Promoted from INFO anchor S05 order 39

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED following independent audit. This is a normative specification, not evidence that the live repository or production system implements or passes these requirements.
criticality_rationale: Status disclaimer; misreading only affects documentation of implementation status.

requirement_text: Section 05 v1.0 is locked after independent review. Four audited decisions are mandatory: (1) one formally approved authoritative forecast with isolated scenarios and preserved history; (2) provisional/qualified forecasts when material inputs are missing or stale, with gaps and supported impact information exposed; (3) realised net profit improvement requires an approved baseline, implementation evidence and authorised verification; and (4) every material calculation preserves its formula/rule version and immutable input snapshot or equivalent immutable references.
criticality_rationale: Lock record of mandatory decisions; content enforced by body rows.

requirement_text: This lock approves the specification baseline only. It does not claim that the live repository, database, calculation engine, forecast controls, benefit verification or historical reconstruction has been implemented or passed. Evidence must be produced through Section 01 discovery and Section 14 verification.
criticality_rationale: Treating lock as implementation evidence would falsely claim verified status.

requirement_text: Next section: Section 06 — Active Intelligence & Profit Leakage Detection.
criticality_rationale: Navigation pointer only; no obligation.
issue_note: Reclassified: navigation text, not a requirement.

requirement_text: The Profitability Calculation Engine is the deterministic financial core of Anchor Profit Guardian. It converts validated, reconciled and appropriately authoritative project data into reproducible financial measures. It must show current financial position, defensible forecast final profitability, profit at risk, potential opportunities and evidence required to verify improvement.
criticality_rationale: Missing core measures (position, forecast, profit at risk) degrades all downstream decisions.

requirement_text: The engine calculates outcomes; it must not manufacture certainty. Results are bounded by validated inputs, approved rules, accounting treatment and explicit assumptions.
criticality_rationale: Results presented with false certainty mislead decisions on unqualified outputs.
issue_note: Principle only; "must not manufacture certainty" is testable only through PGR-05-N017/N020/N021.

requirement_text: 2. Governing design principles
elements: Deterministic arithmetic: identical inputs, calculation rules and versions produce identical outputs. ¶ Explicit financial semantics: actuals, commitments, forecasts, exposures and opportunities remain separate. ¶ No silent overrides: AI and dashboards cannot silently alter authoritative calculations. ¶ Reproducibility: material results trace to inputs, methods, versions and timestamps. ¶ Temporal correctness: distinguish transaction, effective, posting, forecast and calculation-as-of times. ¶ No double counting: linked exposures, savings, costs and recoveries must be consolidated correctly. ¶ Uncertainty remains visible: incomplete or stale evidence qualifies the result. ¶ Recognised margin, forecast final margin and cash-position-adjusted margin are never interchangeable.
criticality_rationale: Non-deterministic arithmetic, silent overrides or double counting corrupt authoritative figures.
issue_note: "Consolidated correctly" and "material results" lack objective criteria in this principle list; specific rows carry the testable content.

requirement_text: Recognised Margin = Recognised Revenue − Recognised Costs.
criticality_rationale: Wrong recognised-margin formula produces wrong authoritative financial figures.

requirement_text: Recognised Margin % = Recognised Margin ÷ Recognised Revenue × 100. If the denominator is zero, return an explicit not-applicable or equivalent state; do not invent a percentage.
criticality_rationale: Invented percentage on zero revenue yields a false authoritative margin figure.

requirement_text: 3.1 Recognised margin
elements: Respect approved revenue and cost recognition policy and reporting period. ¶ Separate posted transactions from unposted estimates and forecasts. ¶ Identify accounting period and calculation cut-off. ¶ Reconcile to relevant accounting records where available. ¶ Preserve adjustments, reversals, credits and restatements. ¶ Do not equate cash received/paid with revenue/cost recognised.
criticality_rationale: Mixing cash with recognition or unposted estimates misstates recognised margin.

requirement_text: Forecast Final Margin = Forecast Final Revenue − Forecast Final Cost.
criticality_rationale: Wrong forecast final margin formula misstates authoritative forecast profitability.

requirement_text: Where supported by the project's approved model, Forecast Final Cost = Cost Recognised to Date + Forecast Cost to Complete. The decomposition must prevent overlap between recognised costs, commitments and cost-to-complete.
criticality_rationale: Overlap between recognised cost, commitments and cost-to-complete double-counts forecast cost.
issue_note: Fallback when the approved project model does not support the decomposition is not stated.

requirement_text: 3.2 Forecast final margin
elements: Distinguish approved contract revenue, approved variations, submitted/unresolved claims, disputed revenue, speculative revenue and scenario-only revenue. ¶ Distinguish actuals, commitments, accruals, remaining work, risk allowances and scenario-only costs. ¶ Do not silently treat unapproved variations, disputed claims or speculative recoveries as secured revenue. ¶ A commitment is not automatically an additional cost on top of a forecast; determine whether it is already represented.
criticality_rationale: Treating disputed/speculative revenue as secured overstates forecast margin.

requirement_text: For comparable scope and basis: Cost Variance = Approved Budget − Forecast Final Cost. Positive means forecast cost below budget; negative means forecast cost above budget.
criticality_rationale: Wrong sign convention or basis inverts reported cost variance.

requirement_text: Record budget baseline ID/version, scope, reporting period, currency, tax treatment, approved changes, effective dates, calculation timestamp and exclusions. Do not compare incompatible baselines without visible qualification.
criticality_rationale: Unqualified comparison of incompatible baselines produces misleading variance.

requirement_text: It must not be represented as statutory margin or treat every cash-flow exposure as an accounting expense. Show the underlying profitability measure and separate cash/capital adjustments.
criticality_rationale: Cash-adjusted view presented as statutory margin misstates financial position.

requirement_text: 4. Canonical calculation inputs
elements: Contract/revenue: approved, recognised, submitted, disputed and scenario-only amounts. ¶ Actual costs: validated authoritative transactions, reversals and corrections. ¶ Commitments: open, fulfilled, cancelled and amended commitments; avoid overlap with actuals and forecasts. ¶ Cost-to-complete: estimate basis, owner, date, assumptions, confidence and revisions. ¶ Accruals: period, basis, status and reconciliation to actuals. ¶ Variations/claims: approval state, value, evidence and overlap status. ¶ Schedule/productivity: financial effects only through explicit, evidenced rules. ¶ Material/procurement exposure: purchase price, expected future price, freight, duties, tax and other applicable costs. ¶ Retentions/security: face value and release conditions separate from incremental carrying cost. ¶ Defects/DLP: evidenced rectification and carrying impacts with linked exposure identities. ¶ Risks/opportunities: estimated exposure separate from booked costs, recognised revenue and realised savings.
criticality_rationale: Missing input state distinctions allow overlap and misclassification of costs and revenue.

requirement_text: Every material input must have source, status, effective date where available, provenance and applicable authority rule.
criticality_rationale: Inputs without provenance or authority break audit and evidence integrity.
issue_note: "Material input" has no materiality threshold anywhere in the blueprint, so the scope of the obligation is undefined.

requirement_text: Support a defensible forecast of remaining project cost. The precise algorithm must be selected after repository discovery and data assessment; no single formula is mandated for every trade or project.
criticality_rationale: Algorithm deferred to discovery; failure limits forecast defensibility rather than corrupting state.
issue_note: "Defensible forecast" has no pass/fail basis; algorithm selection is deferred with no acceptance criterion.

requirement_text: 5. Forecast cost-to-complete engine
elements: Remaining committed work. ¶ Remaining uncommitted scope. ¶ Expected labour and productivity costs. ¶ Material quantities and expected procurement costs. ¶ Plant, equipment, logistics and site overhead. ¶ Schedule-related holding costs. ¶ Quality, rework and defect rectification exposure. ¶ Approved changes and evidenced unresolved commercial exposures. ¶ Explicit risk allowances and scenario adjustments. ¶ Reconciliation of forecast changes against the prior forecast.
criticality_rationale: Omitted cost-to-complete components understate remaining cost and forecast exposure.
issue_note: Unclear whether every listed component is mandatory per project, given PGR-05-N015 says no single formula applies to all.

requirement_text: Each component must be classified as actual, committed, estimated, risk-adjusted or scenario-only. If inputs are insufficient, return a qualified/incomplete forecast rather than silently filling gaps.
criticality_rationale: Silently filled gaps produce a false complete forecast.

requirement_text: Each project must have one formally approved Authoritative Forecast for the applicable scope and as-of state. Alternative scenarios, draft forecasts and prior approved versions must remain separately identified and must not compete as simultaneous official forecasts.
criticality_rationale: Competing official forecasts produce conflicting authoritative figures.

requirement_text: 5.1 One authoritative forecast — mandatory
elements: Record the authorised forecast ID, version, approval status, owner, scope, as-of time and applicable calculation/rule versions. ¶ Preserve previous approved versions and the reason for each replacement. ¶ Scenario outputs must reference a base forecast but remain isolated until an authorised, auditable workflow approves a change. ¶ Enforce a single active authoritative forecast for the defined project/scope through the appropriate repository/database invariant where feasible; otherwise document the enforceable control and its limitations. ¶ Do not silently promote a scenario, draft or recalculation into the authoritative forecast.
criticality_rationale: Scenario or draft silently promoted becomes a false authoritative forecast.

requirement_text: Where material cost-to-complete inputs are missing, stale, incomplete or unresolved, the engine may calculate a provisional forecast to support operational decisions. The result must be marked qualified and expose missing components, stale sources, unresolved conflicts, assumptions and uncertainty/impact information where it can be reasonably supported.
criticality_rationale: Provisional forecast without qualification gives unqualified uncertain output.

requirement_text: 5.2 Provisional and qualified forecasts — mandatory
elements: Never silently present a qualified forecast as complete or authoritative. ¶ Display which values are evidenced, estimated, stale, missing or scenario-derived. ¶ Where a defensible numeric impact range cannot be calculated, state that limitation rather than inventing a range. ¶ Apply decision-aware freshness thresholds and downgrade or suppress dependent recommendations when necessary. ¶ Record how and when the forecast can be reconciled or upgraded.
criticality_rationale: Qualified forecast shown as complete/authoritative is a false authoritative state.

requirement_text: Every forecast revision must explain the change from its prior comparable version. Classify movements including newly recorded actuals, commitment changes, updated cost-to-complete estimates, quantity/productivity changes, procurement price changes, schedule/holding costs, approved commercial changes, newly identified risks/opportunities and corrections.
criticality_rationale: Unexplained forecast revisions hide leakage and mislead reviewers.

requirement_text: Classified movements must reconcile to the total forecast change, subject to explicitly identified rounding or unallocated differences. Unexplained movement must be surfaced.
criticality_rationale: Non-reconciling bridges hide unexplained forecast movement.

requirement_text: Avoid counting one economic cost in multiple financial states.
criticality_rationale: One cost counted in several states overstates cost and exposure.

requirement_text: 6. Cost commitment and actual-cost reconciliation
elements: When an invoice is posted against a purchase order, apply a documented transition so the invoiced portion is not counted both as actual cost and as an unreduced open commitment. ¶ Handle partial invoices/deliveries, PO amendments, credits/reversals, cancelled commitments, supplier retentions, accrual reconciliation, unapproved orders, disputes and ordered/delivered/invoiced/accepted quantity differences. ¶ Respect approved financial semantics and reconciliation state. ¶ Keep unresolved differences visible; do not force them into a clean-looking total.
criticality_rationale: Invoice and unreduced commitment double-count actual cost.

requirement_text: Each exposure must have a unique identity and documented relationships to related exposures. Record gross estimated amount, method/inputs, evidence, confidence/uncertainty, time window, currency, financial classification, overlap status, owner, review state and resolution outcome.
criticality_rationale: Exposures without identity/overlap status get double-counted or lost in prioritisation.

requirement_text: An estimated exposure is not automatically an incurred cost or recoverable entitlement.
criticality_rationale: Estimated exposure booked as incurred cost or entitlement misstates financial state.

requirement_text: A simplified calculation is Estimated Holding Cost = Applicable Cost Rate × Eligible Delay Duration. It is valid only where the rate and eligible duration are evidenced and the cost is incremental for the period.
criticality_rationale: Unevidenced rates or durations overstate holding-cost estimates.

requirement_text: Avoid treating every calendar day of delay as incremental cost where spending would have occurred anyway, activities overlap, or the cost is already included in the forecast. Distinguish estimated cost consequence from contractual entitlement or recoverability.
criticality_rationale: Counting non-incremental delay days inflates estimated holding cost.

requirement_text: Maintain separate values for retention principal withheld/receivable, expected release amount/timing, security instrument face value, expiry/renewal/release dates, incremental financing/carrying cost, defect rectification cost and disputed deductions/recoveries.
criticality_rationale: Conflated retention/security values mislead cash and carrying-cost views.

requirement_text: Illustrative simple carrying-cost formula: Carrying Cost = Eligible Tied-up Balance × Annual Rate × Eligible Days ÷ Day-count Basis. Record rate source, eligible balance, dates, day-count basis and method.
criticality_rationale: Carrying-cost method recording supports traceability; formula itself is illustrative.
issue_note: Formula labelled "illustrative" but recording obligations are mandatory; unclear whether this formula or an approved alternative is required.

requirement_text: Retention or bank-guarantee face value is not itself a profit loss. If an open defect delays retention release, link the relationship and calculate only distinct, evidence-supported consequences. Do not count defect cost twice.
criticality_rationale: Face value booked as loss or defect cost counted twice misstates profit.

requirement_text: 10. Profit improvement and realised-benefit accounting
elements: Maintain explicit states: identified opportunity; estimated gross benefit; estimated implementation cost; estimated net benefit; approved action; implemented; benefit observed; benefit verified; realised net benefit; reversed/invalidated/not realised. ¶ Estimated Net Benefit = Estimated Gross Benefit − Estimated Implementation Cost, adjusted for relevant incremental operating, financing, transition, quality, delay or other supported costs.
criticality_rationale: Missing benefit states allow estimates to be shown as realised benefit.
issue_note: Net-benefit formula paragraph captured as a list element of the states list. "Relevant ... supported costs" adjustment is open-ended.

requirement_text: A saving must not be claimed merely because a proposed price is below a historical quote. Require comparable baseline, scope/specification, quantity, timing, landed-cost treatment and outcome evidence.
criticality_rationale: Quote-below-history claimed as saving is a false realised-saving claim.

requirement_text: A benefit may be reported as realised net profit improvement only after (a) an approved, versioned baseline is established; (b) implementation evidence exists; and (c) an authorised verification step confirms the outcome against the baseline, including relevant offsetting or hidden costs. A negotiated price, quote, approved recommendation or forecast alone is not a realised saving.
criticality_rationale: Benefits reported realised without baseline/verification is a false realised claim.

requirement_text: Where work is not yet executed, invoiced or otherwise sufficiently reconciled to establish the outcome, retain the benefit in an appropriate non-realised state. The exact verification evidence may vary by benefit type but must be specified and auditable.
criticality_rationale: Unexecuted work shown as realised benefit falsely claims realisation.
issue_note: Verification evidence per benefit type "must be specified" but no specification location or owner is given.

requirement_text: Support buy-now/wait, domestic/international sourcing, exchange-rate/freight assumptions, delivery schedules, productivity, delay mitigation, defect rectification, retention timing and cost-to-complete scenarios.
criticality_rationale: Missing scenario types limit decision support; no authoritative state corrupted.

requirement_text: 11. Scenario calculations
elements: Preserve base-case reference and version. ¶ Record changed assumptions, rule version, input provenance/freshness, owner and creation time. ¶ Show gross/net effects, uncertainty and limitations. ¶ Keep scenario outputs isolated from authoritative actuals and approved forecasts unless an authorised workflow incorporates them.
criticality_rationale: Scenario outputs leaking into authoritative views corrupt actuals and approved forecasts.

clause: 12. Rounding, currency, tax and numerical integrity
requirement_text: 12. Rounding, currency, tax and numerical integrity
elements: Define decimal precision, currency-specific precision, rounding boundaries, unit conversion, tax treatment, exchange-rate source/effective date, percentages, allocations, negative amounts, credits and missing values. ¶ Use decimal-safe financial arithmetic and approved platform conventions; do not rely on uncontrolled binary floating-point arithmetic for authoritative monetary calculations. ¶ Retain adequate intermediate precision and document rounding boundaries. ¶ Make rounding differences explainable and test them. ¶ Treat zero denominators and missing inputs explicitly.
criticality_rationale: Binary floating point or undefined rounding produces wrong monetary figures.

clause: 13. Reproducibility and immutable calculation versioning — mandatory
requirement_text: Every material calculation must preserve its formula/rule version and an immutable input snapshot or equivalent immutable references sufficient to reconstruct the result after source records change. A pointer to a mutable current record alone is insufficient unless versioning guarantees the referenced historical state remains available.
criticality_rationale: Without immutable inputs and versions, historical results cannot be reconstructed.
issue_note: "Material calculation" is never defined; scope of mandatory immutable versioning is therefore indeterminate.
