clause: 13. Reproducibility and immutable calculation versioning — mandatory
requirement_text: 13. Reproducibility and immutable calculation versioning — mandatory
elements: Record calculation ID/type, project/entity/reporting period and as-of time. ¶ Preserve input record identities, immutable versions or snapshot references, source authority/reconciliation state and relevant source timestamps. ¶ Record formula/rule version, currency, units, tax and rounding policy, assumptions, exclusions and calculation timestamp. ¶ Record result, quality status, prior result/version, recalculation reason and downstream use. ¶ Distinguish changed inputs from changed rules and explicit corrections. ¶ Define retention, access and integrity controls for snapshots/references consistent with platform security and legal requirements. ¶ Verify historical replay/reconstruction using the recorded versions, without silently rewriting the originally reported result.
criticality_rationale: Missing calculation metadata breaks audit trail and replay integrity.

clause: 13. Reproducibility and immutable calculation versioning — mandatory
requirement_text: Historical results must not drift silently when an underlying record or formula changes.
criticality_rationale: Silently drifting historical results destroy audit integrity of reported figures.

requirement_text: Do not begin production feature code or core integration logic until Section 01 Discovery Exit Report is signed off.
criticality_rationale: Coding before discovery sign-off bypasses the phase gate.
issue_note: Restates the Section 01 implementation freeze; intentional cross-section repetition.

requirement_text: Map calculations to actual repository/canonical models and inspect existing financial arithmetic, aggregation, forecasting and audit mechanisms first.
criticality_rationale: Skipping repository mapping risks duplicate or inconsistent arithmetic mechanisms.

requirement_text: Produce a calculation catalogue listing each metric, formula, inputs, authority requirements, versioning rules and acceptance tests.
criticality_rationale: Missing calculation catalogue weakens traceability of metrics to tests.
issue_note: Reclassified: deliverable (calculation catalogue).

requirement_text: Separate deterministic financial calculations from AI interpretation and recommendations.
criticality_rationale: AI interpretation mixed into calculations risks unsanctioned changes to figures.

requirement_text: Implement one-authoritative-forecast control, qualified/provisional forecast states, realised-benefit verification and immutable calculation versioning as mandatory controls.
criticality_rationale: Mandatory controls not implemented blocks section acceptance.

requirement_text: Test arithmetic, financial state transitions, double counting, precision, historical reconstruction, replay and regression.
criticality_rationale: Untested state transitions and precision leave financial defects undetected before release.

requirement_text: Provide calculation-level evidence and requirement traceability.
criticality_rationale: Without calculation-level evidence acceptance gates lack inputs.
issue_note: Reclassified: evidence/deliverable obligation.

requirement_text: Record database, source, integration and policy blockers in the DB-Dependent Closure Register.
criticality_rationale: Unrecorded blockers hide incomplete closure status.

requirement_text: Do not claim production readiness solely from unit tests; include integration, reconciliation and regression evidence.
criticality_rationale: Readiness claimed from unit tests alone risks premature release.

requirement_text: Challenge semantic separation of the three financial views.
criticality_rationale: Unchallenged view separation lets margin conflation pass audit.
issue_note: "Challenge" gives no expected outcome or pass/fail condition.

requirement_text: Test actual/commitment reconciliation and forecast movement completeness.
criticality_rationale: Unaudited reconciliation lets double counting reach release.

requirement_text: Test that only one authoritative forecast is active for the defined scope and that scenarios cannot leak into it.
criticality_rationale: Unaudited forecast invariant lets competing forecasts reach release.

requirement_text: Test missing/stale input qualification and whether uncertainty is honestly presented.
criticality_rationale: Unaudited qualification lets unqualified stale outputs reach release.

requirement_text: Verify retention/security and DLP relationships without double-counting.
criticality_rationale: Unaudited retention/DLP linkage lets double counting reach release.

requirement_text: Attempt to promote benefits to realised without baseline, implementation evidence or verification.
criticality_rationale: Untested promotion path could allow false realised-benefit claims.

requirement_text: Test deterministic arithmetic, decimal precision, currency conversion, tax and rounding.
criticality_rationale: Unaudited arithmetic and rounding lets monetary defects reach release.

requirement_text: Reconstruct historical calculations from immutable inputs and formula versions after source/rule changes.
criticality_rationale: Unaudited replay lets reconstruction defects reach release.

requirement_text: Inspect provenance, edge-case coverage and whether tests detect deliberately introduced defects.
criticality_rationale: Weak test-suite sensitivity check reduces audit confidence.

requirement_text: Report specification gaps, implementation defects, missing evidence and access blockers separately.
criticality_rationale: Mixed finding categories obscure remediation ownership.

requirement_text: Each finding must include requirement, severity, evidence, reproducible test/counterexample, remediation and retest result.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete finding records hinder remediation and retest.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-01: Deterministic rules can be configured, versioned, executed and tested.
criticality_rationale: Untestable rules undermine deterministic baseline reliability.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-02: New/changed evidence triggers relevant re-evaluation.
criticality_rationale: Missing re-evaluation delays leakage detection.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-03: Scheduled reassessment identifies persistent/stale conditions.
criticality_rationale: Persistent conditions undetected without sweeps.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-04: Missing/unreliable data creates a qualification or data-quality finding.
criticality_rationale: Unflagged data gaps produce unqualified findings.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-05: Findings preserve provenance and rule/model version.
criticality_rationale: Findings without provenance/version break evidence integrity.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-06: Financial amounts use Section 05 calculations or are labelled estimates.
criticality_rationale: Unlabelled non-engine amounts present estimates as authoritative.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-07: Findings can exist without a defensible financial amount.
criticality_rationale: Forced amounts lead to invented figures on findings.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-08: Severity, urgency and confidence remain separate.
criticality_rationale: Merged dimensions misrepresent weak evidence as confirmed loss.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-09: Repeated detections update existing findings without duplicate alert spam; material changes support controlled reopening/notification.
criticality_rationale: Alert spam or missed renotification degrades review.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-10: Related findings link together while overlapping financial amounts are not blindly summed.
criticality_rationale: Blind summing of linked findings overstates exposure.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-11: Correlation is not presented as proven causation without evidence.
criticality_rationale: Correlation shown as causation misleads remedial action.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-12: AI claims are grounded or labelled as hypotheses.
criticality_rationale: Ungrounded AI claims mislead reviewers.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-13: Dismissal, deferral, confirmation, approval and resolution are auditable.
criticality_rationale: Non-auditable dispositions break audit integrity of decisions.
issue_note: Deferral is checked here but is not a status in the PGR-06-N018 finding contract.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-14: Consequential actions cannot bypass human approval.
criticality_rationale: Bypassed approval allows consequential external actions without humans.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-15: Opportunities can be detected when budgets are on track.
criticality_rationale: Opportunities missed when budgets look healthy.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-16: Opportunity estimates cannot be reported as realised savings without Section 05 verification.
criticality_rationale: Estimates reported as realised savings is a false realised claim.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-17: Portfolio intelligence respects tenant isolation and sharing permissions.
criticality_rationale: Portfolio leakage across tenants exposes client data.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-18: Failed monitoring runs and stale data are observable.
criticality_rationale: Silent failures give false reassurance of no leakage.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-19: Rule/model changes are versioned and regression-tested.
criticality_rationale: Unversioned or untested rule changes degrade detection reliability.

requirement_text: PG-AI-AC-20: Tests cover false positives, duplicate signals, missing/conflicting data and overlap scenarios.
criticality_rationale: Untested edge scenarios leave false positives and double counting undetected.
issue_note: No coverage depth or pass threshold stated.

requirement_text: Deterministic rules baseline first, with statistical/AI-assisted methods layered under explicit controls
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-06-1

requirement_text: Repeated detections update existing findings with history and controlled reopening/re-notification
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-06-2

requirement_text: Cross-domain findings use explicit relationships and overlap controls to prevent double-counting
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-06-3

requirement_text: The system remains recommendation-driven, with human approval for consequential external actions and verification before reporting realised improvement
criticality_rationale: Locked mandatory decision; see P3 CP-06-4

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED following independent audit. This is a normative specification, not evidence that the live repository or production system implements or passes these requirements.
criticality_rationale: Status disclaimer; misreading only affects documentation of implementation status.

requirement_text: Section 06 v1.0 is locked following independent audit. Four decisions are mandatory: (1) deterministic rules baseline first, with statistical/AI-assisted methods layered under explicit controls; (2) repeated detections update existing findings with history and controlled reopening/re-notification; (3) cross-domain findings use explicit relationships and overlap controls to prevent double-counting; and (4) the system remains recommendation-driven, with human approval for consequential external actions and verification before reporting realised improvement.
criticality_rationale: Lock record of mandatory decisions; content enforced by body rows.

requirement_text: This lock approves the specification only. It does not claim that live detection rules, models, workflows, connectors or controls have been implemented, tested or accepted. Evidence is required through Section 01 discovery and Section 14 verification.
criticality_rationale: Treating lock as implementation evidence would falsely claim verified status.

requirement_text: Next section: Section 07 — Schedule, Delay & Holding-Cost Intelligence.
criticality_rationale: Navigation pointer only; no obligation.
issue_note: Reclassified: navigation text, not a requirement.

requirement_text: Its permanent missions are (1) stop profit leakage and (2) find additional profit. It must do more than compare actual costs against budget or wait for users to open a dashboard. It must examine changing conditions, relationships, deviations and opportunities even when a project appears financially healthy.
criticality_rationale: Purely reactive detection misses leakage on apparently healthy projects.
issue_note: "Do more than compare actual costs against budget" has no objective pass/fail; operationalised by PGR-06-N006 and PGR-06-N031.

requirement_text: The intelligence layer identifies and explains findings. It does not replace the deterministic financial engine, make unsupported causal claims or autonomously execute consequential external actions.
criticality_rationale: Autonomous consequential actions or overriding the financial engine bypass human control.

requirement_text: 2. Architectural boundary
elements: Logical flow: governed project evidence → signal detection and relationship analysis → evidence-backed finding → deterministic quantification or clearly labelled estimate → recommendation and human review. This is a logical model, not a claim about the current repository.
criticality_rationale: Logical flow guides layering; explicitly not a repository claim.
issue_note: Logical-flow paragraph captured as a list element under the clause heading rather than as requirement text.

requirement_text: The layer must not bypass governed ingestion or independently write authoritative financial results. Financial quantification must use Section 05 calculations or explicitly labelled estimates where a validated calculation is not possible. Implementation must use actual Anchor Engine, Governor and AUIF contracts discovered under Section 01.
criticality_rationale: Intelligence writing authoritative results bypasses governed calculation authority.

requirement_text: 3. Intelligence operating model
elements: Observe new, changed, stale or corrected evidence. ¶ Identify relevant signals and evaluate rules, trends, relationships, anomalies and opportunities. ¶ Gather supporting and contradictory evidence. ¶ Quantify implications where defensible. ¶ Create or update a finding, prioritise it and assign an owner. ¶ Recommend investigation or improvement action. ¶ Track review, decision, implementation and outcome. ¶ Reassess when evidence changes; close, downgrade, reopen or supersede with an audit trail.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete operating loop leaves findings unowned or unreassessed.

requirement_text: Support event-triggered analysis and scheduled reassessment. Scheduled sweeps are required for persistent conditions that may not generate a new event. Failed monitoring runs must be observable; the absence of an alert is not proof that no issue exists.
criticality_rationale: Without sweeps or failure visibility, persistent leakage is missed silently.

requirement_text: 4. Intelligence taxonomy
elements: Commercial and revenue: unpriced scope changes, unsubmitted variations, disputed revenue exposure and missed credits. ¶ Cost and commitments: forecast overruns, duplicated exposure, commitment growth and unexplained cost movements. ¶ Procurement and materials: price variance, unusual quotes, quantity mismatch, delivery risk and buying-timing opportunities. ¶ Labour and productivity: productivity deterioration, excessive hours, rework labour and abnormal output variance. ¶ Schedule and holding costs: emerging delay, critical-path disruption, avoidable hire costs and extended site overhead. ¶ Quality and defects: repeat defects, rework cost growth, unresolved DLP obligations and defect-linked cash delays. ¶ Suppliers/subcontractors: pricing, delivery consistency, quality, expired licence/insurance/safety evidence and other relevant compliance gaps. ¶ Design and constructability: design changes, avoidable rework, specification inconsistencies and potential constructability improvements. ¶ Equipment and logistics: idle equipment, duplicated hire, inefficient deliveries, storage and handling costs. ¶ Cash flow and capital: overdue receivables, delayed retention release, avoidable financing costs and security renewal exposure. ¶ Market and external conditions: commodity changes, FX movement, freight changes, supply constraints and other relevant observations. ¶ Portfolio intelligence: repeated loss patterns, recurring supplier issues and reusable opportunities across authorised projects. ¶ Data integrity: conflicting sources, missing inputs, suspicious duplicates, stale data and unreliable calculations.
criticality_rationale: Taxonomy defines classification families; gaps reduce detection coverage.
issue_note: Unclear whether every family is mandatory for initial detection scope or only a classification vocabulary.

requirement_text: Data-integrity findings must be distinguishable from confirmed financial leakage. A missing record may create reporting risk but is not automatically a financial loss.
criticality_rationale: Data gaps presented as confirmed leakage mislead prioritisation.

requirement_text: The initial implementation must establish a tested deterministic rules baseline before relying on statistical or AI-assisted detection as a primary detection method. More complex detection may be layered on later under explicit evidence, quality, versioning and governance controls.
criticality_rationale: Primary reliance on unproven AI detection degrades finding reliability.

requirement_text: Each rule requires a stable identifier, version, purpose, inputs, evaluation logic, thresholds, exceptions, severity mapping and test cases. Thresholds must be configurable within approved governance boundaries and may not be silently changed by AI.
criticality_rationale: Unversioned or AI-altered thresholds make detection irreproducible.

requirement_text: 5.2 Deterministic rules
elements: Actual cost exceeds a defined tolerance against a comparable budget/forecast. ¶ Commitment increases without an associated approved change. ¶ Invoice quantity/rate differs from the relevant order beyond an approved tolerance. ¶ Variation remains unpriced or unresolved beyond a defined workflow threshold. ¶ Retention release date has passed without release evidence or an explained hold. ¶ Supplier insurance/licence evidence is approaching expiry or has expired. ¶ Material quote exceeds a comparable reference after relevant landed-cost adjustments. ¶ Equipment hire continues beyond evidenced need. ¶ Forecast changes materially without a sufficiently explained movement bridge.
criticality_rationale: Missing baseline rules cause missed leakage detection.
issue_note: Tolerances, workflow threshold, "materially" and expiry-warning window have no default values or approval owner.

requirement_text: Detect repeated cost increases, deteriorating productivity, growing rework rates, commitment-to-budget variance, supplier price changes, late deliveries, forecast margin deterioration and persistent payment/approval/retention delays. Comparisons must use compatible periods, scope, units and operating conditions; a seasonal or scope-driven change is not automatically an anomaly.
criticality_rationale: Incompatible comparisons generate false or missed trend findings.

requirement_text: Connect related evidence across design, quantities, procurement, delivery, programme, labour, quality, defects, retention and cash flow. Show the evidence chain and distinct financial effects. Related findings must not automatically be summed as independent losses.
criticality_rationale: Summing related findings overstates loss and misprioritises action.

requirement_text: 5.5 Statistical/anomaly detection
elements: Establish an explainable baseline or comparison population. ¶ Show why an observation differs from the baseline. ¶ Expose data-quality and sample-size limitations. ¶ Do not treat an anomaly as proof of wrongdoing, waste or financial loss. ¶ Provide a human review path. ¶ Monitor false-positive rates and drift where the method supports it.
criticality_rationale: Unexplained anomalies mislead investigation priorities.

requirement_text: Anomaly detection may prioritise investigation but must not independently create authoritative costs, revenue adjustments or contractual allegations.
criticality_rationale: Anomalies creating authoritative costs or allegations corrupt financial state.

requirement_text: AI may classify unstructured evidence, summarise findings, identify related records, generate investigation questions and propose possible explanations. It must not invent evidence, silently alter rules or authoritative inputs, claim contractual entitlement without verified evidence and human review, treat correlation as causation, promote provisional inputs to authoritative status or execute consequential external actions.
criticality_rationale: AI inventing evidence or executing actions bypasses human approval and integrity.

requirement_text: Material AI-generated assertions must trace to supporting evidence or be labelled as inference, hypothesis or unverified suggestion.
criticality_rationale: Ungrounded AI assertions mislead reviewers.

requirement_text: 6. Finding data contract
elements: Identity: stable finding ID, project/portfolio scope and finding version. ¶ Classification: taxonomy family, subtype and detection method. ¶ Status: detected, under review, confirmed, dismissed, action proposed, action approved, in progress, resolved, reopened or superseded. ¶ Evidence: source references, timestamps, provenance and reconciliation status. ¶ Rule/model: identifier, version and relevant parameters. ¶ Explanation: observed condition, expected condition and reason. ¶ Financial interpretation: actual loss, forecast exposure, potential opportunity, data-quality risk or non-financial operational risk. ¶ Quantification: gross amount, incremental cost, estimated net amount, currency, calculation reference and assumptions. ¶ Confidence/uncertainty: evidence strength, missing information and alternative explanations. ¶ Priority: severity, urgency, time sensitivity and potential impact. ¶ Ownership: responsible role, reviewer and next review date. ¶ Relationships: linked findings, root-cause hypotheses and overlap/double-counting groups. ¶ Disposition and audit: decision, rationale, evidence, approver, outcome, timestamps and change history.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete finding records weaken audit, ownership and overlap control.
issue_note: Status set lacks deferred, closed/downgraded and outcome-verified states referenced by PGR-06-N005, PGR-06-N029, PGR-06-N030 and PGR-06-A013.

requirement_text: A finding may exist without a defensible financial amount. State why it is unquantified rather than inventing a number.
criticality_rationale: Invented amounts on unquantified findings mislead prioritisation.

requirement_text: Preserve Section 03 classifications and Section 05 calculation authority. Distinguish confirmed actual cost/loss, recognised impact, forecast exposure, potential revenue at risk, unresolved/contingent commercial exposure, estimated opportunity, avoided cost, estimated gross benefit, implementation cost, estimated net benefit, verified realised net benefit and non-financial risk.
criticality_rationale: Conflating exposure, estimate and verified benefit misstates financial state.

requirement_text: Never combine these categories into a single ‘profit saved’ number without a transparent definition and reconciliation.
criticality_rationale: Single undefined "profit saved" figure gives false realised-saving claims.

requirement_text: 7. Financial classification and quantification
elements: Example: a possible procurement improvement of $18,000 with $3,000 implementation/logistics cost and an unresolved $4,000 handling risk cannot be presented as a verified $15,000 saving. Disclose the unresolved risk and label scenario results. Only report realised improvement after Section 05 verification requirements are met.
criticality_rationale: Unverified saving reported as realised is a false realised claim.
issue_note: Worked example paragraph captured as a list element under the clause heading; normative sentences follow the example.

requirement_text: Keep severity, urgency and confidence separate. A high-severity finding with weak evidence warrants careful verification, not presentation as a confirmed loss. Thresholds and weights must be documented, testable and approved; AI cannot silently rewrite policy.
criticality_rationale: Merged severity/confidence presents weak evidence as confirmed loss.

requirement_text: One event can create schedule, equipment-hire, overhead and productivity findings. Retain distinct findings when useful, but link them to a shared event/root-cause hypothesis and explicitly identify financial overlap.
criticality_rationale: Unlinked event findings double-count overlap and misprioritise.

requirement_text: 9. Deduplication, correlation and root cause
elements: Deduplicate repeated detection of the same underlying condition. ¶ Update the existing finding identity for ordinary changes while preserving history. ¶ Create a new linked finding for a genuinely distinct issue. ¶ Link symptoms to a common cause where evidence supports it; distinguish suspected relationships from confirmed causation. ¶ Prevent portfolio aggregation from summing overlapping exposures. ¶ Preserve dismissed and superseded findings for audit. ¶ Reopen when new evidence materially changes the situation.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate findings and overlapping portfolio sums overstate exposure.

requirement_text: Repeated detections of the same unresolved condition must update the existing finding rather than generate duplicate findings or notifications each processing cycle. Preserve change history and notification history. Controlled reopening or renewed notification is permitted when material new evidence, a meaningful status transition or an approved escalation condition occurs. Define deduplication identity, suppression window and re-notification rules, and test them.
criticality_rationale: Alert spam causes reviewers to miss material findings.

requirement_text: 10. Continuous monitoring and reassessment
elements: New/revised source record or changed canonical state. ¶ Approved forecast, commitment, invoice, credit or variation change. ¶ Schedule revision or delay event. ¶ New quote or changed market observation. ¶ Supplier/subcontractor compliance status change. ¶ Defect or retention state transition. ¶ Missed deadline or expected release date. ¶ Source becoming stale/unavailable. ¶ Periodic reassessment of open risks/opportunities.
criticality_rationale: Missing reassessment triggers cause late leakage detection.

requirement_text: Use discovered event/workflow contracts. Scheduled sweeps must detect persistent conditions that do not generate events. Failed monitoring runs must be observable; no alert does not prove no issue.
criticality_rationale: Persistent conditions missed and failures silent give false reassurance.
issue_note: Sweep and failed-run observability sentences substantially repeat PGR-06-N006.

requirement_text: 11. Finding lifecycle and human review
elements: Logical lifecycle: signal detected → evidence/data-quality checks → quantify where defensible or mark unquantified/qualified → prioritise/assign → human review → confirm/dismiss → investigate/propose action → human approval where consequential → track implementation → verify outcome → resolve/reopen/supersede.
criticality_rationale: Skipping human approval step lets consequential actions proceed unapproved.
issue_note: Lifecycle paragraph captured as a list element under the clause heading.

requirement_text: Distinguish detected signal from confirmed finding, recommendation from approved action, and implemented action from verified outcome. Dismissal/deferment of material findings must record rationale; retain evidence and allow future reassessment.
criticality_rationale: Implemented action shown as verified outcome is a false verified claim.

clause: 12. Opportunity discovery when budgets are on track
requirement_text: Identify opportunities independent of budget overruns: supplier pricing/terms, purchase timing, waste/surplus reduction, delivery sequencing, productivity, equipment hire, supported variation resolution, financing/retention carrying costs, design/procurement/site coordination and verified portfolio lessons.
criticality_rationale: Opportunities missed on on-budget projects reduce profit recovery.

clause: 12. Opportunity discovery when budgets are on track
requirement_text: Explain why the opportunity applies to the project, evidence, assumptions and additional information needed. Apply the same authority, quantification and verification discipline as leakage detection.
criticality_rationale: Opportunities without evidence discipline mislead decisions.

requirement_text: Where authorised, identify repeated overruns, supplier trends, comparable pricing differences, recurring rework/schedule issues, successful verified interventions and recurring variation/retention delays.
criticality_rationale: Portfolio pattern detection is additive; absence limits learning.

requirement_text: Compare only sufficiently comparable projects, periods, quantities, specifications and terms. Respect tenant boundaries and data-sharing rules. One client's commercially sensitive data must not be disclosed to another merely because aggregation is useful. Govern eligibility, permitted fields, privacy and limitations for aggregated/de-identified learning.
criticality_rationale: Cross-tenant aggregation could disclose commercially sensitive client data.

clause: 14. False positives, missed detections and model performance
requirement_text: 14. False positives, missed detections and model performance
elements: Track findings by detection method/category, confirmation/dismissal rates, reopened findings and identifiable late/missed findings. ¶ Track time to review/resolution, estimated versus verified outcomes, data-quality factors and performance changes after rule/model revisions. ¶ A dismissal is not automatically proof of false positive; review evidence and reason. ¶ A successful intervention does not prove every part of the original explanation was correct. ¶ Version rules/models; material changes require regression testing and a documented release decision.
criticality_rationale: Unmeasured performance and untested rule changes degrade detection reliability.

requirement_text: Section 07 v1.0 is locked following independent audit. Four decisions are mandatory: (1) full critical-path/concurrency analysis only when schedule data supports it, otherwise qualified simpler assessment; (2) strict separation of observed events, suspected causes, supported causal relationships, financial consequences and contractual responsibility; (3) documented counterfactual baseline, evidenced rates, eligible duration and overlap checks for material holding-cost exposures; and (4) mitigation recommendations disclose time benefit, incremental cost, material trade-offs and uncertainty before human approval.
criticality_rationale: Records mandatory lock decisions; loss obscures which controls are non-negotiable.

requirement_text: This lock approves the specification only. It does not claim that schedule integrations, critical-path analysis, holding-cost calculations or mitigation workflows have been implemented, tested or accepted. Evidence is required through Section 01 discovery and Section 14 verification.
criticality_rationale: Without evidence boundary, lock could be cited as implementation acceptance.

requirement_text: Next section in the approved roadmap: Section 08 — Materials, Global Markets & Procurement Intelligence. Recommendations, Prioritisation & Scenario Engine remains Section 10.
criticality_rationale: Roadmap navigation note; no requirement.

requirement_text: Define how Anchor Profit Guardian identifies schedule-related threats to profit, quantifies incremental financial consequences of delay and discovers opportunities to reduce avoidable time-related costs.
criticality_rationale: Purpose statement; no testable behaviour of its own.

requirement_text: The engine must connect schedule evidence to commercial and operational consequences including extended site overheads/supervision, plant/equipment hire, labour standby/disruption/remobilisation, material storage and logistics, subcontractor sequencing/productivity, financing/working capital, revenue timing, potential contractual exposure, quality/rework, defects and delayed retention release.
criticality_rationale: Unlinked schedule consequences mean holding-cost and retention leakage goes undetected.

requirement_text: A delayed activity is not automatically a financial loss. The engine must establish what changed, which costs are genuinely incremental, what evidence supports the relationship, and whether costs are already represented elsewhere in the forecast.
criticality_rationale: Treating all delay as loss overstates exposures and may duplicate costs already in forecast.

requirement_text: Schedule intelligence consumes governed schedule, progress, cost, procurement, commercial and quality data. It produces evidence-backed schedule findings and financial calculations for Section 05. It must not independently modify the approved programme, issue contractual notices, approve extensions of time, alter purchase orders or make authoritative financial adjustments.
criticality_rationale: Engine could alter programme, issue notices, approve EOTs or change POs without human approval.

requirement_text: 2. Scope and architectural boundary
elements: Logical flow: governed schedule/project evidence → schedule-state assessment → causal and financial assessment → finding, scenario and recommendation. This is a logical model, not a claim about the current repository.
criticality_rationale: Logical-flow description, explicitly not a claim about the repository.
issue_note: Paragraph placed in elements with the clause heading as requirement_text; content is descriptive context, not a requirement.

requirement_text: Implementation must use actual Anchor Engine, Governor and AUIF contracts discovered under Section 01.
criticality_rationale: Implementation built on assumed rather than discovered contracts causes integration rework.

requirement_text: 3. Schedule data and baseline management
elements: Project/programme identity, programme version and approval status, baseline date and scope. ¶ Activity identifiers/descriptions, planned and actual start/finish dates, forecast dates, dependencies and relationship types. ¶ Activity calendars, working days/holidays, duration and remaining-duration estimates. ¶ Progress measures and source, resource/subcontractor dependencies, relevant milestones and contractual dates. ¶ Data timestamp, provenance, freshness, approved changes and revision history.
criticality_rationale: Missing schedule fields limit assessment completeness and provenance.
issue_note: Source list has no lead-in obligation; heading substituted as text, so required action (capture/assess/detect) is implied only.

requirement_text: Distinguish original programme, approved revisions, working forecasts and actual performance. Preserve historical versions. Working forecasts and what-if scenarios must remain separate from approved programme versions.
criticality_rationale: Working forecasts or what-if scenarios could silently overwrite approved programme versions.

requirement_text: When a programme changes, record whether the change is an approved scope/schedule revision, operational forecast update, correction or unapproved proposal. A revised completion date must not erase the earlier forecast.
criticality_rationale: Revised completion dates erasing earlier forecasts destroys schedule audit history.

requirement_text: 4. Schedule-state assessment
elements: Planned versus actual progress. ¶ Planned versus forecast dates. ¶ Remaining duration and forecast completion, where the source/model supports it. ¶ Milestone variance and dependency exposure. ¶ Criticality and available float where a valid schedule network exists. ¶ Schedule data quality, including stale progress, missing dependencies and inconsistent dates.
criticality_rationale: Missing schedule-state assessment leaves delays and stale progress undetected.
issue_note: Source list has no lead-in obligation; heading substituted as text, so required action (capture/assess/detect) is implied only.

requirement_text: Do not claim critical-path or reliable completion calculations if source data and the schedule model do not support them.
criticality_rationale: Unsupported critical-path or completion claims mislead delay decisions.

requirement_text: Full critical-path and concurrency analysis is permitted only when connected schedule data has sufficient validated logic, dependencies, calendars, progress and other required inputs for a defensible calculation. Where the schedule is incomplete, stale or structurally unsuitable, provide a qualified simpler assessment, disclose missing links/assumptions and avoid false precision. The system must not silently represent a simplified estimate as full critical-path analysis.
criticality_rationale: Simplified estimates presented as full critical-path analysis give false precision.

requirement_text: 5. Delay classification and attribution
elements: Late material delivery. ¶ Supplier or subcontractor delay. ¶ Labour availability/productivity shortfall. ¶ Design information or approval delay. ¶ Late variation or scope decision. ¶ Access restrictions or site-readiness issues. ¶ Plant/equipment availability. ¶ Inspection, testing or quality failure. ¶ Rework and defect rectification. ¶ Weather or external disruption. ¶ Client/principal decision dependency. ¶ Multiple interacting or unresolved causes. ¶ Data-quality issue preventing reliable assessment.
criticality_rationale: Analytical delay taxonomy; misclassification degrades reporting but not authoritative state.
issue_note: Category list with no stated obligation to classify each delay; informative block 07/45 limits it to analytical, non-legal use.

requirement_text: Maintain distinct states for (1) observed event, (2) suspected cause, (3) supported causal relationship, (4) estimated schedule consequence, (5) estimated financial consequence and (6) contractual responsibility/entitlement requiring separate evidence and human review.
criticality_rationale: Suspected causes could be presented as supported causation or contractual responsibility.

requirement_text: Do not infer contractual liability merely because a supplier, subcontractor or party is associated with an affected activity. Contractual conclusions and consequential notices remain subject to authorised human review.
criticality_rationale: Inferred liability could drive consequential contractual notices without authorised human review.

requirement_text: Basic calculation: Incremental Holding Cost = Eligible Cost Rate × Eligible Incremental Duration. For multiple components, Total Incremental Cost = sum of eligible incremental components. Each component requires defined scope, time window, rate, source and overlap treatment.
criticality_rationale: Incorrect rate x duration components misstate incremental holding-cost exposure.

requirement_text: Do not assume every cost continues at a constant rate throughout delay; rates may change, resources may be redeployed and some costs may be avoided.
criticality_rationale: Constant-rate assumption overstates holding costs where resources were redeployed or avoided.

subclause: 6.1 Counterfactual baseline and overlap controls — mandatory
requirement_text: Every material quantified holding-cost exposure must use a documented counterfactual baseline or scenario, evidenced cost rates, eligible incremental duration and overlap checks before inclusion as a quantified financial exposure.
criticality_rationale: Unsupported holding-cost figures could enter Section 05 calculations as quantified exposure.
issue_note: Gate applies to "material" exposures but no section defines a materiality threshold for holding-cost exposure.

subclause: 6.1 Counterfactual baseline and overlap controls — mandatory
requirement_text: 6.1 Counterfactual baseline and overlap controls — mandatory
elements: Identify the reference programme/scenario and affected activities/period. ¶ Identify applicable resource/cost rates and their source/effective period. ¶ Exclude costs that would have occurred regardless, costs already included elsewhere in the forecast, and duplicate/overlapping cost components. ¶ Record avoided/reduced costs and other causes that may explain the same expenditure. ¶ Document assumptions and uncertainty. ¶ If required inputs are incomplete, retain a qualified estimate or unquantified finding; do not silently present a precise figure.
criticality_rationale: Costs already in forecast or occurring regardless would be double counted as delay exposure.

requirement_text: Where supported, evaluate critical/near-critical status, float, dependency chains, successor activities, independent constraints, parallel activities, resequencing/mitigation options, forecast completion movement and incremental financial effects.
criticality_rationale: Downstream impact evaluation incomplete; limited to where schedule model supports it.

requirement_text: Do not add every delayed activity duration. Overlapping delays and concurrent activities require schedule-aware treatment. If criticality or concurrency cannot be assessed reliably, qualify the result and request review.
criticality_rationale: Summing concurrent delays overstates schedule and cost impact.

requirement_text: Distinguish observed inefficiency from hypothesised cause. Compare productivity against a suitable baseline accounting for scope, trade, work conditions, crew composition and other relevant differences. Unusual productivity is not automatically avoidable waste.
criticality_rationale: Unqualified productivity comparisons mislabel constrained work as avoidable waste.

requirement_text: Link required-on-site dates, forecast delivery dates, lead times and affected activities. Detect late forecasts, lead-time changes, substitutions requiring approval, early-delivery storage costs, fragmented delivery costs, supply risks across work packages and alternative supply opportunities.
criticality_rationale: Late deliveries against required-on-site dates go undetected until they cause delay.

requirement_text: Distinguish forecast risk from actual delay. A late estimate does not prove work will be delayed if stock, resequencing or alternative supply can prevent the effect. Lowest price is not sufficient without schedule, specification, quality, logistics and landed-cost considerations.
criticality_rationale: Forecast supply risk reported as actual delay misleads prioritisation.

requirement_text: Support scenarios for resequencing, resource changes, alternative delivery, expediting critical materials, plant arrangements, subcontractor coordination, design decisions, approval resolution and alternative rectification sequences.
criticality_rationale: Scenario coverage gaps limit mitigation options presented to users.

requirement_text: 10. Schedule scenarios and mitigation
elements: Reference programme/scenario and version. ¶ Activities and dependencies changed. ¶ Duration, resource and productivity assumptions. ¶ Estimated direct implementation cost. ¶ Estimated holding costs avoided or added. ¶ Quality, safety and operational constraints requiring review. ¶ Forecast completion/milestone changes. ¶ Uncertainty, evidence gaps and responsible reviewer.
criticality_rationale: Scenarios lacking assumptions, costs or reviewer are incomplete for decisions.
issue_note: Source list has no lead-in obligation; heading substituted as text, so required action (capture/assess/detect) is implied only.

requirement_text: A scenario is not a guaranteed recovery or profit improvement.
criticality_rationale: Scenarios presented as guaranteed recovery overstate expected benefit.
issue_note: Stated as a fact; the implied obligation (label scenarios as non-guaranteed estimates) is not expressed.

requirement_text: Before a human approves a mitigation action, show the estimated time benefit, incremental cost, other material trade-offs, uncertainty and evidence basis. Include relevant costs such as overtime, expedited freight, extra plant, quality risk, remobilisation and other supported effects.
criticality_rationale: Approvers lack cost, trade-off and uncertainty inputs before approving mitigation.

requirement_text: Simplified relationship: Estimated Net Benefit = Estimated Avoided Cost − Incremental Mitigation Cost, adjusted for other material incremental costs and forecast overlap. Show both savings and added costs; do not recommend acceleration based solely on days recovered.
criticality_rationale: Acceleration recommended on days recovered alone ignores net cost.

clause: 11. Contractual dates, notices and commercial implications
requirement_text: It must not autonomously determine entitlement to an extension of time, liability, valid service of a notice or delay damages. Contract terms and circumstances govern. Any generated deadline/interpretation must identify its source, clause/rule, assumptions and review status. Consequential notices/submissions require authorised human review and approval.
criticality_rationale: System could autonomously determine EOT entitlement, liability or notice validity without human approval.

requirement_text: Continue monitoring where obligations remain after practical completion, including defects delaying retention release, extended rectification, security instruments remaining in place, final-account/close-out dependencies and outstanding inspections/certificates.
criticality_rationale: Post-completion retention and defect delays escape monitoring, delaying cash recovery.

requirement_text: Link findings to retention, security, defect and cash-flow records. Distinguish instrument face value from incremental cost of delayed release and prevent the same defect/delay from being counted multiple times across schedule, quality and financial findings.
criticality_rationale: Same defect or delay counted repeatedly across schedule, quality and financial findings.

requirement_text: 13. Data quality, freshness and confidence
elements: Age of latest schedule revision and progress update. ¶ Missing actual start/finish dates, inconsistent activity identifiers and missing/invalid dependencies. ¶ Contradictory dates across systems and unexplained forecast completion changes. ¶ Unverified resource rates, missing cost evidence and incomplete delay-event records.
criticality_rationale: Stale or inconsistent schedule data feeds unqualified outputs.
issue_note: Source list has no lead-in obligation; heading substituted as text, so required action (capture/assess/detect) is implied only.

requirement_text: When data is inadequate, qualify the result, identify missing evidence and avoid false precision. Do not claim real-time intelligence where sources update periodically.
criticality_rationale: Inadequate data presented with false precision or as real-time.

clause: 14. Finding lifecycle and Active Intelligence integration
requirement_text: Use Section 06's governed finding lifecycle and alert-noise controls. Repeated detections update the existing finding; new material evidence may change severity, estimate, affected activities or recommendation.
criticality_rationale: Repeated detections create duplicate findings and alert noise.

clause: 14. Finding lifecycle and Active Intelligence integration
requirement_text: Link to procurement/materials, labour/productivity, equipment/logistics, quality/rework, commercial variations, retention/security/DLP, forecast margin and cash flow. Preserve distinct effects but prevent overlapping financial amounts from being blindly aggregated. Section 05 governs financial calculations and financial classifications.
criticality_rationale: Overlapping amounts blindly aggregated across linked domains overstate exposure.

requirement_text: 2. Governing principles
elements: Comparable before cheaper: align specification, grade, quantity, units, currency, tax treatment, delivery basis and relevant terms. ¶ Landed cost over headline price: include applicable freight, insurance, duties, handling, currency and other relevant costs. ¶ Price is not the whole decision: account for lead time, reliability, quality, storage, working capital and programme effects. ¶ Evidence before authority: quotes and market observations do not become authoritative project costs merely because they were ingested. ¶ Freshness is explicit: market observations retain source, observation date and applicable validity window. ¶ Forecasts remain separate: procurement scenarios cannot silently alter the approved project forecast. ¶ Human approval remains mandatory for purchase commitments and material substitutions. ¶ Benefits must be verified: estimates are not realised profit until Section 05 verification requirements are satisfied.
criticality_rationale: Bundles approval, forecast-isolation and realised-saving controls; failure allows unapproved commitments or false savings.

requirement_text: 3. Procurement intelligence domains

requirement_text: Monitor recorded commercial dates and identify potential notice, submission, valuation, certification, payment and final-account deadlines where supported by available contract/project records.
criticality_rationale: Missed notice or payment deadlines cause late or lost commercial recovery.

requirement_text: Each deadline records underlying source and clause/rule where applicable, triggering event/reference date, calculation method/assumptions, required action/review, last verification date, interpretation/approval status and responsible person/role where known.
criticality_rationale: Untraceable deadline basis makes reminders unreliable and unreviewable.

requirement_text: Distinguish verified administrative dates from dates inferred from ambiguous contractual language. Do not autonomously determine entitlement, waiver, compliance with notice requirements or validity of a notice. Consequential interpretations and submissions require authorised human review.
criticality_rationale: Autonomous entitlement or notice-validity determinations bypass required human review of consequential submissions.

requirement_text: Contract-derived deadlines must be traceable to their source, trigger, calculation and review status. Ambiguous or consequential contractual interpretations require authorised human review. Generated reminders do not constitute legal advice or proof that a notice is validly served.
criticality_rationale: Untraceable deadlines or unreviewed interpretations risk invalid notices and bypassed review.
issue_note: Human-review sentence substantively repeats PGR-11-N016; traceability fields repeat PGR-11-N015.

requirement_text: 8. Revenue and commercial-value states
elements: Potential commercial opportunity: Possible source of additional value requiring assessment. ¶ Estimated claim/variation value: Analytical estimate, not approved entitlement. ¶ Draft submission: Proposed claim or submission awaiting review. ¶ Submitted value: Amount formally submitted, subject to recorded status. ¶ Approved/certified value: Amount approved or certified under the relevant process. ¶ Recognised revenue: Revenue recognised under applicable accounting policy. ¶ Invoiced amount: Amount invoiced and recorded. ¶ Collected cash: Cash receipt evidenced by relevant records. ¶ Disputed/rejected amount: Value subject to dispute, rejection or unresolved review.
criticality_rationale: State vocabulary; the separation obligation itself is carried by PGR-11-N019.
issue_note: requirement_text holds only the heading; operative content sits in elements.

requirement_text: Potential, estimated, submitted, approved/certified, recognised, invoiced and collected values must remain distinct, with no silent transition between states. Exact lifecycle mappings must be aligned to actual Anchor and accounting integration contracts during discovery. No state transition may silently change another authoritative financial state without the required process.
criticality_rationale: Silent transitions between commercial states corrupt authoritative revenue and cash figures.
issue_note: Permitted transitions and their required processes are deferred to discovery; no transition rules are specified.

requirement_text: Connect potential revenue loss to cost and operational evidence. Examples include work without a linked commercial assessment, approved variations missing from contract-value records, claim values below supported measured quantities, unexplained certified-value reductions, unbilled approved amounts, cost-increasing commercial changes without corresponding revenue assessment, disputes causing financing exposure and unresolved final-account/retention items.
criticality_rationale: Unlinked revenue loss evidence leaves leakage undetected.

requirement_text: Distinguish potential gross amount, evidence-supported amount, unresolved amount, justified confidence assessment, associated costs and possible net benefit. Potential recovery is not certain profit; extra labour, materials, subcontractor costs, financing or other expenditure may apply.
criticality_rationale: Potential recovery presented without costs overstates net benefit.
issue_note: 'Justified confidence assessment' is listed among amount categories but is not an amount; intended distinction unclear.

clause: 10. Integration with finance and cash flow
requirement_text: Link commercial findings to Section 05 margin calculations, cash-position-adjusted margin, receivables/payment status, retention/security, Section 06 finding and overlap controls, Section 07 schedule/delay, Section 09 labour/productivity and Section 10 recommendations/scenarios.
criticality_rationale: Missing integration links weaken cross-domain overlap control.

clause: 10. Integration with finance and cash flow
requirement_text: Approved claims may affect expected revenue without proving collection. Delayed payment may create financing exposure without reducing recognised accounting revenue by the same amount. Financing estimates use evidenced balances, timing and rates and avoid duplication with other holding-cost calculations.
criticality_rationale: Equating approval with collection, or duplicating financing costs, misstates exposure.

requirement_text: Track differences between claimed, certified, invoiced and collected amounts. Potential findings include rejected/partially certified claims, unexplained deductions, disputed variations, missing evidence, repeated valuation discrepancies, payment delays, unresolved final-account items and commercial correspondence requiring action.
criticality_rationale: Untracked claimed-certified-collected differences hide deductions and payment leakage.

requirement_text: Distinguish a recorded dispute from a determination about who is correct. Summarise evidence and identify gaps, but do not make autonomous legal conclusions.
criticality_rationale: Autonomous legal conclusions mislead consequential commercial decisions.

requirement_text: Support scenarios for completing claim evidence, reassessing measured quantities, preparing variations for human review, reconciling certified/invoiced values, escalating overdue decisions, resolving disputed deductions, evaluating negotiated settlements, prioritising final-account close-out and improving evidence capture.
criticality_rationale: Missing scenario types limit analysis; functional completeness.

requirement_text: Each scenario records baseline, assumptions, estimated value, implementation costs, dependencies, risks, uncertainty, approvals and verification method. Section 10 governs prioritisation/action workflows; this section supplies evidence and analysis but does not independently approve or execute actions.
criticality_rationale: Scenarios lacking costs, risks or approvals degrade decisions; must not self-approve.

requirement_text: Commercial opportunities remain estimates until their financial outcome is supported and verified. Verification must account for applicable approval/certification, invoicing and collection states, incremental delivery costs, disputes, financing effects, offsets and overlapping benefits. These states are tracked separately; the required verification criterion depends on the benefit being claimed and the applicable accounting/commercial policy. No submitted claim alone may be labelled collected cash or realised net profit.
criticality_rationale: Submitted claims labelled collected cash or realised profit is a false realised claim.
issue_note: Verification criterion 'depends on benefit and applicable policy' leaves the exact pass condition open; relies on Section 05 rows.

requirement_text: Map contract, variation, claim, certification, invoice and collection data to actual Anchor domain/integration contracts after Section 01 discovery.
criticality_rationale: Mis-mapped commercial data causes integration defects; discovery precedes build.

requirement_text: Establish field-level source authority and reconciliation rules.
criticality_rationale: Without field-level authority, conflicting sources may feed commercial figures.

requirement_text: Implement explicit commercial lifecycle states and permitted transitions.
criticality_rationale: Unconstrained lifecycle transitions allow silent corruption of commercial states.

requirement_text: Preserve original contract baselines, approved revisions and immutable historical calculations.
criticality_rationale: Mutable baselines or calculations destroy audit and evidence integrity.

requirement_text: Link operational evidence to commercial findings without treating correlation as entitlement.
criticality_rationale: Treating correlation as entitlement would overstate recoverable value.

requirement_text: Integrate Sections 05–10 for financial integrity, finding lifecycle, schedule, labour and recommendation workflows.
criticality_rationale: Weak integration reduces cross-domain consistency.

requirement_text: Implement source-traceable deadline monitoring with human-review gates.
criticality_rationale: Untraceable deadlines or missing review gates mislead notice decisions.

requirement_text: Test disputed values, partial approvals, stale data, duplicate claims and overlapping benefits.
criticality_rationale: Untested disputed and duplicate cases let state defects reach release.

requirement_text: Record database/integration blockers in the DB-Dependent Closure Register.
criticality_rationale: Unrecorded blockers hide open closure items.

requirement_text: Do not claim automated contractual interpretation or production claim intelligence without reproducible evidence.
criticality_rationale: Unsupported capability claims falsely assert verified status.

requirement_text: Verify contract baselines and approved variations remain historically distinguishable.
criticality_rationale: Unverified baseline history could let contract-value corruption pass audit.

requirement_text: Check operational evidence is not automatically treated as proof of entitlement.
criticality_rationale: Entitlement-assumption defects could pass audit undetected.

requirement_text: Trace claim calculations to quantities, rates and source documents.
criticality_rationale: Untraced claim calculations could pass audit.

requirement_text: Verify deadlines are traceable and ambiguous interpretations qualified.
criticality_rationale: Untraceable deadlines could pass audit.

requirement_text: Test that commercial lifecycle states do not silently alter authoritative financial values.
criticality_rationale: Silent state-change defects could pass audit, corrupting figures.

requirement_text: Verify claimed, certified, recognised, invoiced and collected amounts remain separate.
criticality_rationale: Merged commercial amounts could pass audit undetected.

requirement_text: Check disputes/deductions are not converted into unsupported legal conclusions.
criticality_rationale: Unsupported legal conclusions could pass audit.

requirement_text: Test financing and other cost effects for double counting.
criticality_rationale: Double-counting defects could pass audit.

requirement_text: Verify human approval cannot be bypassed for consequential commercial actions.
criticality_rationale: Approval-bypass paths could pass audit undetected.

requirement_text: Reconstruct historical commercial decisions and calculations.
criticality_rationale: History reconstruction defects could pass audit.

requirement_text: Each finding must include requirement, severity, evidence, reproduction steps, remediation and retest result. Distinguish missing source capability from an implementation defect.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete audit findings slow remediation; reporting-format obligation.

requirement_text: Actual cash cannot be confused with scheduled, forecast, disputed, conditional, or scenario-only amounts in user interfaces, APIs, exports, and calculations.
criticality_rationale: Confusing actual cash with forecast amounts misstates authoritative cash.
issue_note: 'Cannot be confused' needs an objective test definition (e.g. distinct state fields and labels in each channel).

requirement_text: Material cash-flow records expose provenance, source authority, as-of time, freshness, reconciliation/verification status, and qualification.
criticality_rationale: Missing provenance makes cash records unverifiable and stale data unflagged.
issue_note: 'Material cash-flow records' threshold not defined.

requirement_text: Missing/stale critical inputs produce an explicit qualified result or blocker rather than an unqualified precise forecast.
criticality_rationale: Unqualified precise forecasts from stale inputs mislead decisions.
issue_note: 'Critical inputs' and staleness thresholds not defined, so trigger condition is not objective.

requirement_text: A state transition between claim, certification, invoice, approval, collection, retention release, or security return requires defined evidence and a recorded event.
criticality_rationale: Unevidenced state transitions corrupt cash and receivable states.

requirement_text: Working-capital exposure is calculated separately from accounting margin and forecast final margin.
criticality_rationale: Working capital mixed into margin would misstate accounting margin.

requirement_text: Material financing-cost calculations expose balance basis, rate basis, eligible period, method/day-count basis, fees where applicable, uncertainty, and overlap controls.
criticality_rationale: Opaque financing calculations cannot be verified.
issue_note: 'Material financing-cost calculations' threshold not defined.

requirement_text: Retention and security are represented as different instruments/states; expiry or forecast release dates do not automatically establish eligibility or returned cash.
criticality_rationale: Expiry treated as returned cash falsely states released capital.

requirement_text: Consequential security/retention release or cancellation cannot be executed autonomously; authorised approval and evidence are recorded.
criticality_rationale: Autonomous release or cancellation bypasses human approval.

requirement_text: Payment delay findings distinguish overdue, not due, disputed, uncertified, unapproved, and collected amounts and avoid unsupported breach/fault assertions.
criticality_rationale: Merged receivable states misstate collectible and collected cash.

requirement_text: Cash-timing scenarios disclose incremental costs, expected timing impact, trade-offs, uncertainty, and dependencies and remain isolated from the authoritative forecast.
criticality_rationale: Scenario leakage into the authoritative forecast corrupts cash state.

requirement_text: Post-completion monitoring continues while relevant obligations remain unresolved.
criticality_rationale: Unmonitored post-completion obligations hide trapped capital.

requirement_text: Cross-domain linked consequences are traceable and not blindly added together.
criticality_rationale: Added linked consequences overstate exposure.
issue_note: 'Not blindly added' lacks an objective criterion; should state that linked effects are de-duplicated with recorded relationships.

requirement_text: Automated tests cover state separation, invalid state transitions, stale/missing evidence, financing-cost calculations, overlap prevention, retention/security release controls, permissions, audit trails, and regression behaviour.
criticality_rationale: Missing automated tests let state and release defects reach release.

requirement_text: Production closure requires implementation evidence, test results, relevant database/integration validation, and independently reviewable closure evidence. This specification alone does not satisfy that gate.
criticality_rationale: Closing without evidence would release despite unmet blocking gate.

clause: 12.14 Mandatory checkpoint decisions — accepted and locked
requirement_text: B — Financing-cost evidence gate

clause: 12.14 Mandatory checkpoint decisions — accepted and locked
