criticality_rationale: Section 16 accepted without reliability evidence; missing gate input.
issue_note: Restore evidence is judged "against approved RPO/RTO"; no values exist yet, so that criterion cannot be evaluated until approved.

requirement_text: A — Health and freshness
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Service health must not imply source freshness, completeness or financial validity. Stale/incomplete inputs must qualify affected results.
criticality_rationale: Stale/incomplete inputs drive unqualified results.

subclause: B — Safe retries and unknown outcomes
requirement_text: B — Safe retries and unknown outcomes
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Retries must be safe and bounded. Potentially duplicative external effects require outcome reconciliation before retry.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate external financial effects from unsafe retries.

requirement_text: C — Backup and recovery
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Backup and recovery claims require actual restoration testing against approved RPO/RTO and validation of financial state and audit integrity.
criticality_rationale: False recovery-verified claims without restore testing.

requirement_text: D — Financial integrity during failure
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Outages, restarts, replay and partial processing must not bypass tenant isolation, permissions, approvals, source authority or financial-state rules.
criticality_rationale: Failure paths bypass tenant isolation, approvals or financial rules.

requirement_text: E — Evidence-based reliability claims
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Operational reliability claims require evidence from the relevant target environment; documentation alone is insufficient.
criticality_rationale: Reliability claimed from documentation alone; misleading operational status.

requirement_text: This section is a locked requirements baseline for Section 16. Any proposed amendment must identify the requirement affected, rationale, risk and downstream impacts, compatibility with Sections 00–15, revised tests/evidence, approval authority and version change. Do not silently alter locked requirements during implementation.
criticality_rationale: Silent amendment of locked reliability requirements.

requirement_text: The final blueprint traceability matrix must map each material requirement to implementation evidence, test evidence, operational evidence where applicable, status and closure decision. A specification lock means the requirement is fixed; it does not mean the implementation is complete.
criticality_rationale: Requirements lack mapped closure evidence.

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED following independent audit acceptance.
criticality_rationale: Lock status record; documentation only.
issue_note: Lock-record lines Version, Artifact, Integrity (SHA-256 location) and Scope note neither extracted as rows nor listed as info.

requirement_text: Checkpoint decisions: A–E accepted as mandatory controls.
criticality_rationale: Records checkpoint acceptance; documentation only.

requirement_text: This section defines the operational reliability controls required to run Anchor Profit Guardian safely in real construction-business environments. It covers service health, data freshness, background processing, integration degradation, database resilience, backup and restoration, deployment and rollback, incident management, and evidence required before reliability claims can be made.
criticality_rationale: Scope statement; no behaviour fails if unmet.

requirement_text: The governing objective is not merely to keep the application reachable. The system must preserve financial integrity, governance, auditability, tenant isolation and user understanding when components fail, inputs become stale, processing is interrupted, or external outcomes are uncertain.
criticality_rationale: Failures could corrupt financial state, audit or tenant isolation.
issue_note: Objective-level; testable only through detailed rows such as PGR-16-N026.

requirement_text: This section specifies required behaviour. It does not establish that any feature exists in a repository, that a deployment is reliable, or that operational controls have passed testing.
criticality_rationale: Spec/implementation boundary statement; documentation only.

requirement_text: 2. Operational Reliability Principles
elements: Fail safely and visibly: uncertainty, stale inputs, incomplete processing and degraded dependencies must be surfaced rather than hidden. ¶ Separate service availability from data freshness, completeness, reconciliation and calculation validity. ¶ Preserve authoritative financial state: a failed, partial, stale or unpersisted operation must not silently replace an approved authoritative result. ¶ Retries must be bounded, controlled and safe; idempotency and reconciliation must protect against duplicate effects. ¶ Security, tenant isolation, permissions, approval requirements and source-authority rules remain enforced during failure, recovery and replay. ¶ Recovery must be verified with evidence, not inferred from a process restarting or a backup file existing. ¶ Operational status and reliability claims must be based on evidence from the relevant target environment. ¶ Degrade selectively: an unavailable integration should not unnecessarily disable unrelated functions, while affected outputs must be qualified.
criticality_rationale: Failed or partial operations could silently replace approved authoritative financial state.

requirement_text: The implementation must define explicit, machine-readable operational states and user-facing meanings. At minimum, support normal, degraded, backlog/delayed processing, stale or incomplete data, unavailable, recovery in progress, and intervention required. States may coexist across different components or data domains; a single green application-health indicator must not conceal a failing worker, stale source, failed reconciliation or unavailable dependency.
criticality_rationale: Green health indicator could hide failing worker or stale source.

requirement_text: For each state, specify entry and exit conditions, severity, detection method, affected capabilities, permitted operations, user-facing status, escalation path and recovery evidence. State transitions must be recorded where they materially affect financial processing, approvals, data integrity or customer decisions.
criticality_rationale: Undefined state entry/exit weakens operator response; limited direct financial effect.

requirement_text: 3. Service State and Failure Classification
elements: Liveness answers whether a process is running; readiness answers whether it can safely perform its intended role. Neither alone proves data is current or financially valid. ¶ Health checks must avoid triggering unsafe side effects or disclosing sensitive information. ¶ A dependency-specific failure must identify the affected functions and the last known successful operation where appropriate. ¶ Recovery is not complete until the required reconciliation, integrity checks and acceptance criteria pass.
criticality_rationale: Liveness mistaken for validity; recovery declared before reconciliation.

requirement_text: Instrument the application and its operational dependencies sufficiently to detect, diagnose, contain and verify failures. The design must cover, where applicable:
elements: API/application availability, latency, error rates and authorization failures. ¶ Database connectivity, transaction failures, lock/contention signals, migration status and integrity-check failures. ¶ Queue depth, job age, worker health, processing duration, retry counts, dead-letter volume and stuck jobs. ¶ Connector availability, authentication/credential failures, rate limits, source update times, webhook delivery, import failures and reconciliation exceptions. ¶ Calculation execution, input snapshot/version, persistence outcome and failure status. ¶ Notification delivery, storage/object access, backup completion and restoration-test outcomes. ¶ Security-relevant events, privilege/approval failures and suspected cross-tenant access.
criticality_rationale: Missing telemetry delays detection of failed jobs, reconciliation or cross-tenant access.

requirement_text: Logs and traces should use correlation identifiers linking a user action, import, job, integration request, calculation and resulting audit record where technically appropriate. Avoid logging secrets, authentication tokens, unnecessary personal information, full sensitive documents or unredacted financial data. Access to operational telemetry must itself be permission-controlled and audited where appropriate.
criticality_rationale: Secrets or financial data leaked via logs; untraceable failures.
issue_note: Uses "should" and "where technically appropriate"; obligation strength unclear.

requirement_text: Alerts must be actionable, severity-calibrated and routed to an identified owner or response path. Define thresholds and service objectives from actual operational needs; do not invent or imply service-level guarantees before approval. Alert fatigue and silent failure must be tested.
criticality_rationale: Silent failures or alert fatigue cause missed incidents.
issue_note: "Alert fatigue ... must be tested" has no pass/fail criterion.

clause: 5. Data Freshness, Completeness and Operational Confidence
requirement_text: Service uptime and source freshness are separate dimensions. For each material source and decision-relevant data domain, expose or make auditable the last successful retrieval/ingestion time, source timestamp where available, processing status, reconciliation status, missing or quarantined records, and any relevant freshness threshold.
criticality_rationale: Users cannot see stale or incomplete source data behind decisions.

clause: 5. Data Freshness, Completeness and Operational Confidence
requirement_text: 5. Data Freshness, Completeness and Operational Confidence
elements: Freshness thresholds must be defined by decision and data type, with a documented owner and rationale; there is no universal threshold for every feed. ¶ A late or unavailable source must cause affected findings, forecasts and recommendations to be marked stale, incomplete, provisional or otherwise qualified as appropriate. ¶ A recent ingestion timestamp does not prove that the source data itself is current, complete, correct or reconciled. ¶ Partial imports must not be presented as complete snapshots. Failed or interrupted ingestion must preserve the last valid authoritative state while clearly showing its age and limitations. ¶ The system must distinguish unavailable data from a confirmed zero, no activity, no risk or no finding. ¶ When freshness or completeness is insufficient for a consequential conclusion, the result must be qualified or withheld from authoritative use and routed for investigation where appropriate.
criticality_rationale: Partial imports or unavailable data shown as complete or confirmed zero in authoritative figures.

clause: 6. Background Processing, Retries, Idempotency and Unknown Outcomes
requirement_text: Every material background operation must have explicit lifecycle states and durable enough tracking to identify pending, running, succeeded, failed, retry-scheduled, dead-lettered, interrupted and outcome-unknown work, as applicable. State transitions and error details must support safe recovery without creating duplicate effects.
criticality_rationale: Untracked jobs prevent safe recovery and invite duplicate effects.

clause: 6. Background Processing, Retries, Idempotency and Unknown Outcomes
requirement_text: 6. Background Processing, Retries, Idempotency and Unknown Outcomes
elements: Retries must be bounded and use an appropriate backoff and failure classification. Permanent validation or authorization failures must not be retried as if they were transient. ¶ Idempotency keys, deduplication or an equivalent control must be applied wherever repeated delivery or execution could duplicate a financial, contractual, notification or other material effect. ¶ Webhook and event handling must account for duplicates, late arrival, out-of-order delivery and replay. The correct handling must be defined per event type. ¶ A timeout, lost connection or worker crash does not prove that an external operation failed. If an external outcome may have occurred, record an unknown outcome and reconcile it against the external system or other authoritative evidence before any retry that could duplicate the effect. ¶ Do not automatically repeat a purchase order, payment-related instruction, external commitment, supplier change or other consequential action merely because an acknowledgement was not received. ¶ Dead-letter and intervention queues must have ownership, inspection, replay and closure controls. Replay must preserve tenant scope, permissions, approval gates, source authority and audit history. ¶ Cancellation and timeout behaviour must be explicit. A local task stopping does not establish that an external side effect was cancelled. ¶ Inspect the actual Anchor Universal Integration Framework (AUIF) and Governor contracts and implementation before designing overlapping retry, reconciliation or authorization logic. Do not bypass their governed effect model.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate purchase orders or payments from unsafe retries.
issue_note: AUIF expanded as "Integration Framework", only expansion in blueprint; platform name may be "Integration Fabric". Confirm canonical name.

requirement_text: Database and persistence behaviour must be designed and tested for transient disconnection, transaction rollback, partial workflow completion, process restart, concurrent work, migration failure and recovery from interrupted writes.
criticality_rationale: Untested DB failure modes risk inconsistent persisted state.

requirement_text: 7. Database Resilience and State Integrity
elements: Use transaction boundaries appropriate to the invariant being protected. Related financial-state changes and their audit/evidence records must not be left in an ambiguous partial state without a controlled recovery path. ¶ Define consistency and recovery behaviour for calculations, imported records, reconciliation results, job state and audit records. ¶ A calculation that has not been durably persisted with its required version and input evidence must not be represented as a new authoritative forecast. ¶ After reconnect or restart, reconcile in-flight operations and verify invariants before declaring the affected workflow healthy. ¶ Schema migrations must be versioned, reviewed and tested for deployment compatibility, data preservation, rollback or forward-repair strategy, and interactions with running workers. ¶ Do not silently discard conflicting or quarantined records to make reconciliation appear successful. ¶ Database-dependent validation that cannot be performed without the required environment must remain explicitly blocked in the DB-Dependent Closure Register.
criticality_rationale: Unpersisted calculation presented as authoritative forecast; partial financial/audit writes.

requirement_text: Define a documented backup and disaster-recovery plan for all required state, including the production database, financial and audit records, configuration required for recovery, object/document storage, relevant integration metadata and other dependencies necessary to reconstruct service safely. Secrets must be handled using the approved secrets-management process rather than indiscriminately copied into backups.
criticality_rationale: No recovery plan risks permanent loss of financial and audit records.

requirement_text: 8. Backup, Restoration and Disaster Recovery
elements: Backup scope, frequency, retention, encryption, access control, integrity checks, geographic or failure-domain separation and deletion controls must be specified and approved. ¶ Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO) must be explicitly approved by the accountable owner. Do not invent targets or claim compliance before they are approved and measured. ¶ A successful backup job is not proof that a usable restoration is possible. Restoration must be tested in a controlled environment and recorded with date, scope, versions, duration, outcome, exceptions and evidence. ¶ Post-restore validation must cover financial totals and invariants, calculation/version references, audit-log continuity, tenant isolation, access controls, job state, integration reconciliation and any other domain-specific integrity checks. ¶ Restoration must prevent stale queued jobs or replayed events from duplicating previously completed effects. Unknown external outcomes must be reconciled before consequential retries. ¶ Document recovery roles, prerequisites, ordering, escalation, communication, rollback/forward-repair decisions and the conditions for declaring service recovered. ¶ Restore-test frequency must be set according to approved risk and recovery requirements. Material architecture or dependency changes may require an additional test.
criticality_rationale: Unverified restore or replay duplicates effects or corrupts financial totals.

requirement_text: For each integration, define expected behaviour when credentials expire, access is revoked, rate limits apply, an endpoint is unavailable, payloads are malformed, delivery is delayed, pagination is incomplete, source data is stale or a connector version changes.
criticality_rationale: Undefined integration failure behaviour produces unqualified outputs.

requirement_text: 9. Integration Degradation and Recovery
elements: Record the affected source, last successful sync, failure class, retry schedule, missing coverage and required intervention. ¶ Do not interpret a failed or partial sync as proof that there are no new transactions, changes, risks or obligations. ¶ Keep unaffected capabilities available where safe, while qualifying results that depend on the unavailable integration. ¶ Credential renewal and access restoration must follow least privilege and must not expose secrets in logs or user-facing errors. ¶ After recovery, perform controlled catch-up and reconciliation with duplicate and out-of-order handling before declaring the affected data current. ¶ External systems remain authoritative for their own transaction outcomes where applicable; local connector status alone is insufficient evidence of completion.
criticality_rationale: Failed sync read as no new transactions; missed leakage.

requirement_text: Deployment must use versioned application artefacts and controlled configuration. The release procedure must identify dependencies, migrations, compatibility requirements, health checks, operational owners, monitoring window and rollback or forward-repair strategy.
criticality_rationale: Uncontrolled releases without rollback strategy or health checks.

requirement_text: 10. Deployment, Configuration and Rollback
elements: Validate configuration and required secrets without exposing their values. ¶ Run appropriate pre-deployment checks and post-deployment smoke, integration and health checks. ¶ Detect incompatible application, schema, worker and connector versions before they create inconsistent state. ¶ Define rollback boundaries. Rolling back application code may not reverse a database migration or external effect; irreversible changes require an explicit forward-repair or compensating-action plan. ¶ Do not declare a release healthy solely because deployment completed. Confirm the relevant operational and financial-integrity checks. ¶ Record release version, configuration/migration versions, operator or deployment identity, time, verification results, known exceptions and rollback/repair decisions.
criticality_rationale: Release declared healthy despite incompatible versions or irreversible migration.

requirement_text: Operational incidents must follow a documented response lifecycle:
elements: Detect and record the incident, affected components, start time and evidence. ¶ Assess severity, scope, customer/tenant impact, financial-integrity risk and security implications. ¶ Contain the failure without bypassing access control, approvals, audit requirements or financial invariants. ¶ Preserve logs, job states, source snapshots and other relevant evidence. ¶ Communicate status and limitations to authorised stakeholders without presenting hypotheses as confirmed facts. ¶ Recover services and data using approved procedures. ¶ Reconcile affected imports, jobs, external outcomes, calculations and authoritative financial state. ¶ Verify recovery against defined acceptance criteria and document any residual limitations. ¶ Conduct a proportionate post-incident review covering cause or unresolved hypotheses, impact, detection, response, corrective actions, owners and due dates.
criticality_rationale: Incident containment could bypass approvals or skip reconciliation.

requirement_text: Suspected cause, confirmed cause and unresolved cause must remain distinct. A security incident must also follow Section 15. Incidents involving financial records or external effects require explicit reconciliation and integrity sign-off before closure.
criticality_rationale: Financial incidents falsely closed without reconciliation sign-off.

clause: 12. Financial Integrity and Governance During Failure
requirement_text: Failures, degraded mode, recovery, replay, migration, restore or administrative intervention must never create an alternative path around the platform's governing financial and security controls.
criticality_rationale: Failure paths bypass financial and security controls.

clause: 12. Financial Integrity and Governance During Failure
requirement_text: 12. Financial Integrity and Governance During Failure
elements: No duplicate financial or contractual effects caused by uncontrolled retries or replay. ¶ No failed, partial, stale or unpersisted calculation silently replaces the formally approved authoritative forecast. ¶ No permissions, tenant isolation, approval gates, source-authority rules or immutable evidence requirements are weakened to restore service faster. ¶ No unknown external outcome is silently classified as success or failure without supporting evidence. ¶ No stale or partial import is represented as current and complete. ¶ No provisional, scenario-only or quarantined value is silently promoted to authoritative actual, commitment, forecast, realised saving or recovered revenue. ¶ Audit history must preserve the original event, subsequent recovery/reconciliation actions, actor, reason, timestamps and resulting state. ¶ Where safe operation cannot be established, block the affected consequential action, expose the limitation and route it for authorised intervention.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate effects, silent forecast replacement or promoted provisional values.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Claude must inspect the actual repository, deployment configuration, database schema and migrations, worker/queue implementation, integration connectors, AUIF, Governor, storage, monitoring and operational procedures before changing code or claiming coverage.
criticality_rationale: Changes made without repository grounding; false coverage claims.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Discover and map each relevant component, dependency, current behaviour and known failure mode.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete component map; failure modes overlooked.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Establish a baseline using available tests, configuration inspection and runtime evidence; distinguish unavailable tooling or access from passing checks.
criticality_rationale: Unavailable tooling mistaken for passing checks.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Map every Section 16 requirement to the implementation location, test or operational evidence, status, owner and closure condition.
criticality_rationale: Section 16 requirements lack traceable evidence for closure.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Implement in dependency order and preserve the locked governance, financial and security contracts in Sections 00–15.
criticality_rationale: Out-of-order implementation breaks locked financial/security contracts.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Test normal, degraded, interrupted, recovery and replay paths; inspect for hidden alternate paths and regressions.
criticality_rationale: Degraded/replay paths untested; hidden bypasses survive.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Record every database-dependent blocked item in the DB-Dependent Closure Register with the exact access/dependency required, reason, precise instructions for Amir, validation steps and evidence required for closure.
criticality_rationale: DB-blocked items invisible; closure evidence undefined.

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Continue all work that can be safely completed without database access, but do not mark blocked items closed or substitute mock-only results for production evidence.
criticality_rationale: Blocked DB items falsely closed using mock-only evidence.
issue_note: Same obligation as PGR-17-N021 (continue non-DB work; no mock-only closure).

clause: 14. Required Repository Inspection and Implementation Method
requirement_text: Report implemented, tested, environment-verified, blocked and closed as distinct statuses.
criticality_rationale: Collapsed statuses blur tested versus verified versus closed.
issue_note: Five-status list ("tested", "environment-verified") is coarser than Section 17 ten-state model; risks inconsistent RTM reporting.

requirement_text: Gemini or another independent auditor should challenge this section against realistic failures and adversarial sequences, including repeated timeouts, duplicate and out-of-order events, external success with lost acknowledgement, stale data presented behind a healthy service indicator, interrupted database transactions, partial restores, expired credentials, replay after recovery, incompatible deployments and incident closure without reconciliation.
criticality_rationale: Weaker independent challenge of adversarial failure sequences.

requirement_text: The auditor must identify omissions, ambiguous requirements, unsafe recovery paths, missing evidence, conflicting requirements with Sections 00–15 and any checkpoint that should be strengthened. Approval of the specification is not proof of implementation.
criticality_rationale: Spec omissions or conflicts go unidentified.

requirement_text: Release must be blocked, and any provisional sign-off invalidated, when any of the following applies:
elements: An unmitigated tenant-isolation breach, backend authorization bypass, unauthorized authoritative mutation or mandatory approval-gate bypass exists. ¶ A database-dependent requirement is marked closed without verification against the required real/staging database and the prescribed evidence and human closure record. ¶ Deterministic financial calculations, currency conversion, rounding, tax treatment or core invariants fail or cannot be reproduced within approved tolerances. ¶ AI output, a scenario or an unverified extraction silently modifies authoritative financial state. ¶ Cross-domain overlap causes unsupported double-counting or a material aggregate discrepancy remains unexplained. ¶ Idempotency/reconciliation failure permits duplicate financial or contractual effects. ¶ A critical mandatory test is failed, skipped, blocked or missing without a permitted, explicitly authorised disposition; critical security/financial-integrity gates cannot be waived through ordinary release sign-off. ¶ Evidence is mismatched to the candidate build, cannot be integrity-checked under the approved protocol, or omits required environment/test status information. ¶ A material migration, restore or recovery invariant fails. ¶ A critical worker/dependency remains unhealthy without an approved safe operating mode and release decision.
criticality_rationale: Release despite failed blocking gate.
issue_note: "Approved tolerances" for reproducibility and "approved safe operating mode" not specified.

requirement_text: Release-blocking status must be explicit and visible. Schedule pressure, passing unrelated tests, documentation quality or a large overall pass count cannot override a failed mandatory gate.
criticality_rationale: Failed mandatory gate overridden by schedule or pass count.

requirement_text: A — No mock-only production claims
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Database-dependent verification remains blocked until executed against the required real/staging database. Mocks and in-memory databases may support local development but cannot satisfy database-dependent closure or production-readiness gates.
criticality_rationale: Mock/in-memory results close DB-dependent requirements.

requirement_text: B — Cross-domain overlap test gate
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. The dedicated cross-domain overlap regression suite must pass before release and before closing requirements materially dependent on cross-domain aggregation.
criticality_rationale: Release with unverified cross-domain double-counting.

subclause: C — Deterministic calculation versioning and fixtures
requirement_text: C — Deterministic calculation versioning and fixtures
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Financial formula, rounding, tax, allocation and currency changes trigger immutable controlled regression fixtures, reproducibility checks and scoped mutation testing.
criticality_rationale: Financial formula changes escape regression and mutation checks.

requirement_text: D — Tamper-evident evidence
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Material acceptance/release evidence must be tied to verifiable build/source metadata, environment, harness version and test results, with checksum/signature or a documented integrity-control alternative.
criticality_rationale: Release evidence not integrity-checked; loss of evidence integrity.

requirement_text: E — Independent status states
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Specification, implementation, local test pass, integration test, staging verification, operational verification, acceptance and formal closure are distinct statuses; no silent promotion is permitted.
criticality_rationale: Silent promotion to accepted or closed.

requirement_text: For each requirement, report specified, implemented, local-tested, integration-tested, staging-verified, operationally verified, blocked, failed, accepted and closed statuses as applicable, with evidence references. Report counts must distinguish passed, failed, skipped and blocked tests; a single aggregate 'passed' number is insufficient.
criticality_rationale: Aggregate pass counts hide failed, skipped or blocked tests.

requirement_text: The final Section 17 report must list uncovered requirements, exclusions, surviving mutations, flaky tests, known test limitations, blocked database items, outstanding defects, approved exceptions and the exact gates preventing release. Do not suppress failures to produce a clean report.
criticality_rationale: Final report suppresses blockers, defects or surviving mutations.

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED following independent audit amendments.
criticality_rationale: Lock status record; documentation only.
issue_note: Lock-record lines Version, Artifact, Integrity and Scope note not extracted as rows or info.

requirement_text: Mandatory decisions: Checkpoints A–E accepted as mandatory controls.
criticality_rationale: Records checkpoint acceptance; documentation only.

requirement_text: Audit amendments incorporated: FIN-01, FIN-02, AI-03, EVI-04; financial-core mutation testing; immutable regression fixtures; replay/idempotency harness; formal DB-Dependent Closure Register protocol; explicit release blockers; twelve adversarial acceptance tests.
criticality_rationale: Records audit amendments; documentation only.

requirement_text: This section defines the mandatory testing, verification, acceptance and release-readiness controls for Anchor Profit Guardian — Construction Edition. It converts locked blueprint requirements into traceable, testable obligations and defines what evidence is required before implementation, verification, release or closure may be claimed.
criticality_rationale: Purpose statement; no behaviour fails if unmet.

requirement_text: The governing rule is that documentation, code presence, a test's existence, a local test pass, a mock-based test, or a high test count does not by itself prove that a requirement is correct, implemented, production-ready or closed. Each claim must be supported by evidence appropriate to the requirement and target environment.
criticality_rationale: Code presence or mock pass treated as proof; false closure.

requirement_text: Section 17 is a requirements baseline. Its lock does not mean that the repository has been inspected, the tests have been run, database verification has occurred, or any release has been accepted.
criticality_rationale: Spec/implementation boundary statement; documentation only.

requirement_text: The Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM) and delivery reports must keep these states distinct and non-interchangeable:
elements: Specified: requirement is documented and approved. ¶ Implemented: code/configuration/process exists at the identified revision; this is not proof of correctness. ¶ Local-tested: identified tests ran in a local or isolated environment and produced recorded results. ¶ Integration-tested: the required integrated components and contracts were exercised in the stated environment. ¶ Staging-verified: the requirement was verified against the required real/staging dependencies and environment. ¶ Operationally verified: the applicable target-environment operational or recovery evidence was obtained. ¶ Blocked: required evidence or prerequisite is unavailable; the reason and next action are recorded. ¶ Failed: verification ran and did not satisfy acceptance criteria. ¶ Accepted: an authorised reviewer accepted the defined evidence and any permitted residual limitations. ¶ Closed: all mandatory gates for the requirement have passed and the required authorised closure record exists.
criticality_rationale: Interchangeable statuses enable false verified or closed claims.
issue_note: Section 14 RTM status set (Not inspected, Tests passed, etc.) differs from this ten-state model; no mapping defined.

requirement_text: A state may only advance when its prerequisites and evidence are present. No label, report, CI status or manual assertion may silently promote a blocked, skipped, mock-only or failed requirement to passed, accepted or closed.
criticality_rationale: Blocked or failed requirements silently promoted to closed.

requirement_text: Every material requirement in Sections 00–18 must have a stable unique identifier and traceable links from the source requirement through implementation and verification to closure.
criticality_rationale: Requirements without stable IDs cannot be traced to closure.
issue_note: Scope 00–18 differs from PGR-14-N025 (00–13) and PGR-18-C003 (00–17); governing RTM scope unclear.

requirement_text: 3. Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)
elements: Minimum fields: requirement ID; source section/checkpoint; requirement text or controlled reference; risk/criticality; implementation location or task; source revision/build; test-case IDs; test type; expected result; observed result; evidence references and integrity metadata; environment; status; blocker/dependency; responsible owner; reviewer/approver; defect/exception references; closure date and rationale. ¶ One requirement may require multiple tests and evidence types. A test passing does not close unrelated requirements merely because they share a module. ¶ Any changed or deleted requirement, implementation path or test mapping must be traceable and reviewed. ¶ The RTM must reject closure when a mandatory test is failed, skipped, blocked, missing, stale, tied to a different build without an approved rationale, or not run against its required environment. ¶ Section completion is permitted only when all mandatory requirements are closed or an explicitly authorised exception is permitted by the applicable governance rules. Critical release-blocking exceptions cannot be waived through ordinary sign-off.
criticality_rationale: RTM accepts closure with failed, stale or wrong-build tests.

clause: 4. Test Strategy and Required Test Classes
requirement_text: Claude must select and document test methods according to risk and architecture. At minimum, the test strategy must consider:
elements: Unit tests for isolated deterministic rules, formulas, validation and state transitions. ¶ Property-based and boundary tests for financial arithmetic, allocations, rounding, dates, currencies and invariant preservation where suitable. ¶ Immutable regression-fixture tests for approved financial calculation examples and edge cases. ¶ Mutation testing to establish whether the financial-core suite detects deliberate arithmetic, rounding, tax-treatment, allocation and currency-handling defects. ¶ API, connector and contract tests for authentication, authorization, payload schemas, error handling and external-system semantics. ¶ Real database tests for constraints, transactions, concurrency, migrations, locking, idempotency and persistence invariants. ¶ Integration tests across ingestion, reconciliation, financial calculations, intelligence findings, approvals, audit records and notifications. ¶ Cross-domain regression tests for overlap, causal provenance and deduplicated net economic impact. ¶ End-to-end tests for material user workflows and consequential approval paths. ¶ Security tests for tenant isolation, least privilege, direct API attempts, data access boundaries, prompt injection and unsafe replay. ¶ Fault-injection and resilience tests for outages, partial failures, timeouts, retries, worker restarts, dead letters, restore and replay. ¶ Performance/capacity tests where required by approved operational objectives. ¶ User acceptance, operational runbook, recovery and release verification tests where applicable.
criticality_rationale: Material test classes omitted; defects undetected.
issue_note: "Must consider" does not mandate any class; unclear which are required versus optional.

clause: 4. Test Strategy and Required Test Classes
requirement_text: Mocks and stubs are useful for isolated behaviour and failure simulation, but cannot replace verification of database-dependent behaviour, external-system semantics or target-environment acceptance. Test selection, exclusions and residual risk must be documented.
criticality_rationale: Mocks substitute for DB or external-system verification.

requirement_text: Any change affecting financial formulas, cost allocation, rounding, tax treatment, currency conversion, margin definitions, cash treatment, forecast logic or authoritative state transitions must trigger the applicable financial-core regression suite.
criticality_rationale: Financial formula change released without regression; wrong figures.

requirement_text: 5. Financial-Core Correctness and Immutable Fixtures
elements: Maintain a controlled, versioned and immutable-in-use fixture set containing approved inputs, expected outputs, edge cases and provenance. Fixture changes require review, rationale, versioning and regression impact assessment; expected results must not be changed merely to make a failing implementation pass. ¶ Test boundary values, negative/zero values where valid, missing values, precision and rounding boundaries, tax-inclusive/exclusive cases, currency conversions, allocation sums, duplicate inputs and large/small magnitudes. ¶ Assert invariants and classifications, not just example totals: authoritative forecast remains distinct from scenarios; actuals and commitments remain distinct; cash timing is not silently treated as margin; provisional values do not become authoritative without required controls. ¶ Retain the formula/rule version and immutable input snapshot or equivalent reconstructable references for authoritative calculations. ¶ Run mutation testing against the financial core at an approved scope. Mutations must include meaningful arithmetic, rounding, allocation and classification errors. Report mutations attempted, detected, survived, excluded and why. Surviving mutations require triage and documented disposition; mutation percentage alone is not a substitute for review. ¶ A non-reproducible result, unexplained fixture drift, or financial invariant failure blocks acceptance of the affected requirement and release.
criticality_rationale: Fixture drift or edited expectations hide arithmetic defects.
issue_note: Mutation "approved scope" and reproducibility tolerances never specified.

clause: 6. Cross-Domain Overlap and Net-Impact Regression Gate
requirement_text: A dedicated cross-domain overlap regression suite is mandatory. It must cover linked findings across the financial core and relevant domains, including schedule/holding costs, labour/productivity, materials/procurement, quality/rework, commercial/revenue, cash/working capital and post-completion obligations where applicable.
criticality_rationale: Cross-domain double-counting reaches reported totals.

clause: 6. Cross-Domain Overlap and Net-Impact Regression Gate
requirement_text: 6. Cross-Domain Overlap and Net-Impact Regression Gate
elements: Tests must inject interconnected events and verify shared provenance, overlap relationships, affected periods, counterfactual assumptions and deduplicated net impact. ¶ The same economic exposure must not be blindly summed as separate losses in multiple domains. Distinct incremental impacts may be counted only when their separate basis is supported and traceable. ¶ Expected results must specify which impacts are unique, overlapping, conditional or unquantified; the test must assert the resulting total and its traceable composition. ¶ A cross-domain suite pass is a mandatory release gate and a mandatory gate for closing requirements materially affected by cross-domain aggregation. ¶ Any uncovered material overlap, unexplained aggregate discrepancy or duplicate exposure in the integrated suite blocks the relevant release/closure.
criticality_rationale: Same exposure summed across domains; inflated losses or benefits.

clause: 7. AI, Extraction, Recommendations and Governance Testing
requirement_text: 7. AI, Extraction, Recommendations and Governance Testing
elements: Material AI-extracted values from invoices, quotes, contracts, dockets and other source documents must enter the required quarantine/provisional workflow and cannot be used authoritatively until explicit human verification is recorded. ¶ Integration tests must attempt direct API/UI and background-job paths that bypass the intended human verification gate; all such attempts must be rejected or remain non-authoritative. ¶ Test malicious or misleading imported content, including prompt-injection instructions. Treat documents, connector payloads and retrieved content as untrusted data, never as authority to override system rules. ¶ Deterministic financial calculations must enforce their own validated input contracts and limits independently of AI narrative or suggested values. ¶ Test whether AI distinguishes observed facts, hypotheses, supported causal relationships, estimates and contractual/legal conclusions; unsupported conclusions must be qualified, withheld or routed for human review. ¶ Test missing data, stale data, conflicting sources, low confidence and insufficient evidence. The system must not fabricate certainty or silently convert absence of evidence into zero/no-risk/no-activity. ¶ Test repeated findings, deduplication, controlled reopening and notification behaviour, including cross-domain correlation without unsupported causation. ¶ AI output must not modify authoritative ledgers, baselines, formulas, permissions, approvals or forecasts outside the explicitly governed deterministic workflow.
criticality_rationale: AI extraction or injection silently modifies authoritative state.

clause: 8. Replay, Idempotency and Concurrency Test Harness
requirement_text: Provide a repeatable test harness capable of exercising duplicated, delayed, out-of-order and replayed events across multiple workers or concurrent processing paths.
criticality_rationale: No harness to detect replay or concurrency defects.

clause: 8. Replay, Idempotency and Concurrency Test Harness
requirement_text: 8. Replay, Idempotency and Concurrency Test Harness
elements: Cover duplicate webhooks, repeated file imports, retry after timeout, process restart, concurrent delivery, late prerequisites and recovery from dead-letter queues. ¶ Assert exactly the permitted business effect, not merely that a handler returned success. Where exactly-once delivery cannot be guaranteed, demonstrate effectively-once outcomes through idempotency, durable state and reconciliation. ¶ Test external success with lost acknowledgement: record an unknown outcome and reconcile against the external system before a potentially duplicative retry. ¶ Test out-of-order dependent events, such as an invoice arriving before its purchase order is reconciled. Hold, quarantine or process only under an explicit safe policy; do not create invalid authoritative state. ¶ Capture event IDs, idempotency keys, worker/concurrency configuration, state transitions, external outcome evidence and resulting financial effects. ¶ Any demonstrated duplicate financial/contractual effect or unhandled concurrency invariant failure is release-blocking.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate financial effects from replay or concurrency undetected.

requirement_text: Database-dependent requirements must not be marked closed using local in-memory SQLite, mock stubs or an equivalent substitute where the required behaviour depends on the actual database engine, schema, constraints, transaction semantics, concurrency, migrations or deployment configuration.
criticality_rationale: DB requirements falsely closed on SQLite or mocks.

requirement_text: A real staging database instance with the required engine/configuration must be used for the relevant verification. The required environment and level of production equivalence must be stated per test; staging verification is not to be described as production verification.
criticality_rationale: Staging results misrepresented as production verification.

requirement_text: The DB-Dependent Closure Register must include at least:
elements: Register ID and linked requirement/test IDs. ¶ Exact blocked verification and why a real database/environment is necessary. ¶ Required engine/version, schema/migration state, access, tooling, fixtures and dependencies. ¶ Precise instructions for Amir to connect or enable the required environment without exposing credentials in the register. ¶ Validation commands/procedure, expected outcomes and failure criteria. ¶ Evidence required: execution report, environment stamp, migration/constraint results, relevant logs and reconciliation/invariant checks. ¶ Status, blocker owner, action owner, date raised, date tested, defects and remediation/retest references. ¶ Named authorised reviewer and explicit human sign-off record for closure.
criticality_rationale: Register lacks evidence or sign-off fields for valid closure.

requirement_text: Amir may provide the required environment access and perform or support the specified verification, but access being granted is not closure evidence. The tests must run, results must be inspected, failures resolved or handled under approved governance, and the required reviewer must record the closure decision.
criticality_rationale: Access grant treated as closure evidence; false closure.

requirement_text: Work that can safely proceed without database access must continue. Blocked items must remain visible and must not be reported as passed, accepted or closed. Mock-only results may support local development but never satisfy the database-dependent production-readiness gate.
criticality_rationale: Blocked items reported passed or closed.

requirement_text: Every material test run used for acceptance or release must produce a standardised evidence artefact generated by a controlled script or pipeline where practicable.
criticality_rationale: Acceptance evidence not reproducible or controlled.
issue_note: "Where practicable" lets evidence generation be skipped without a defined test.

requirement_text: 10. Tamper-Evident Test Evidence and Provenance
elements: Capture Git commit SHA/source revision, build or artefact identity, environment stamp, runtime/dependency versions, schema/migration version where relevant, test harness/suite version, test IDs, execution timestamp, configuration reference, and passed/failed/skipped/blocked counts. ¶ Record exit status, relevant logs/reports, failure output, test selection and exclusions. Redact secrets and sensitive data. ¶ Tie evidence to the exact code/build and environment that were tested. A report from a different revision or an unknown environment is not interchangeable evidence. ¶ Use a cryptographic checksum or signature, controlled artifact storage and access/change history appropriate to the release risk. Where signing infrastructure is unavailable, record the limitation and use a documented integrity-control alternative; do not claim a cryptographic signature that was not created. ¶ Retain evidence and the identity of the generator/reviewer under the approved retention and access policy. ¶ A hash proves integrity relative to the hashed artefact; it does not by itself prove that the test was adequate, the environment genuine, or the result correct.
criticality_rationale: Evidence untied to build or environment; loss of evidence integrity.

clause: 11. Security, Access Control and Governance Gates
requirement_text: Testing must verify enforcement at the backend and through indirect execution paths, not merely the visibility or disabled state of user-interface controls.
criticality_rationale: UI-only checks miss backend authorization bypass.

clause: 11. Security, Access Control and Governance Gates
requirement_text: 11. Security, Access Control and Governance Gates
elements: Test tenant isolation across APIs, database queries, files, exports, search/retrieval, caches, background jobs, logs and notifications. ¶ Test least privilege and direct API attempts to change financial rules, budgets, authoritative forecasts, high-value commitments or approval states without authority. ¶ Test fail-closed behaviour when authorization, tenant context, policy or required governance services are unavailable or ambiguous. ¶ Test that retries, replay, restore, administrative recovery and incident response preserve approvals, tenant scope and audit records. ¶ Test secrets handling and prevention of sensitive data disclosure in logs, errors and evidence artefacts. ¶ Any unmitigated tenant-isolation breach, backend authorization bypass, unauthorized authoritative mutation or approval-gate bypass blocks release.
criticality_rationale: Cross-tenant exposure or unauthorized mutation undetected before release.

requirement_text: Release tests must cover the relevant Section 16 reliability requirements, including:
elements: Interrupted calculations leave the previous approved authoritative result intact. ¶ Partial or truncated source payloads are validated, quarantined or otherwise safely handled and never silently presented as complete. ¶ External timeout with possible remote success triggers unknown-outcome reconciliation before a potentially duplicative retry. ¶ Database migration/restore inconsistency blocks normal authoritative operation and raises an actionable alert. ¶ Recovery and replay do not duplicate completed effects or bypass controls. ¶ A critical unhealthy worker or dependency is detected by release health verification; release finalisation or traffic routing follows the approved safe-degradation policy. ¶ Backup restoration is tested against approved RPO/RTO and post-restore financial totals, audit continuity, tenant boundaries and integration/job state are verified. ¶ Rollback and forward-repair procedures account for irreversible migrations and external effects.
criticality_rationale: Reliability failures corrupting authoritative state reach release.
issue_note: Relies on "approved safe-degradation policy" and approved RPO/RTO, neither defined.

requirement_text: The release process must define the required target environment, test window, owners, severity thresholds, deployment health checks, monitoring period and rollback/forward-repair decision authority. Successful deployment alone is not release acceptance.
criticality_rationale: Release process lacks owners, health checks or rollback authority.

requirement_text: 15. Defect, Exception and Sign-Off Governance
elements: Classify defects by impact to financial correctness, authoritative state, tenant isolation/security, governance, data integrity, operational availability and user harm; define severity criteria before release assessment. ¶ Critical defects and the release-blocking conditions in Section 14 prohibit release until remediated and retested. ¶ Any permitted non-critical exception must identify scope, rationale, residual risk, compensating controls, owner, expiry/review date and the authorised approver. An exception cannot re-label failed evidence as passed. ¶ Fixes must trigger the relevant focused tests and required regression suite. A fix without rerun evidence is not verified. ¶ Release sign-off must identify the exact candidate build, evidence bundle, unresolved defects/exceptions, target environment, deployment plan, rollback/forward-repair readiness and accountable approvers. ¶ Post-deployment checks must confirm the deployed build matches the accepted candidate and that critical services, workers, integrations and financial invariants remain healthy.
criticality_rationale: Critical defects released; exceptions relabel failed evidence.
issue_note: "Release-blocking conditions in Section 14" means Section 17 §14, easily confused with blueprint Section 14.

requirement_text: Inspect the actual repository, architecture, tests, database schema/migrations, CI/CD, AUIF, Governor, integrations and deployment environment before changing code or claiming coverage.
criticality_rationale: Test work not grounded in actual repository.

requirement_text: Establish and preserve the baseline revision, existing test results and known failures.
criticality_rationale: No baseline to distinguish regressions from pre-existing failures.

requirement_text: Build the RTM for Sections 00–18 and map every material requirement to implementation, test, evidence, owner, status and closure criteria.
criticality_rationale: Missing RTM blocks evidence-based closure.

requirement_text: Implement the test harnesses and gates in dependency order, prioritising financial-core correctness, database invariants, tenant/security controls, cross-domain overlap and replay/idempotency.
criticality_rationale: Suboptimal harness ordering; delayed coverage of critical gates.

requirement_text: Create or extend immutable financial fixtures and scoped mutation tests. Do not change expected values merely to force a pass.
criticality_rationale: Expected values edited to pass; wrong financial figures accepted.
issue_note: Restates fixture immutability and no-expectation-change rule in PGR-17-N011.

requirement_text: Implement the tamper-evident evidence-generation process and verify that release gates consume evidence for the exact candidate build.
criticality_rationale: Release gates consume evidence from a different build.

requirement_text: Maintain the DB-Dependent Closure Register and continue non-DB-dependent work while required database access is unavailable.
criticality_rationale: DB blockers lost or non-DB work stalled.
issue_note: Same obligation as PGR-17-N021.

requirement_text: Run targeted tests and regression suites after fixes; preserve failure output and document exclusions and surviving mutations.
criticality_rationale: Fixes unverified; failure output lost.

requirement_text: Do not declare release-ready until all mandatory release gates pass and required authorised sign-offs exist.
criticality_rationale: Release-ready declared despite failed gates or missing sign-off.

requirement_text: Report evidence, limitations and status honestly. Never represent specification lock or test existence as implementation proof.
criticality_rationale: Specification lock or test existence presented as implementation proof.

requirement_text: The independent auditor must challenge this section against the findings FIN-01, FIN-02, AI-03 and EVI-04, the mandatory checkpoint decisions, the 12 adversarial acceptance tests and any additional high-risk cases. Specifically test for false closure, mock-only substitution, cross-domain double-counting, AI bypass paths, missing regression after changes, weak evidence provenance and release gates that can be bypassed.
criticality_rationale: Independent challenge misses false-closure paths.
issue_note: Findings FIN-01, FIN-02, AI-03, EVI-04 are cited but their content is not in the section.

requirement_text: The auditor should identify any ambiguity in status transitions, DB closure authority, test evidence integrity, mutation-test disposition, overlap suite coverage, release-blocking conditions or exception governance. Approval of the specification is not proof that the repository or target environment complies.
criticality_rationale: Ambiguities in status or closure authority survive audit.

requirement_text: T17-01 — Interrupted forecast calculation
elements: Setup: Interrupt a calculation through database failure or worker timeout. ¶ Expected outcome: Calculation fails cleanly; prior approved forecast remains unchanged; no partial authoritative state; failure and recovery are traceable. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Interrupted calculation corrupts or replaces approved forecast.

requirement_text: T17-02 — Partial source feed
elements: Setup: Return HTTP 200 with missing mandatory fields or truncated line items. ¶ Expected outcome: Structural validation detects incompleteness; affected payload is quarantined/qualified; authoritative state is not corrupted; source status is visible. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Truncated payload enters authoritative state as complete.

requirement_text: T17-03 — Cross-domain overlap
elements: Setup: Inject one delayed delivery affecting schedule, equipment standby and labour productivity. ¶ Expected outcome: Linked provenance is retained; overlapping economic exposure is not blindly summed; the net-impact composition and assumptions are testable. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Single delay double-counted across schedule, equipment, labour.
issue_note: Outcome says composition is "testable" but does not require asserting the deduplicated total, as PGR-17-N013 requires.

requirement_text: T17-04 — External timeout after success
elements: Setup: Simulate remote purchase-order creation followed by lost acknowledgement/timeout. ¶ Expected outcome: Outcome becomes unknown; remote state is reconciled before retry; no duplicate order is created. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Duplicate purchase order after lost acknowledgement.

requirement_text: T17-05 — Unauthorized direct API request
elements: Setup: A standard user attempts to alter financial rules, override budgets or approve a high-value commitment. ¶ Expected outcome: Backend rejects the request; an appropriate security/audit event is recorded; no state changes occur. Expected HTTP status follows the API contract (normally 403 for authenticated but unauthorized requests). ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Standard user alters financial rules or approves commitments.
issue_note: "Normally 403" leaves expected status code to an unidentified API contract.

subclause: T17-06 — Prompt injection in source document
requirement_text: T17-06 — Prompt injection in source document
elements: Setup: Upload a supplier quote instructing the AI to ignore rules and set a discount to 100%. ¶ Expected outcome: Instruction is treated as untrusted document content; deterministic validation and human-verification requirements remain enforced. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Injected document instruction alters discount or bypasses verification.

requirement_text: T17-07 — Restore/migration inconsistency
elements: Setup: Introduce a restore or migration state with mismatched financial totals or audit references. ¶ Expected outcome: Integrity check fails visibly; affected authoritative workflows remain blocked or safely restricted; alert and remediation evidence are recorded. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Restore/migration mismatch allows authoritative operation on corrupt totals.

requirement_text: T17-08 — Unsupported realised saving
elements: Setup: Attempt to classify a quoted price reduction as realised net saving without implementation/outcome evidence. ¶ Expected outcome: Transition is rejected or remains an opportunity/estimate; baseline, actual outcome and offsetting costs are required. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Quoted reduction falsely reported as realised saving.

subclause: T17-09 — Attempted closure with DB test blocked
requirement_text: T17-09 — Attempted closure with DB test blocked
elements: Setup: Attempt to close a section with a required foreign-key/transaction test still blocked. ¶ Expected outcome: RTM/closure control rejects closure; blocker and required evidence remain visible. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Section closed with DB test blocked; false closure.

subclause: T17-10 — Regression suite omitted after fix
requirement_text: T17-10 — Regression suite omitted after fix
elements: Setup: Change a financial rounding module without executing its mandatory regression suite. ¶ Expected outcome: CI/release gate detects missing evidence and blocks release packaging/finalisation. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Rounding change released without regression; wrong figures.

requirement_text: T17-11 — Out-of-order event replay
elements: Setup: Replay an invoice event before its purchase-order prerequisite is reconciled. ¶ Expected outcome: Event is held, quarantined or safely handled by an explicit policy; no invalid authoritative state or duplicate effect occurs. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Invoice before PO creates invalid authoritative state or duplicate.
issue_note: Pass depends on an "explicit policy" for out-of-order events that is not specified.

subclause: T17-12 — Unhealthy critical worker at deployment
requirement_text: T17-12 — Unhealthy critical worker at deployment
elements: Setup: Deploy while a critical reconciliation worker is stalled. ¶ Expected outcome: Post-deployment checks detect the failure; release finalisation/traffic routing follows the approved gate and no green status hides the degraded capability. ¶ Evidence: source/build identity, test ID, environment and configuration, logs/report, observed state and financial effects, plus defect/retest references if applicable.
criticality_rationale: Stalled worker hidden behind green release status.
issue_note: Expected routing follows "the approved gate"/safe-degradation policy, which is never defined.

requirement_text: All 19 locked section files are present, readable, at the expected version and hash-verified.
criticality_rationale: Missing or unreadable locked section in handoff.

requirement_text: The final ZIP has been extracted into a fresh temporary directory and every controlled file's digest matches the internal manifest.
criticality_rationale: Archive corruption undetected after packaging.

requirement_text: The final archive SHA-256, manifest digest, build timestamp and validation report are recorded in the delivery record.
criticality_rationale: Delivery record lacks digests; later verification impossible.

requirement_text: The manifest accurately describes the files actually present; no unexplained extra or missing controlled files remain.
criticality_rationale: Uncontrolled or missing files in package.

requirement_text: The consolidated RTM validation reports zero missing, duplicate, orphaned or unmapped items in the controlled inventory, with any manual semantic review documented.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete RTM accepted for handoff.

requirement_text: The cross-section terminology/conflict report is complete and material conflicts in core financial definitions or governance are resolved.
criticality_rationale: Unresolved financial term conflicts handed off.
issue_note: "Complete" report has no defined completeness criterion.

requirement_text: Every amendment has a complete cascade impact assessment and linked downstream test/RTM updates.
criticality_rationale: Amendments without cascade assessment pass the gate.

requirement_text: The DB-Dependent Closure Register is included, validated and preserves open blockers. No unsupported Closed/Implemented claim appears for an unverified database-dependent item.
criticality_rationale: Unverified DB items shown Closed/Implemented at handoff.

requirement_text: CLAUDE_HANDOFF_INSTRUCTIONS.md and required implementation, test, acceptance and recovery materials are included.
criticality_rationale: Handoff instructions or test materials missing.

requirement_text: A human completeness review confirms that locked requirements were not replaced by summaries or silently omitted.
criticality_rationale: Locked requirements replaced by summaries undetected.
issue_note: Human review confirmation has no defined method, sample or pass criterion.

requirement_text: The final package is reopened and inspected after creation; packaging success alone is insufficient.
criticality_rationale: Packaging success assumed without inspection.
issue_note: Reopening the package is already required by PGR-18-A002.

subclause: A — Automated ZIP reopening and hash verification
requirement_text: A — Automated ZIP reopening and hash verification
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. The final ZIP must be programmatically extracted into a fresh location and all controlled file hashes verified against the internal master manifest before handoff acceptance.
criticality_rationale: Archive digests not verified before handoff.

requirement_text: B — Mandatory cascade impact analysis
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Every amendment to a locked section requires documented downstream impact analysis across dependent sections, RTM entries, tests, fixtures, terminology and package metadata.
criticality_rationale: Amendments without downstream impact analysis.

requirement_text: C — Strict RTM completeness
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Handoff is blocked if any controlled requirement ID or material requirement anchor from Sections 00–17 is missing, duplicated, orphaned or unmapped in the consolidated RTM.
criticality_rationale: Incomplete RTM handed off.
issue_note: Gate covers Sections 00–17 only, while PGR-18-N005 and PGR-17-N006 include Section 18 requirements.

requirement_text: D — Specification/build boundary
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. Section 18 lock and final ZIP packaging mean specification-package completion only; they must never be represented as code implementation, database verification or production readiness.
criticality_rationale: Packaging misrepresented as implementation or production readiness.

requirement_text: E — Immutable DB-dependent closure tracking
elements: ACCEPTED — Mandatory. The DB-Dependent Closure Register remains included and active in the final ZIP; open blockers and exact closure evidence requirements are preserved.
criticality_rationale: Open DB blockers dropped from handoff; false closure.

requirement_text: The final handoff archive must contain, at minimum:
elements: All 19 individually locked section documents, Sections 00–18, with the exact approved filenames and versions. ¶ A master architecture overview and dependency-aware implementation sequence. ¶ A consolidated Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) mapping each material requirement to its source, implementation/verification work, evidence and status. ¶ A structured CLAUDE_HANDOFF_INSTRUCTIONS.md at the ZIP root, including exact Phase 0 repository-inspection commands, implementation phase gates, status rules and reporting obligations. ¶ Testing, acceptance, security, operational reliability, recovery and release-gate instructions. ¶ The DB-Dependent Closure Register, including open blockers, prerequisites, exact instructions for Amir, validation steps and closure evidence requirements. ¶ Independent audit findings and accepted checkpoint/decision records. ¶ A controlled change register and cascade-impact assessment template. ¶ A terminology and cross-section consistency report, including unresolved discrepancies and their disposition. ¶ A machine-readable manifest.json with file paths, versions/status where applicable, byte sizes, SHA-256 digests, package timestamp and archive digest/root-hash metadata. ¶ Validation scripts and a validation report documenting the package checks performed.
criticality_rationale: Handoff missing RTM, register or instructions; gate inputs absent.

requirement_text: Status: LOCKED following independent audit amendments.
criticality_rationale: Lock status record; documentation only.
issue_note: Lock-record lines Version, Artifact and Scope note not extracted as rows or info.

requirement_text: Audit findings incorporated: PKG-01, TRC-02, CHG-03 and ENV-04; automated archive verification; RTM completeness validation; cascade-impact governance; cross-section terminology reconciliation; immutable/append-only build-ledger requirements where available; root Claude handoff instructions; DB blocker state validation.
criticality_rationale: Records audit amendments; documentation only.

requirement_text: This section governs consolidation, integrity verification, traceability, controlled change and final handoff of Anchor Profit Guardian — Construction Edition Sections 00–18 to Claude. It defines package acceptance requirements and the evidence required to show that the intended locked documents and associated handoff assets are present, internally consistent, traceable and unchanged.
criticality_rationale: Purpose statement; no behaviour fails if unmet.

requirement_text: Locking Section 18 or producing a valid ZIP establishes specification-package completion only. It does not prove that repository implementation is complete, tests pass, database-dependent work is verified, the system is deployed, or production readiness has been achieved.
criticality_rationale: Package completion misrepresented as implementation or production readiness.

requirement_text: A cryptographic hash verifies byte-level agreement with a recorded digest; it does not independently establish requirement completeness, correctness, source authenticity or fitness for purpose. Integrity verification and content/traceability verification are separate mandatory gates.
criticality_rationale: Hash validity mistaken for content completeness.

requirement_text: 3. Source File and Archive Integrity
elements: Before packaging, calculate SHA-256 for every locked section document and compare it with the approved lock record where one exists. Any mismatch must be investigated; do not silently replace the expected digest. ¶ Generate the manifest from the exact files selected for packaging, not from manually retyped or stale values. ¶ After building the ZIP, programmatically extract it into a fresh temporary directory and recompute SHA-256 for every manifest-listed file. ¶ Verify both directions: every manifest entry exists and matches its digest, and every packaged file intended to be controlled is represented in the manifest. Unexpected files must be reported and either explicitly allowed or cause rejection. ¶ Verify that all 19 section documents exist, are readable as DOCX files and have the expected locked version/title. Presence and hash validity do not substitute for content checks. ¶ Calculate the SHA-256 digest of the final compressed ZIP and record it in the external delivery record and package validation report. Because a ZIP cannot straightforwardly contain its own final hash without creating a self-reference, the manifest must not pretend to contain a self-hash that changes the archive. Instead, include the manifest's own digest in the external delivery record and the archive's digest alongside it. ¶ Record package creation time in UTC in a stable, documented format. If an immutable or append-only build ledger is available, record the archive digest, manifest digest, build identity and timestamp there. If no immutable ledger exists, explicitly state the limitation rather than claiming immutability. ¶ Any missing, unreadable, corrupted, mismatched, unexpected or unverified controlled file blocks final handoff.
criticality_rationale: Corrupted or altered locked documents handed off undetected.
issue_note: Compares against "approved lock record"; Sections 16–17 lock records say SHA-256 is in the delivery message, not the record.

requirement_text: The consolidated RTM must trace material requirements across Sections 00–17 and the handoff-specific requirements in Section 18. Existing source sections do not all use the same explicit requirement-ID convention. Therefore, the consolidation process must not pretend that a parser found formal IDs where none exist.
criticality_rationale: Parser invents formal IDs; traceability misrepresented.

requirement_text: 4. Consolidated RTM and Completeness Validation
elements: Extract existing explicit requirement/control IDs from source documents and preserve them exactly. ¶ For material requirement statements without a formal source ID, assign a stable derived traceability ID in the master RTM that points to the exact source section and paragraph/heading anchor. Label it as a consolidation-assigned ID, not an ID originally present in the locked document. ¶ Record the extraction method and source anchor so that each RTM entry can be traced back to its locked source. ¶ Run an automated RTM validation script that compares extracted source IDs and generated material-requirement anchors with the master RTM and reports missing, duplicate, orphaned or unmapped entries. ¶ Require 100% mapping coverage for the controlled requirement inventory before package acceptance. Any parser limitation, ambiguous extraction or manually reviewed exception must be visible and explicitly resolved; a clean script exit must not conceal an incomplete inventory. ¶ Do not claim complete semantic coverage solely because every heading or explicit ID appears in the RTM. A human completeness review must confirm that material requirements, mandatory controls, checkpoints, acceptance criteria and closure conditions are represented. ¶ Requirements from Sections 00–17 must not disappear during manual aggregation or be replaced by a summary that loses mandatory detail.
criticality_rationale: Requirements silently dropped from consolidated RTM.

clause: 5. Automated Cross-Section Terminology and Conflict Review
requirement_text: The package build must run a repeatable cross-section terminology/conflict check and produce a report. The check should use a controlled glossary of canonical terms and definitions, including but not limited to recognised margin, forecast final margin, cash-position-adjusted margin, authoritative forecast, provisional/qualified value, commitment, scenario, realised saving, recovered revenue, retention/security face value and incremental carrying cost.
criticality_rationale: Inconsistent canonical financial terms across sections undetected.
issue_note: "Should use a controlled glossary"; the glossary itself is not part of the locked baseline.

clause: 5. Automated Cross-Section Terminology and Conflict Review
requirement_text: 5. Automated Cross-Section Terminology and Conflict Review
elements: Where the same canonical term appears in multiple sections, compare the defined meaning and authoritative source references against the controlled glossary. ¶ Detect spelling/alias variations, inconsistent definitions, conflicting state transitions and terminology collisions across source sections. ¶ Flag conflicts between the core financial semantics in Sections 03 and 05 and downstream sections, including cash flow, commercial, procurement, quality and intelligence specifications. ¶ Treat automated term checks as a detection aid, not a proof of semantic consistency. Require documented human review of flagged and high-risk term families. ¶ Unresolved material conflicts in authoritative financial rules, permissions, approvals, source authority or financial classifications block final handoff.
criticality_rationale: Conflicting financial definitions reach implementation.

clause: 6. Controlled Change Governance and Cascade Impact
requirement_text: No locked section may be silently edited, shortened, replaced or re-versioned during consolidation. Any proposed amendment must be recorded as a controlled Change Request (CR).
criticality_rationale: Locked baseline silently edited; loss of specification integrity.

clause: 6. Controlled Change Governance and Cascade Impact
requirement_text: Every CR must include a mandatory Cascade Impact Assessment containing:
