elements: CR ID, requester, date, affected locked section/version and exact requirement IDs or source anchors. ¶ Current wording/reference, proposed change, reason and supporting evidence. ¶ Risk and impact assessment, including financial correctness, security, privacy, tenant isolation, approvals, auditability and operational resilience as applicable. ¶ All downstream dependent section IDs, requirement IDs, RTM rows, implementation tasks, tests, immutable fixtures, acceptance criteria, glossary entries, handoff instructions and manifest/hash records affected. ¶ Required regression, integration, cross-domain, security or database tests and evidence needed to validate the amendment. ¶ Independent review and named approval authority, disposition, versioning plan and post-change verification. ¶ A traceable link from the CR to resulting source changes, test runs, revised hashes and closure record.
criticality_rationale: Amendments approved without downstream impact analysis.

clause: 6. Controlled Change Governance and Cascade Impact
requirement_text: A CR must not be approved until the cascade assessment is complete. A change affecting a canonical financial definition must identify downstream effects and relevant test/fixture updates; an unreviewed dependent section blocks approval. Following an approved change, regenerate the affected artefacts, rerun the required consistency/regression checks and update the manifest and RTM. Preserve the prior locked version and its hash as history.
criticality_rationale: Changed financial definition leaves tests/fixtures stale.

clause: 7. DB-Dependent Closure Register — Retention and State Integrity
requirement_text: The DB-Dependent Closure Register must be embedded in the final handoff package and remain active after handoff. Open items must be preserved, not deleted, hidden, relabelled or converted to closed merely to make the package appear complete.
criticality_rationale: Open DB blockers deleted or relabelled closed.

clause: 7. DB-Dependent Closure Register — Retention and State Integrity
requirement_text: 7. DB-Dependent Closure Register — Retention and State Integrity
elements: Minimum fields: register ID; linked section/requirement/test IDs; blocked verification; why the real database/environment is required; exact engine/version/schema/migration and access prerequisites; instructions for Amir; validation procedure; expected result; evidence references; status; blocker/action owner; dates; defect/retest references; reviewer and approval/sign-off ID. ¶ Allowed status transitions must be defined. A blocked item cannot transition to Closed without the required real/staging execution evidence, successful result, linked evidence artefact, and authorised human sign-off ID. ¶ A status of Resolved, Implemented, Locally Tested or Access Provided is not equivalent to Closed. ¶ Validation must reject a closed database-dependent item when staging evidence, environment identity, test result, or required approval metadata is empty, invalid or mismatched. ¶ Open database-dependent items may coexist with final specification-package handoff, but must remain explicitly blocked and must prevent any claim that the corresponding implementation or production verification is complete.
criticality_rationale: DB items closed without staging evidence or sign-off.

requirement_text: The ZIP root must contain CLAUDE_HANDOFF_INSTRUCTIONS.md. It must direct Claude to follow this sequence:
elements: Phase 0 — Repository discovery and baseline: inspect repository structure, current branch/commit, working tree, runtime/tool versions, dependency files, test commands, application entry points, database schema/migrations, authorization and tenant boundaries, audit logging, integration connectors, AUIF, Governor, background workers, CI/CD and deployment configuration. Record commands executed and actual outputs; do not assume a guessed path or command exists. ¶ Phase 0 exit gate: deliver a baseline inventory, current test results, existing failures, architecture map, requirement-to-code observations, access/tooling blockers and DB-Dependent Closure Register. No material code changes until the baseline is recorded, except an explicitly approved emergency correction. ¶ Phase 1 — Control foundations: identity, tenant isolation, permissions, audit, canonical entities, ingestion/source authority and durable state invariants. ¶ Phase 2 — Authoritative financial core: canonical calculations, calculation versioning, immutable/reconstructable inputs, fixtures and mutation/regression suite. ¶ Phase 3 — Domain intelligence: implement domain capabilities against the locked contracts, retaining deterministic financial authority and AI boundaries. ¶ Phase 4 — Cross-domain integration: verify overlap controls, deduplicated net impact, linked provenance, dependency handling and portfolio aggregation. ¶ Phase 5 — Security, reliability and recovery: verify the mandatory Section 15–17 gates in the actual architecture and target environments. ¶ Phase 6 — Acceptance and release evidence: complete RTM status/evidence, required staging/database checks, release-blocker review, and authorised sign-off. ¶ At every phase, update RTM entries, tests, defects, evidence references, statuses and DB blockers. Keep specified, implemented, locally tested, integration tested, staging verified, operationally verified, accepted and closed distinct. ¶ Never claim production readiness from the locked blueprint, code presence, mocks, local tests alone, a successful deployment command or a high pass count. Preserve blockers and report limitations honestly.
criticality_rationale: Claude follows a phase order inconsistent with locked plan.
issue_note: Phases 5–6 (security/reliability; acceptance) differ from Section 14 (Phase 5 interface, 6 verification, 7 DB closure). Status list omits blocked/failed.

requirement_text: The handoff file must include repository-adaptive commands as examples with a requirement to verify each command/path before execution. Do not invent repository paths or claim that commands were executed in advance.
criticality_rationale: Invented paths or commands in handoff file.

requirement_text: T18-01 — Corrupted section detection
elements: Setup: Alter one byte in a copied section document inside a test archive without updating the manifest. ¶ Expected outcome: Fresh-extraction verification recalculates SHA-256, reports the precise mismatch and rejects the package. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: Byte-level corruption of a locked section not detected.

requirement_text: T18-02 — Orphaned/missing RTM entry
elements: Setup: Remove a controlled requirement ID or consolidation-assigned requirement anchor from the master RTM. ¶ Expected outcome: RTM validation reports the missing mapping and fails the completeness gate. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: Missing RTM entry passes completeness gate.

requirement_text: T18-03 — Cascade impact failure
elements: Setup: Submit a CR changing a canonical financial definition without updating dependent section references and tests. ¶ Expected outcome: CR validation flags downstream dependencies and prevents approval until the assessment and required updates are complete. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: CR approved without cascade updates to dependent sections/tests.

requirement_text: T18-04 — DB blocker retention
elements: Setup: Package a register containing an open cash-flow database migration item. ¶ Expected outcome: The item remains Blocked in the register and RTM, with Amir instructions and required staging evidence preserved. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: Open DB blocker lost or closed at packaging.

requirement_text: T18-05 — ZIP extraction verification
elements: Setup: Build the package, extract into a fresh temporary directory and run the validator. ¶ Expected outcome: All required files are present/readable, all digests match, manifest and archive inventory align, and RTM/terminology gates report results. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: Package validator not exercised on fresh extraction.
issue_note: RTM/terminology gates need only "report results"; no pass condition stated.

subclause: T18-06 — Closed DB item without evidence
requirement_text: T18-06 — Closed DB item without evidence
elements: Setup: Change a DB-dependent item to Closed while staging logs or approval ID are absent. ¶ Expected outcome: Register validation fails and the item cannot be accepted as closed. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: DB item accepted as Closed without staging evidence or approval.

requirement_text: T18-07 — Term conflict
elements: Setup: Introduce an inconsistent definition for a canonical financial term in a test copy of a downstream document/glossary. ¶ Expected outcome: Terminology validation flags the collision and handoff acceptance is blocked until reviewed and resolved. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: Conflicting canonical term definition undetected.

requirement_text: T18-08 — Unapproved locked-section edit
elements: Setup: Alter a locked section without a linked approved CR and new hash/version record. ¶ Expected outcome: Pre-package validation detects the source hash mismatch or absent approved change record and rejects the altered file. ¶ Evidence: validator output, build/package identity, test ID, relevant manifest/RTM/register entries and recorded disposition.
criticality_rationale: Unapproved edit to locked section packaged.
